modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Clinical Consultation & Initial Assessment. Grammar focus: Present Simple + Present Continuous. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 25 vocabulary items, 24 smart phrases, 6 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please take a seat. What brings you in today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning, Doctor. I've been feeling increasingly weak and light-headed for the past few weeks, and over the last few days I've also been getting short of breath when I walk upstairs.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. When you say you feel light-headed, do you mean the room is spinning, or do you feel as though you might faint?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's more like I'm about to faint. It usually happens when I stand up quickly, although yesterday it happened while I was walking.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How often is this happening, and how long does each episode last?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It happens several times a day. The worst episodes last for a couple of minutes, although the milder ones pass more quickly.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has anything changed recently in your diet, sleep, workload, or medication?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been working longer hours and sleeping badly. I'm also eating less regularly than I used to.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Doctor, his blood pressure is 98 over 62, and his pulse is 104. Oxygen saturation is 97% on room air.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Have you ever had blood pressure readings that low before?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No. I usually have normal blood pressure.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Are you experiencing chest pain, palpitations, nausea, or unusual sweating at the moment?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm not having chest pain, but my heart sometimes feels as though it's racing when I climb stairs.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you have any diagnosed conditions, and are you taking any regular medication?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I was told I had mild hypertension two years ago. I take an antihypertensive every morning, although I've occasionally forgotten it recently.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any recent weight loss, changes in your appetite, bleeding, or black stools?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've lost about three kilograms without trying. My appetite is slightly reduced, but I haven't noticed any bleeding or black stools.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What about your family history? Has anyone had anemia, diabetes, heart disease, or thyroid problems?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My mother has iron-deficiency anemia, and my father has type 2 diabetes.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to examine you now. I'll check your pulse, blood pressure lying and standing, heart and lungs, and I'd also like to look for signs of pallor or dehydration.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is low blood pressure the main reason I'm feeling this way?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It may be contributing, but we shouldn't assume that it explains everything. Your fatigue, exertional breathlessness, weight loss, and tachycardia could have several causes.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Doctor, he has been much more tired than usual recently. He sometimes has to stop halfway up the stairs.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That is useful information. We'll arrange a full blood count, iron studies, glucose, renal and thyroid function, and an ECG. Depending on the results, we may need further investigations.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean you suspect anemia?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It is one possibility, but we need to distinguish it from cardiovascular, endocrine, metabolic, and other causes before deciding on treatment.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll take the blood samples now and repeat his blood pressure after he has rested.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. If you develop severe chest pain, fainting, or significant difficulty breathing while you're waiting, tell us immediately.

phrasebook.phrase: What brings you in today?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bugun sizni klinikaga nima olib keldi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Что привело вас сегодня в клинику?

phrasebook.phrase: When you say you feel light-headed, what exactly do you mean?
phrasebook.translation_uz: "Boshim aylanadi" deganda aynan nimani nazarda tutyapsiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Что именно вы имеете в виду, когда говорите, что у вас кружится голова?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you feel as though you might faint, or does the room seem to be spinning?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hushingizdan ketadigandek bo'lasizmi yoki xona aylanayotgandek tuyuladimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам кажется, что вы можете потерять сознание, или вам кажется, что вращается комната?

phrasebook.phrase: How often is this happening?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Как часто это происходит?

phrasebook.phrase: How long does each episode last?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Har bir xuruj qancha davom etadi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сколько длится каждый эпизод?

phrasebook.phrase: Does it usually happen when you stand up quickly?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu odatda tez o'rningizdan turganingizda sodir bo'ladimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это обычно происходит, когда вы быстро встаёте?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you noticed anything that seems to trigger your symptoms?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы заметили что-нибудь, что провоцирует ваши симптомы?

phrasebook.phrase: Has anything changed recently in your diet, sleep, workload, or medication?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yaqinda ovqatlanishingiz, uyqungiz, ish yuklamangiz yoki dorilaringizda o'zgarish bo'ldimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Что-нибудь недавно изменилось в вашем питании, сне, рабочей нагрузке или лекарствах?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you experiencing any chest pain, palpitations, nausea, or unusual sweating?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ko'krak og'rig'i, yurak urishini sezish, ko'ngil aynishi yoki noodatiy terlash kuzatilyaptimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы испытываете боль в груди, сердцебиение, тошноту или необычную потливость?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you noticed any recent weight loss or changes in your appetite?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yaqinda vazn yo'qotish yoki ishtahangizda o'zgarish sezganmisiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы заметили недавнюю потерю веса или изменения аппетита?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you taking any regular medication?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Doimiy ravishda biror dori qabul qilasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы регулярно принимаете какие-либо лекарства?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you occasionally forgotten to take it?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ba'zida uni qabul qilishni unutib qo'yganmisiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы иногда забывали его принимать?

phrasebook.phrase: Is there any family history of anaemia, diabetes, heart disease, or thyroid problems?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Oilangizda kamqonlik, diabet, yurak kasalligi yoki qalqonsimon bez muammolari bo'lganmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: В вашей семье были случаи анемии, диабета, сердечных или заболеваний щитовидной железы?

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to examine you now.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сейчас я вас осмотрю.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll check your blood pressure lying and standing.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Qon bosimingizni yotgan va tik turgan holatda tekshiraman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я измерю ваше давление лёжа и стоя.

phrasebook.phrase: It may be contributing to your symptoms, but we shouldn't assume that it explains everything.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu simptomlaringizga sabab bo'layotgan omillardan biri bo'lishi mumkin, ammo hammasini shunga bog'lab qo'ymasligimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это может способствовать вашим симптомам, но не следует предполагать, что этим объясняется всё.

phrasebook.phrase: It is one possibility, but we need to rule out other causes.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu ehtimollardan biri, ammo boshqa sabablarni ham istisno qilishimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это одна из возможных причин, но нам необходимо исключить другие причины.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll arrange a full blood count and iron studies.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Umumiy qon tahlili va temir almashinuvi bo'yicha tekshiruvlarni tayinlaymiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы назначим общий анализ крови и исследование показателей железа.

phrasebook.phrase: Depending on the results, we may need further investigations.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Natijalarga qarab, qo'shimcha tekshiruvlar kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: В зависимости от результатов могут потребоваться дополнительные обследования.

phrasebook.phrase: If you develop severe chest pain, tell us immediately.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar kuchli ko'krak og'rig'i paydo bo'lsa, darhol bizga ayting.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если у вас появится сильная боль в груди, немедленно сообщите нам.

phrasebook.phrase: His blood pressure is 98 over 62, and his pulse is 104.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning qon bosimi 98 ga 62, pulsi esa 104.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Его давление 98 на 62, пульс 104.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll take the blood samples now.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сейчас я возьму образцы крови.

phrasebook.phrase: He has been much more tired than usual recently.
phrasebook.translation_uz: So'nggi paytlarda u odatdagidan ancha ko'proq charchayapti.
phrasebook.translation_ru: В последнее время он гораздо сильнее устаёт, чем обычно.

phrasebook.phrase: He sometimes has to stop halfway up the stairs.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ba'zida u zinadan chiqayotganda yarim yo'lda to'xtashiga to'g'ri keladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Иногда ему приходится останавливаться на полпути по лестнице.

grammar.title: Grammar focus: Present Simple + Present Continuous
grammar.title_en: Grammar focus: Present Simple + Present Continuous
grammar.title_uz: Modul grammatikasi: Present Simple + Present Continuous
grammar.title_ru: Грамматика модуля: Present Simple + Present Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V1 (he/she/it + V-s) | Do/Does + subject + V1? | am / is / are + V-ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ushbu dialogda Present Simple va Present Continuous asosan simptomlarning odatiy/takroriy holati, hozirgi va vaqtinchalik holat, shuningdek klinik kuzatuv va baholashni ifodalash uchun ishlatilgan. Signal so'zlar: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Главное: сначала определите, что вы хотите сказать. Если речь идёт об обычном, повторяющемся или постоянном факте, используйте Present Simple. Если действие или симптом происходит сейчас или является временным/развивающимся, используйте Present Continuous. Сигналы: Важно: signal word помогает, но решающим является смысл. Сигнальные слова: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. Signal words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.signal_words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never

grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Simple описывает привычные, регулярные действия, общие факты и постоянные состояния. В клинике используется для типичных симптомов («The pain usually starts at night»), регулярного приёма лекарств и общих медицинских фактов. Сигнальные слова: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.

grammar.title: Present Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Continuous hozir ayni paytda davom etayotgan yoki hozirgi davrda vaqtinchalik davom etayotgan holatlarni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Ushbu dialogda ayniqsa bemorning hozirgi simptomlari va so'nggi davrdagi o'zgarishlarini tasvirlashda ishlatilgan. temporary or developing situations — vaqtinchalik yoki rivojlanayotgan holatlar ayni paytdagi simptomning yo'qligi Signal so'zlar: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Continuous описывает действие в момент речи или временную, меняющуюся ситуацию: «His condition is getting worse», «I am going to examine you now». Также используется для ближайших действий врача. Сигнальные слова: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. Signal words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.

grammar.title: Important: Dialogue Has Other Tenses Too
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Grammar focus Present Simple + Present Continuous bo'lsa-da, dialog tabiiy clinical conversation bo'lgani uchun boshqa zamonlar ham uchraydi. Ularni yashirish yoki Present Simple/Continuous deb noto'g'ri tasniflash kerak emas.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Хотя грамматический фокус — Present Simple + Present Continuous, в естественном клиническом диалоге встречаются и другие времена. Их не нужно скрывать или ошибочно относить к Present Simple/Continuous — распознавайте каждую форму по её собственному значению.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Although the grammar focus is Present Simple + Present Continuous, a natural clinical conversation also contains other tenses. Do not hide them or mislabel them as Present Simple/Continuous — recognise each form by its own meaning.

examples.sentence: I've been feeling increasingly weak and light-headed for the past few weeks.

examples.note: Present Perfect Continuous — for the past few weeks → o'tmishda boshlangan va hozirgacha davom etayotgan holat.
examples.note_en: Present Perfect Continuous — for the past few weeks → a state that started in the past and continues now.
examples.note_ru: Present Perfect Continuous — for the past few weeks → состояние, начавшееся в прошлом и продолжающееся сейчас.

examples.note_en: Present Perfect — a recent event with a result in the present.
examples.note_ru: Present Perfect — недавнее событие с результатом в настоящем.

grammar.title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V1 (he/she/it + V-s) | Do/Does + subject + V1? | am / is / are + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Simple odatiy, takrorlanuvchi harakatlar, umumiy faktlar va doimiy holatlarni bildiradi. Klinikada odatdagi simptomlar ("The pain usually starts at night"), muntazam dori qabuli va umumiy tibbiy faktlar uchun ishlatiladi. Present Continuous ayni paytda bo'layotgan yoki vaqtinchalik, o'zgarayotgan holatni bildiradi: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". Shifokorning hozirgi rejasini aytishda ham ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Simple описывает привычные, регулярные действия, общие факты и постоянные состояния. В клинике используется для типичных симптомов («The pain usually starts at night»), регулярного приёма лекарств и общих медицинских фактов. Present Continuous описывает действие в момент речи или временную, меняющуюся ситуацию: «His condition is getting worse», «I am going to examine you now». Также используется для ближайших действий врача. Сигнальные слова: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. Signal words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.

grammar.title: Common Mistakes
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ayni paytdagi vaqtinchalik simptomni ta'kidlashda Continuous tabiiyroq. Does dan keyin fe'l V1 bo'ladi.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Самые частые ошибки студентов в грамматике этого модуля с исправленным клиническим вариантом.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Why: "usually" odatiy holat → Present Simple. Why: Routine → Present Simple. Why: He/She/It → doesn't.

practice.setting: general medical clinic / hospital admissions unit
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Daniel Brooks
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative but anxious about the diagnosis

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning, Doctor. I've been feeling increasingly weak and light-headed for the past few weeks, and over the last few days I've also been getting short of breath when I walk upstairs.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. Please take a seat. What brings you in today?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning, Doctor. I've been feeling increasingly weak and light-headed for the past few weeks, and over the last few days I've also been getting short of breath when I walk upstairs.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. When you say you feel light-headed, do you mean the room is spinning, or do you feel as though you might faint?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It's more like I'm about to faint. It usually happens when I stand up quickly, although yesterday it happened while I was walking.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How often is this happening, and how long does each episode last?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It happens several times a day. The worst episodes last for a couple of minutes, although the milder ones pass more quickly.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has anything changed recently in your diet, sleep, workload, or medication?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've been working longer hours and sleeping badly. I'm also eating less regularly than I used to.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. Have you ever had blood pressure readings that low before?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No. I usually have normal blood pressure.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Are you experiencing chest pain, palpitations, nausea, or unusual sweating at the moment?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm not having chest pain, but my heart sometimes feels as though it's racing when I climb stairs.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you have any diagnosed conditions, and are you taking any regular medication?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I was told I had mild hypertension two years ago. I take an antihypertensive every morning, although I've occasionally forgotten it recently.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any recent weight loss, changes in your appetite, bleeding, or black stools?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've lost about three kilograms without trying. My appetite is slightly reduced, but I haven't noticed any bleeding or black stools.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What about your family history? Has anyone had anemia, diabetes, heart disease, or thyroid problems?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: My mother has iron-deficiency anemia, and my father has type 2 diabetes.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. I'm going to examine you now. I'll check your pulse, blood pressure lying and standing, heart and lungs, and I'd also like to look for signs of pallor or dehydration.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is low blood pressure the main reason I'm feeling this way?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It may be contributing, but we shouldn't assume that it explains everything. Your fatigue, exertional breathlessness, weight loss, and tachycardia could have several causes.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Doctor, he has been much more tired than usual recently. He sometimes has to stop halfway up the stairs.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That is useful information. We'll arrange a full blood count, iron studies, glucose, renal and thyroid function, and an ECG. Depending on the results, we may need further investig…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Does that mean you suspect anemia?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It is one possibility, but we need to distinguish it from cardiovascular, endocrine, metabolic, and other causes before deciding on treatment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'll take the blood samples now and repeat his blood pressure after he has rested.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Is low blood pressure the main reason I'm feeling this way?
Does that mean you suspect anemia?

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Acute Chest Pain & Acute Coronary Syndrome. Grammar focus: Past Simple + Past Continuous. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 25 vocabulary items, 23 smart phrases, 7 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Please, tell me what happened before the chest pain started.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I was carrying some boxes upstairs when I suddenly felt a heavy pressure in the centre of my chest.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What were you doing immediately before the pressure began?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I was lifting the last box when the pain suddenly appeared. I put it down and sat on the stairs.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How would you describe the pain — sharp, burning, squeezing, or crushing?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It was a crushing pressure. It felt as though someone was sitting on my chest.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did the pain remain in the centre of your chest, or did it radiate anywhere?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It spread towards my left shoulder and down my arm. I also felt it slightly in my jaw.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What happened next?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I became sweaty and nauseated. My wife called an ambulance because I looked very pale.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: He was also extremely anxious. He kept saying that something was seriously wrong.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you lose consciousness at any point?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I didn't. I remained awake, but I felt very weak.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How long did the episode last?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: The worst of it lasted about twenty minutes. It eased slightly while I was resting, but it never disappeared completely.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: His blood pressure is 156 over 94, pulse 108, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Have you ever had similar symptoms during exercise?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I had experienced mild chest tightness when walking uphill over the past month, but I thought it was just because I was out of shape.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you take anything before the ambulance arrived?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No. I wasn't sure what I should take.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you have hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol, or a history of smoking?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I have hypertension and high cholesterol. I stopped smoking five years ago.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We need to treat this as possible acute coronary syndrome until we have evidence to the contrary. Nurse, please obtain a 12-lead ECG immediately and prepare blood samples for cardiac troponin.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Understood. I'll also establish intravenous access.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Doctor, does this mean I'm having a heart attack?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It is one of the possibilities. Your symptoms are concerning, but the diagnosis depends on the ECG, serial troponin results, examination, and clinical course.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What happens if the ECG is abnormal?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If it shows evidence of acute myocardial ischemia, we'll involve the cardiology team urgently and consider reperfusion according to the findings.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Is there anything we should do right now?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Keep him resting and don't give him food or drink unless the clinical team advises it. If the pain suddenly worsens, tell us immediately.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I'm frightened, but I'm glad I came in.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You did the right thing. With chest pain of this type, early assessment is critical.

vocabulary.definition_en: A strong sensation of pressure in the chest.
vocabulary.example: I was carrying some boxes upstairs when I suddenly felt a heavy pressure in the centre of my chest.

vocabulary.definition_en: The central area of the chest where pain may be felt.
A severe pressure-like sensation often used to describe cardiac chest pain.
vocabulary.example: It was a crushing pressure.

vocabulary.definition_en: Pain spreading from its original site to another area.
vocabulary.example: Did the pain remain in the centre of your chest, or did it radiate anywhere?

vocabulary.definition_en: A common site of referred pain in cardiac presentations.
vocabulary.example: It spread towards my left shoulder and down my arm.

vocabulary.definition_en: Pain may radiate to the jaw in acute coronary presentations.
vocabulary.example: I also felt it slightly in my jaw.

vocabulary.definition_en: Covered in or producing sweat; diaphoresis may accompany acute illness.
vocabulary.example: I became sweaty and nauseated.

vocabulary.definition_en: Feeling that you are about to vomit.
vocabulary.example: I became sweaty and nauseated.

vocabulary.definition_en: Having an unusually light or pale appearance.
vocabulary.example: My wife called an ambulance because I looked very pale.

vocabulary.definition_en: To become unconscious.
vocabulary.example: Did you lose consciousness at any point?

vocabulary.definition_en: To stay conscious.
A sensation of pressure or constriction in the chest.
vocabulary.example: I had experienced mild chest tightness when walking uphill over the past month, but I thought it was just because I was out of shape.

vocabulary.definition_en: Not physically fit; patient-friendly language.
vocabulary.example: I had experienced mild chest tightness when walking uphill over the past month, but I thought it was just because I was out of shape.

vocabulary.definition_en: A clinical syndrome caused by acute myocardial ischemia.
vocabulary.example: We need to treat this as possible acute coronary syndrome until we have evidence to the contrary.

vocabulary.definition_en: Evidence showing that an initial assumption may not be correct.
vocabulary.example: We need to treat this as possible acute coronary syndrome until we have evidence to the contrary.

vocabulary.definition_en: A standard ECG recording used to assess cardiac electrical activity.
vocabulary.example: Please obtain a 12-lead ECG immediately and prepare blood samples for cardiac troponin.

vocabulary.definition_en: A biomarker used to detect myocardial injury.
vocabulary.example: Please obtain a 12-lead ECG immediately and prepare blood samples for cardiac troponin.

vocabulary.definition_en: A route established for intravenous medication or fluids.
vocabulary.example: I'll also establish intravenous access.

vocabulary.definition_en: Troponin measurements taken at different time points.
vocabulary.example: The diagnosis depends on the ECG, serial troponin results, examination, and clinical course.

vocabulary.definition_en: Insufficient blood supply to the heart muscle.

vocabulary.definition_en: Restoration of blood flow to previously underperfused tissue.
vocabulary.example: If it shows evidence of acute myocardial ischemia, we'll involve the cardiology team urgently and consider reperfusion according to the findings.

vocabulary.definition_en: How a condition develops over time.
vocabulary.example: The diagnosis depends on the ECG, serial troponin results, examination, and clinical course.

vocabulary.definition_en: Prompt evaluation of a potentially serious condition.
vocabulary.example: With chest pain of this type, early assessment is critical.

vocabulary.definition_en: To become more severe or problematic.
vocabulary.example: If the pain suddenly worsens, tell us immediately.

vocabulary.definition_en: Extremely important, especially for time-sensitive care.
vocabulary.example: With chest pain of this type, early assessment is critical.

phrasebook.phrase: Please, tell me what happened before the chest pain started.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Iltimos, ko'krak og'rig'i boshlanishidan oldin nima bo'lganini ayting.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пожалуйста, расскажите, что произошло до начала боли в груди.
phrasebook.clinical_use: Acute symptom onsetni ochiq savol bilan aniqlash.

phrasebook.phrase: What were you doing immediately before the pressure began?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bosim boshlanishidan oldin aynan nima qilayotgan edingiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Что вы делали непосредственно перед началом давления/боли?

phrasebook.phrase: How would you describe the pain — sharp, burning, squeezing, or crushing?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Og'riqni qanday tasvirlaysiz — sanchuvchi, kuydiruvchi, siquvchi yoki ezuvchi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Как бы вы описали боль — острую, жгучую, сжимающую или давящую?

phrasebook.phrase: Did the pain remain in the centre of your chest, or did it radiate anywhere?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Og'riq ko'krak markazida qoldimi yoki biror joyga tarqaldimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Боль оставалась в центре груди или куда-нибудь иррадиировала?

phrasebook.phrase: What happened next?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Что произошло потом?

phrasebook.phrase: He was also extremely anxious.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он также был крайне обеспокоен.

phrasebook.phrase: Did you lose consciousness at any point?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы в какой-либо момент теряли сознание?

phrasebook.phrase: How long did the episode last?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сколько длился этот эпизод?

phrasebook.phrase: His blood pressure is 156 over 94, pulse 108, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning qon bosimi 156/94, pulsi 108, saturatsiyasi xona havosida 95%.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Давление 156/94, пульс 108, сатурация 95% на атмосферном воздухе.
phrasebook.clinical_use: Nurse vital signsni concise report qiladi.

phrasebook.phrase: Have you ever had similar symptoms during exercise?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Jismoniy zo'riqishda ilgari shunga o'xshash simptomlar bo'lganmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: У вас когда-нибудь были похожие симптомы при физической нагрузке?

phrasebook.phrase: Did you take anything before the ambulance arrived?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tez yordam kelishidan oldin biror narsa qabul qildingizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы что-нибудь принимали до приезда скорой помощи?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you have hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol, or a history of smoking?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizda gipertoniya, diabet, yuqori xolesterin yoki chekish tarixi bormi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: У вас есть гипертония, диабет, высокий холестерин или анамнез курения?

phrasebook.phrase: We need to treat this as possible acute coronary syndrome until we have evidence to the contrary.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Aksini ko'rsatuvchi dalil bo'lmaguncha, buni ehtimoliy o'tkir koronar sindrom sifatida davolashimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: До получения доказательств обратного мы должны расценивать это как возможный острый коронарный синдром.
phrasebook.clinical_use: Clinical risk managementni ehtiyotkor va professional ifodalash.

phrasebook.phrase: Please obtain a 12-lead ECG immediately and prepare blood samples for cardiac troponin.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Darhol 12 kanalli EKG oling va yurak troponini uchun qon namunalarini tayyorlang.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Немедленно снимите 12-канальную ЭКГ и подготовьте образцы крови на кардиальный тропонин.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll also establish intravenous access.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men vena ichiga kirish yo'lini ham ochaman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я также обеспечу внутривенный доступ.

phrasebook.phrase: It is one of the possibilities.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это один из возможных вариантов.

phrasebook.phrase: The diagnosis depends on the ECG, serial troponin results, examination, and clinical course.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tashxis EKG, ketma-ket troponin natijalari, ko'rik va klinik kechishga bog'liq.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Диагноз зависит от ЭКГ, серийных показателей тропонина, осмотра и клинического течения.

phrasebook.phrase: If it shows evidence of acute myocardial ischaemia, we'll involve the cardiology team urgently.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar u o'tkir miokard ishemiyasiga dalil ko'rsatsa, kardiologiya jamoasini zudlik bilan jalb qilamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если ЭКГ покажет признаки острой ишемии миокарда, мы срочно привлечём кардиологическую команду.

phrasebook.phrase: Is there anything we should do right now?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hozir biz qilishimiz kerak bo'lgan biror narsa bormi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Есть ли что-нибудь, что нам сейчас следует сделать?

phrasebook.phrase: Keep him resting and don't give him food or drink unless the clinical team advises it.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uni dam oldiring va klinik jamoa tavsiya qilmaguncha ovqat yoki ichimlik bermang.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пусть он отдыхает, не давайте ему еду или питьё, если клиническая команда не разрешит.

phrasebook.phrase: If the pain suddenly worsens, tell us immediately.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar og'riq to'satdan kuchaysa, darhol bizga ayting.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если боль внезапно усилится, немедленно сообщите нам.

phrasebook.phrase: You did the right thing.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы поступили правильно.

phrasebook.phrase: With chest pain of this type, early assessment is critical.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bunday turdagi ko'krak og'rig'ida erta baholash juda muhim.
phrasebook.translation_ru: При такой боли в груди ранняя оценка имеет критическое значение.

grammar.title: Grammar focus: Past Simple + Past Continuous
grammar.title_en: Grammar focus: Past Simple + Past Continuous
grammar.title_uz: Modul grammatikasi: Past Simple + Past Continuous
grammar.title_ru: Грамматика модуля: Past Simple + Past Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were | was / were + V-ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Dialogda Past Simple va Past Continuous asosan acute chest pain epizodining ketma-ketligi, simptom boshlangan paytdagi davom etayotgan faoliyat, bemorning o'sha paytdagi holati va klinik tarixni bayon qilish uchun ishlatilgan. Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple описывает завершённое действие или событие в прошлом. Past Continuous показывает процесс, который продолжался в определённый момент в прошлом. Главное: сначала определите, что было процессом, а что произошло как отдельное событие. Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Past Continuous describes an action in progress at a moment in the past, often interrupted by a Past Simple event: "I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain". It gives the background of the onset. Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when

grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple описывает завершённые события в определённое время в прошлом: «The pain started yesterday», «When did you take the last dose?». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Why: suddenly → tugagan acute event Past Simple negative Why: five years ago → finished past time Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

grammar.title: Past Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: was / were + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: while, when, at that moment, all morning
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Past Continuous o'tmishdagi ma'lum bir paytda davom etayotgan harakatni ko'rsatadi. Ushbu dialogda ayniqsa chest pain boshlanishidan oldin bemor nima qilayotganini tasvirlash uchun ishlatilgan. o'tmishdagi davom etayotgan harakat bir harakat davom etayotgan paytda boshqa qisqa voqea sodir bo'lishi acute symptom onset kontekstini yaratish onset oldidan davom etayotgan faoliyatni so'rash Signal so'zlar: while, when, at that moment, all morning.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Continuous описывает действие в процессе в определённый момент прошлого, часто прерванное событием в Past Simple: «I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain». Показывает обстоятельства начала симптома. Сигнальные слова: while, when, at that moment, all morning.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: was lifting = background action; appeared = sudden event Signal words: while, when, at that moment, all morning.

grammar.title: Past Continuous + Past Simple
grammar.structure_pattern: was / were + V-ing | Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were
grammar.signal_words: while, when, at that moment, all morning
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Eng muhim pattern: Past Continuous background/contextni beradi; Past Simple esa shu jarayon davomida sodir bo'lgan qisqa yoki tugallangan voqeani bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: while, when, at that moment, all morning.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Continuous описывает действие в процессе в определённый момент прошлого, часто прерванное событием в Past Simple: «I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain». Показывает обстоятельства начала симптома. Past Simple описывает завершённые события в определённое время в прошлом: «The pain started yesterday», «When did you take the last dose?». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Сигнальные слова: while, when, at that moment, all morning.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Continuous describes an action in progress at a moment in the past, often interrupted by a Past Simple event: "I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain". It gives the background of the onset. Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: while, when, at that moment, all morning.

grammar.title: When vs While
grammar.structure_pattern: while + Past Continuous | when + Past Simple | Past Continuous + when + Past Simple
grammar.signal_words: while, when, at that moment, all morning
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: WHEN ko'pincha qisqa event bilan Past Simpleda, WHILE esa davom etayotgan action bilan Past Continuousda ishlatiladi. Ammo bu qat'iy formula emas — gapning ma'nosi muhim. Signal so'zlar: while, when, at that moment, all morning.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Continuous описывает действие в процессе в определённый момент прошлого, часто прерванное событием в Past Simple: «I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Сигнальные слова: while, when, at that moment, all morning.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Continuous describes an action in progress at a moment in the past, often interrupted by a Past Simple event: "I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain". It gives the background of the onset. Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: while, when, at that moment, all morning.

grammar.title: Other Tenses in This Dialogue
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Grammar focus Past Simple + Past Continuous bo'lsa ham, tabiiy clinical dialogue boshqa zamon va konstruksiyalarni ham o'z ichiga oladi. Ularni aynan o'z shakli va ma'nosi bilan tanish kerak.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Хотя грамматический фокус — Past Simple + Past Continuous, естественный клинический диалог включает и другие времена и конструкции. Учитесь распознавать каждую из них по точной форме и значению.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Even though the grammar focus is Past Simple + Past Continuous, a natural clinical dialogue also includes other tenses and constructions. Learn to recognise each of them by its exact form and meaning.

grammar.title: Common Mistakes
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ushbu modul grammatikasida talabalar eng ko'p yo'l qo'yadigan xatolar va ularning to'g'ri klinik varianti.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Самые частые ошибки студентов в грамматике этого модуля с исправленным клиническим вариантом.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Feel is stative here; use Past Simple. Background action = Continuous; sudden event = Simple. Did dan keyin V1. didn't + V1. Why: Process in progress → Past Continuous.

practice.module: Acute Chest Pain & Acute Coronary Syndrome
practice.setting: general medical clinic / hospital admissions unit
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Michael Reed
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative but anxious about the diagnosis

medical_condition.exact_diagnosis: Acute Chest Pain & Acute Coronary Syndrome
medical_condition.chief_complaint: I was carrying some boxes upstairs when I suddenly felt a heavy pressure in the centre of my chest.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Please, tell me what happened before the chest pain started.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I was carrying some boxes upstairs when I suddenly felt a heavy pressure in the centre of my chest.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What were you doing immediately before the pressure began?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I was lifting the last box when the pain suddenly appeared. I put it down and sat on the stairs.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How would you describe the pain — sharp, burning, squeezing, or crushing?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It was a crushing pressure. It felt as though someone was sitting on my chest.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did the pain remain in the centre of your chest, or did it radiate anywhere?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It spread towards my left shoulder and down my arm. I also felt it slightly in my jaw.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What happened next?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I became sweaty and nauseated. My wife called an ambulance because I looked very pale.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did you lose consciousness at any point?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I didn't. I remained awake, but I felt very weak.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How long did the episode last?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: The worst of it lasted about twenty minutes. It eased slightly while I was resting, but it never disappeared completely.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. Have you ever had similar symptoms during exercise?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I had experienced mild chest tightness when walking uphill over the past month, but I thought it was just because I was out of shape.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did you take anything before the ambulance arrived?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No. I wasn't sure what I should take.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you have hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol, or a history of smoking?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I have hypertension and high cholesterol. I stopped smoking five years ago.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We need to treat this as possible acute coronary syndrome until we have evidence to the contrary. Nurse, please obtain a 12-lead ECG immediately and prepare blood samples for card…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Understood. I'll also establish intravenous access.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It is one of the possibilities. Your symptoms are concerning, but the diagnosis depends on the ECG, serial troponin results, examination, and clinical course.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What happens if the ECG is abnormal?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: If it shows evidence of acute myocardial ischemia, we'll involve the cardiology team urgently and consider reperfusion according to the findings.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is there anything we should do right now?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Keep him resting and don't give him food or drink unless the clinical team advises it. If the pain suddenly worsens, tell us immediately.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand. I'm frightened, but I'm glad I came in.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Doctor, does this mean I'm having a heart attack?
What happens if the ECG is abnormal?
Is there anything we should do right now?

modules.title: Acute Asthma Exacerbation
modules.description: Bronxial astmaning o'tkir xuruji mavzusida klinik muloqot moduli. Grammatika: Present Perfect + Present Perfect Continuous. Namunaviy dialog, 30 ta atama, 23 ta smart ibora, 8 ta grammatik qoida va virtual bemor bilan simulyatsiya.
modules.description_uz: Bronxial astmaning o'tkir xuruji mavzusida klinik muloqot moduli. Grammatika: Present Perfect + Present Perfect Continuous. Namunaviy dialog, 30 ta atama, 23 ta smart ibora, 8 ta grammatik qoida va virtual bemor bilan simulyatsiya.
modules.description_ru: Модуль клинического общения: Обострение бронхиальной астмы. Грамматика: Present Perfect + Present Perfect Continuous. Эталонный диалог, 30 терминов, 23 smart-фраз, 8 грамматических тем и симуляция с виртуальным пациентом.
modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Acute Asthma Exacerbation. Grammar focus: Present Perfect + Present Perfect Continuous. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 30 vocabulary items, 23 smart phrases, 8 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What has been happening with your breathing?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been struggling to breathe for about five days, but it has become considerably worse since yesterday evening.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you been wheezing as well?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been wheezing repeatedly, particularly at night, and I've woken up twice feeling unable to get enough air.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you developed a productive cough, fever, or chest pain?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I haven't had a fever. The cough has remained mostly dry, but my chest has felt very tight.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How often have you been using your reliever inhaler?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been using it four or five times a day, whereas I normally use it only occasionally.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has it been providing lasting relief?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It has helped for a short time, but the symptoms have kept returning.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Her respiratory rate is 26. Oxygen saturation is 91% on room air, and she is speaking in short sentences.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Have you ever been admitted to hospital because of asthma?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, but I had an emergency visit about two years ago.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you been taking your preventer inhaler regularly?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Not consistently. I've missed quite a few doses recently because I've been travelling.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any particular triggers?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Cold air has been making it worse, and I've also been exposed to a lot of dust at work.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you recently had a cold or another respiratory infection?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I had a mild cold last week, but I thought I had recovered.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It sounds as though your asthma control has deteriorated. We need to assess the severity of this exacerbation rather than assuming it is simply another mild attack.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Could I be having a serious asthma attack?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Your oxygen saturation and increased work of breathing are concerning, so we need to monitor you closely.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll start continuous oxygen saturation monitoring and prepare the prescribed bronchodilator treatment.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We'll also check your peak expiratory flow if you are able to perform the test safely.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need steroids?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You may need systemic corticosteroids depending on your response to the initial treatment and the severity of the exacerbation.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: How long will I have to stay here?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That depends on how your breathing responds. If your oxygenation improves and your symptoms settle, we may be able to discharge you with a revised asthma plan.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: She has been coughing at night for several weeks, even before this attack.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That suggests her underlying asthma may not have been well controlled for some time. We'll review her long-term treatment as well.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I don't want this to happen again.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Exactly. The immediate priority is stabilising your breathing; afterwards, we'll address prevention and inhaler adherence.

vocabulary.example: Has it been providing lasting relief?

vocabulary.definition_en: Number of breaths per minute.

vocabulary.definition_en: The process/status of supplying oxygen to the blood.
vocabulary.example: If your oxygenation improves and your symptoms settle, we may be able to discharge you with a revised asthma plan.

vocabulary.definition_en: Symptoms becoming less severe or resolving.
vocabulary.example: If your oxygenation improves and your symptoms settle, we may be able to discharge you with a revised asthma plan.

vocabulary.definition_en: Allow a patient to leave healthcare after assessment/treatment.
vocabulary.example: If your oxygenation improves and your symptoms settle, we may be able to discharge you with a revised asthma plan.

phrasebook.phrase: What has been happening with your breathing?

phrasebook.phrase: I've been struggling to breathe for about five days.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Taxminan besh kundan beri nafas olishda qiynalyapman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я испытываю затруднение дыхания около пяти дней.
phrasebook.clinical_use: Uzoqroq davom etayotgan simptomni bemor tilida ifodalash.

phrasebook.phrase: Have you been wheezing as well?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizda xirillab nafas olish ham bo'lyaptimi?

phrasebook.phrase: I've woken up twice feeling unable to get enough air.

phrasebook.translation_ru: Я дважды просыпалась, чувствуя, что не могу вдохнуть достаточно воздуха.

phrasebook.phrase: Have you developed a productive cough, fever, or chest pain?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Balg'amli yo'tal, isitma yoki ko'krak og'rig'i paydo bo'ldimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: У вас появился продуктивный кашель, температура или боль в груди?

phrasebook.phrase: How often have you been using your reliever inhaler?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tez yordam beruvchi inhalerdan qanchalik tez-tez foydalanyapsiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Как часто вы используете ингалятор для облегчения симптомов?
phrasebook.clinical_use: Medication use and change in frequency.

phrasebook.phrase: Has it been providing lasting relief?
phrasebook.translation_uz: U uzoq davom etadigan yengillik beryaptimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он обеспечивает длительное облегчение?

phrasebook.phrase: Her respiratory rate is 26. Oxygen saturation is 91% on room air.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning nafas olish tezligi 26. Saturatsiyasi xona havosida 91%.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Частота дыхания 26, сатурация 91% на атмосферном воздухе.

phrasebook.phrase: Have you ever been admitted to hospital because of asthma?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Astma sababli hech qachon shifoxonaga yotqizilganmisiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вас когда-нибудь госпитализировали из-за астмы?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you been taking your preventer inhaler regularly?

phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы регулярно использовали профилактический ингалятор?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you noticed any particular triggers?

phrasebook.translation_uz: Ishda ko'p chang ta'siriga ham duchor bo'lyapman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я также подвергалась воздействию большого количества пыли на работе.

phrasebook.phrase: It sounds as though your asthma control has deteriorated.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Похоже, что контроль астмы ухудшился.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to assess the severity of this exacerbation rather than assuming it is simply another mild attack.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu shunchaki yana bir yengil xuruj deb taxmin qilishdan ko'ra, zo'rayish darajasini baholashimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо оценить тяжесть этого обострения, а не предполагать, что это просто очередной лёгкий приступ.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to monitor you closely.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо тщательно за вами наблюдать.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll start continuous oxygen saturation monitoring and prepare the prescribed bronchodilator treatment.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Doimiy kislorod saturatsiyasi monitoringini boshlayman va buyurilgan bronxodilatator davolashni tayyorlayman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я начну непрерывный мониторинг сатурации и подготовлю назначенную бронходилататорную терапию.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll also check your peak expiratory flow if you are able to perform the test safely.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar testni xavfsiz bajara olsangiz, maksimal ekspirator oqimni ham tekshiramiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы также проверим пиковую скорость выдоха, если вы сможете безопасно выполнить тест.

phrasebook.phrase: You may need systemic corticosteroids depending on your response to the initial treatment and the severity of the exacerbation.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Boshlang'ich davolashga javobingiz va zo'rayish darajasiga qarab tizimli kortikosteroidlar kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: В зависимости от ответа на начальное лечение и тяжести обострения могут потребоваться системные кортикостероиды.

phrasebook.phrase: If your oxygenation improves and your symptoms settle, we may be able to discharge you with a revised asthma plan.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar kislorodlanishingiz yaxshilansa va simptomlaringiz bosilsa, yangilangan astma rejasi bilan sizni uyga javob berishimiz mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если оксигенация улучшится и симптомы стабилизируются, возможно, мы сможем вас выписать с пересмотренным планом лечения астмы.

phrasebook.phrase: She has been coughing at night for several weeks, even before this attack.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu xurujdan oldin ham bir necha hafta davomida u kechalari yo'talib kelgan.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Она кашляет по ночам уже несколько недель, ещё до этого приступа.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll review her long-term treatment as well.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning uzoq muddatli davolashini ham qayta ko'rib chiqamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы также пересмотрим её длительное лечение.
phrasebook.clinical_use: Move from acute care to prevention.

phrasebook.phrase: The immediate priority is stabilising your breathing; afterwards, we'll address prevention and inhaler adherence.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hozirgi asosiy vazifa nafas olishingizni barqarorlashtirish; keyin profilaktika va inhalerga rioya qilish masalasini ko'rib chiqamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Наша непосредственная задача — стабилизировать дыхание; затем мы займёмся профилактикой и приверженностью к ингаляционной терапии.

grammar.title: Grammar focus: Present Perfect + Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.title_en: Grammar focus: Present Perfect + Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.title_uz: Modul grammatikasi: Present Perfect + Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.title_ru: Грамматика модуля: Present Perfect + Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3 | Have/Has + subject + V3? | have / has + been + V-ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu dialogda Present Perfect va Present Perfect Continuous asosan o'tmishda boshlangan, hozirgacha davom etayotgan simptomlar, yaqinda sodir bo'lgan o'zgarishlar, bemorning oldingi tajribasi va hozirgi klinik vaziyat bilan bog'liq natijalarni ifodalash uchun ishlatilgan. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое с настоящим. Он часто используется для опыта, недавних изменений и результатов, которые важны сейчас. Present Perfect Continuous подчёркивает процесс или длительность действия, начавшегося в прошлом и продолжающегося до настоящего момента. Результат/состояние сейчас: I haven't had a fever. Главное: если важно "что произошло / какой результат", чаще выбираем Present Perfect. Если важно "как долго / как долго продолжается процесс", чаще выбираем Present Perfect Continuous. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. grammar.title: For vs Since
grammar.structure_pattern: for + duration | since + starting point
grammar.signal_words: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Muhim: for vaqt davomiyligini bildiradi; since esa qachondan boshlanganini bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Since» указывает точку начала («since yesterday»), «for» — продолжительность («for three days»), «ago» — отсчёт назад от настоящего («two hours ago»). Точное время («at about 7:15 this morning») критично при инсульте и других неотложных состояниях. Сигнальные слова: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Since" gives the starting point ("since yesterday"), "for" the length of time ("for three days") and "ago" counts back from now ("two hours ago"). Exact times ("at about 7:15 this morning") are essential in time-critical conditions such as stroke. Signal words: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. Have you ever been admitted to hospital because of asthma?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any particular triggers?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Cold air has been making it worse, and I've also been exposed to a lot of dust at work.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you recently had a cold or another respiratory infection?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It sounds as though your asthma control has deteriorated. We need to assess the severity of this exacerbation rather than assuming it is simply another mild attack.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Could I be having a serious asthma attack?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Your oxygen saturation and increased work of breathing are concerning, so we need to monitor you closely.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We'll also check your peak expiratory flow if you are able to perform the test safely.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I need steroids?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: How long will I have to stay here?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That depends on how your breathing responds. If your oxygenation improves and your symptoms settle, we may be able to discharge you with a revised asthma plan.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: She has been coughing at night for several weeks, even before this attack.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That suggests her underlying asthma may not have been well controlled for some time. We'll review her long-term treatment as well.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand. I don't want this to happen again.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: When were you first diagnosed with type 2 diabetes?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I was diagnosed three years ago during a routine health check. I wasn't experiencing obvious symptoms at the time.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What treatment did you start after the diagnosis?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I started metformin and changed my diet. For a while, my glucose levels were fairly stable.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have your glucose readings changed recently?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. They've been considerably higher over the past month.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did you last check your blood glucose?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I checked it this morning before breakfast. It was 12.6 millimoles per litre.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: His fasting capillary glucose here is 13.1 millimoles per litre.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed increased thirst or urination?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been extremely thirsty and I've been getting up several times during the night to urinate.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did those symptoms begin?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: They started about two weeks ago.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you missed any doses of metformin recently?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I have. I missed several doses last week because I was working night shifts.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have your eating habits changed as well?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, yes. I've been eating more fast food and sweet snacks because I haven't had time to cook.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you ever had an HbA1c above your target?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. It was high six months ago, but it improved after I changed my diet.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you experienced vomiting, abdominal pain, marked weakness, or confusion?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No vomiting or confusion, but I've been unusually tired.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We need to repeat your HbA1c, check renal function and electrolytes, and assess whether your current treatment remains appropriate.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Does a high glucose reading mean that my medication has stopped working?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. Poor adherence, dietary changes, infection, stress, and progression of diabetes can all contribute to hyperglycemia.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll arrange the blood tests and record his current medications.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: If my HbA1c is very high, will I need insulin?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It depends on the result and your overall clinical picture. We'll discuss the options once we have the full assessment.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm worried because I thought I was managing my diabetes well.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: The important thing is that you've come in now. We can identify what has changed and adjust the management rather than simply increasing medication without understanding the cause.

grammar.title: Grammar focus: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammar.title_en: Grammar focus: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammar.title_uz: Modul grammatikasi: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammar.title_ru: Грамматика модуля: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3 | Have/Has + subject + V3? | Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu dialogda Present Perfect hozirgi vaziyat bilan bog'liq tajriba, yaqindagi o'zgarish va simptomlarni so'rash uchun; Past Simple esa aniq tugagan vaqt, tashxis qo'yilgan vaqt, simptom boshlanishi va oldingi voqealarni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое с настоящим. В этом диалоге он используется для недавних изменений, опыта и симптомов, которые важны для текущего состояния пациента. Past Simple используется для конкретного завершённого момента в прошлом: три года назад, на прошлой неделе, шесть месяцев назад, две недели назад. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Present Perfect — Formula & Meaning
grammar.structure_pattern: Positive: have/has + V3 | Negative: have/has not + V3 | Question: Have/Has + subject + V3...? | Experience: Have/Has + subject + ever + V3...?
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Asosiy ma'no: o'tmishdagi voqea hozirgi klinik vaziyat bilan bog'langan; aniq tugagan vaqt ko'rsatilmagan. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: recent change with current relevance. life/medical experience up to the present. Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Past Simple — Formula & Meaning
grammar.structure_pattern: Positive: subject + V2 | Negative: subject + did not + V1 | Question: Did + subject + V1...? | Wh-Question: When did + subject + V1...?
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Asosiy ma'no: aniq o'tgan va tugagan vaqt yoki voqea. Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple описывает завершённые события в определённое время в прошлом: «The pain started yesterday», «When did you take the last dose?». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

grammar.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3 | Have/Has + subject + V3? | Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect o'tmishdagi voqeani hozirgi holat bilan bog'laydi: tajriba, yaqinda bo'lgan voqea yoki hozir muhim bo'lgan natija. Anamnez yig'ishda hozirgacha bo'lgan simptomlar so'raladi: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Past Simple o'tmishda aniq vaqtda tugagan voqealarni bildiradi: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Vaqt tugagan yoki aniq ko'rsatilgan bo'lsa shu zamon ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Past Simple описывает завершённые события в определённое время в прошлом: «The pain started yesterday», «When did you take the last dose?». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

Сигнальные слова помогают, но решающим является смысл: конкретное завершённое время → Past Simple; связь с настоящим или опыт → Present Perfect.

practice.setting: general medical clinic / hospital admissions unit
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Robert Lane
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative but anxious about the diagnosis

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I was diagnosed three years ago during a routine health check. I wasn't experiencing obvious symptoms at the time.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When were you first diagnosed with type 2 diabetes?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I was diagnosed three years ago during a routine health check. I wasn't experiencing obvious symptoms at the time.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What treatment did you start after the diagnosis?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I started metformin and changed my diet. For a while, my glucose levels were fairly stable.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have your glucose readings changed recently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. They've been considerably higher over the past month.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When did you last check your blood glucose?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I checked it this morning before breakfast. It was 12.6 millimoles per litre.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed increased thirst or urination?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I've been extremely thirsty and I've been getting up several times during the night to urinate.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When did those symptoms begin?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: They started about two weeks ago.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you missed any doses of metformin recently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I have. I missed several doses last week because I was working night shifts.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have your eating habits changed as well?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Unfortunately, yes. I've been eating more fast food and sweet snacks because I haven't had time to cook.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you ever had an HbA1c above your target?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. It was high six months ago, but it improved after I changed my diet.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you experienced vomiting, abdominal pain, marked weakness, or confusion?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No vomiting or confusion, but I've been unusually tired.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We need to repeat your HbA1c, check renal function and electrolytes, and assess whether your current treatment remains appropriate.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Does a high glucose reading mean that my medication has stopped working?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Not necessarily. Poor adherence, dietary changes, infection, stress, and progression of diabetes can all contribute to hyperglycemia.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'll arrange the blood tests and record his current medications.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It depends on the result and your overall clinical picture. We'll discuss the options once we have the full assessment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm worried because I thought I was managing my diabetes well.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Does a high glucose reading mean that my medication has stopped working?
If my HbA1c is very high, will I need insulin?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Please tell me exactly what happened and what time the symptoms began.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I noticed something was wrong at about 7:15 this morning while I was having breakfast.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What was the first symptom?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My right hand suddenly became weak. I dropped my cup and couldn't pick it up again.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What happened after that?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: A few minutes later, I tried to speak to my wife, but my words came out strangely.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: His face also looked uneven on the right side.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you understand what your wife was saying to you?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I understood everything, but I couldn't express myself properly.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you have any difficulty walking?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. When I stood up, my right leg felt weak and I nearly fell.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: His current blood pressure is 182 over 96. He is alert but has expressive speech difficulty and right-sided weakness.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you lose consciousness at any stage?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I remained conscious throughout.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you develop a sudden severe headache?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you notice any visual disturbance?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My vision became blurred for a few minutes, but then it improved.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What time did the ambulance arrive?

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: At approximately 7:45.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. The exact time of symptom onset is crucial because some stroke treatments are time-dependent.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is it possible to treat the blockage?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Potentially, yes. First we need urgent brain imaging to determine whether this is an ischemic stroke or a haemorrhage.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll arrange immediate transfer for CT imaging and continue neurological observations.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We also need to establish the last-known-well time and confirm whether there are any contraindications to reperfusion therapy.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What happens if the scan shows a blood clot?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If it confirms an eligible ischemic stroke, the stroke team will assess whether thrombolysis or mechanical thrombectomy is appropriate.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: And if there is bleeding?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: The management would be completely different, which is why imaging must be obtained before we make that decision.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I just want to know what we can do.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We are moving quickly because every minute can matter in acute stroke.

phrasebook.translation_ru: Во сколько приехала скорая помощь?

phrasebook.phrase: The exact time of symptom onset is crucial.

phrasebook.translation_ru: Точное время начала симптомов имеет решающее значение.

phrasebook.phrase: Some stroke treatments are time-dependent.

phrasebook.phrase: First we need urgent brain imaging.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to determine whether this is an ischemic stroke or a haemorrhage.
