dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. Come in and take a seat. What brings you to the clinic today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good afternoon, doctor. I'm having an unbearable, throbbing pain in my upper left molar. It's been driving me crazy since last night.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Was the pain sudden, or had you been experiencing mild discomfort before it became this severe?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Well, a couple of weeks ago, I noticed some sensitivity while drinking cold water, but I ignored it. Then yesterday evening, while I was having dinner, a sharp, shooting pain suddenly radiated through my whole jaw.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. That sounds like the nerve might be inflamed. Has the pain been continuous, or does it come and go in waves?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's almost constant now, but it gets significantly worse when I lie down. I couldn't get a single hour of sleep last night despite taking an over-the-counter painkiller.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's a classic symptom of pulpitis. Let's have a look inside. Please open wide... Ah, I can see a deep cavity on the chewing surface of that molar. I need to take a digital radiograph to assess the extent of the damage to the root canals.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right. If the nerve is damaged, does that mean I'll need a root canal treatment?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Most likely, yes. If the pulp is infected, saving the tooth will require removing the inflamed tissue, cleaning the canals, and sealing them. However, we won't know for sure until we examine the X-ray.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Oh dear. Is root canal therapy going to be a long and complicated process?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. With modern endodontic techniques, it is usually completed in one or two visits with minimal discomfort. I'll make sure the tooth is completely numbed before we start any procedure.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That's a relief. I was worried you might have to pull it out immediately.

dialogue.label: Doctor

grammar.title: Present Continuous and Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + V-ing | have / has + been + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ayni vaqtda sodir bo'layotgan yoki yaqin o'tmishdan beri davom etib kelayotgan holatlarni ifodalaydi. Signal so'zlar: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Continuous описывает действие в момент речи или временную, меняющуюся ситуацию: «His condition is getting worse», «I am going to examine you now». Также используется для ближайших действий врача. Present Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается (или только что закончилось и результат заметен). Ключевое время для длительности симптомов: «How long have you been feeling unwell?» — «I have been coughing for five days». Сигнальные слова: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. Present Perfect Continuous describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing (or has just stopped and its effect is visible). It is the key tense for symptom duration: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.

grammar.title: Past Simple and Past Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were | was / were + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: O'tmishda sodir bo'lgan harakatlar hamda boshqa bir harakat fonida davom etayotgan jarayonlarni ifodalash uchun qo'llaniladi. Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple описывает завершённые события в определённое время в прошлом: «The pain started yesterday», «When did you take the last dose?». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Past Continuous описывает действие в процессе в определённый момент прошлого, часто прерванное событием в Past Simple: «I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain». Показывает обстоятельства начала симптома. Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Past Continuous describes an action in progress at a moment in the past, often interrupted by a Past Simple event: "I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain". It gives the background of the onset. Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

grammar.title: Past Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: had + been + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: for, since, before, until
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: O'tmishdagi muayyan voqeadan oldin ma'lum muddat davom etgan harakatni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: for, since, before, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое длилось некоторое время до другого события в прошлом: «I had been feeling dizzy for ten minutes before I collapsed». Подчёркивает длительность до ключевого события. Сигнальные слова: for, since, before, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Perfect Continuous describes an action that had been going on for some time before another past event: "I had been feeling dizzy for ten minutes before I collapsed". It stresses duration before the key event. Signal words: for, since, before, until.

grammar.title: Conditionals — First Conditional
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, will / can / should + V1
grammar.signal_words: if, unless, as soon as, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Tibbiy tashxis va davolashdagi real shart va uning kelajakdagi ehtimoliy natijasini tushuntirishda ishlatiladi (If + Present Simple, Future Simple / Modal). Signal so'zlar: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: First Conditional описывает реальную, возможную ситуацию в будущем и её результат. Врач использует его для предупреждений, планов и рекомендаций по безопасности: «If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately». После «if» «will» не ставится. Сигнальные слова: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: First Conditional describes a real, possible future situation and its result. Clinicians use it for warnings, plans and safety-netting: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". Do not use "will" after "if". Signal words: if, unless, as soon as, when.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs & Future Forms
grammar.structure_pattern: modal (can / could / may / might / must / should / have to) + V1
grammar.signal_words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Zarurat, ehtimol va kelajakdagi harakat yoki va'dalarni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Eslatma: Grammatik qoidalar, fe'l zamonlarining yasalishi va qo'shimcha mashqlar bo'yicha chuqurroq tushunchaga ega bo'lish uchun avvalgi modullar grammatikasiga qaralsin. Signal so'zlar: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы передают отношение говорящего: возможность (may, might, could), способность/разрешение (can, could), совет (should, ought to), обязанность (must, have to) и запрет (mustn't). После модального глагола всегда стоит начальная форма. Сигнальные слова: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Modal verbs add the speaker's attitude: possibility (may, might, could), ability/permission (can, could), advice (should, ought to), obligation (must, have to) and prohibition (mustn't). The main verb after a modal is always the base form. Signal words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please, sit down. What brings you in today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning, Doctor. I've had a severe, throbbing pain in my lower left tooth for three days now, and my cheek is noticeably swollen.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Let's take a look. Please open wide. Ah, yes, I can see significant inflammation and swelling in the surrounding gum tissue. It appears you have a dental abscess, which is a localized accumulation of pus caused by a bacterial infection.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: A dental abscess? That sounds alarming. Could that explain why I've also been feeling slightly feverish and having trouble opening my mouth fully?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Exactly. A low-grade fever and difficulty opening your mouth are classic signs that the infection is spreading to adjacent tissues. The infection typically originates in the tooth's pulp—usually from deep decay or a micro-crack—and extends down to the root tip.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I see. Does this mean the tooth has to be extracted, or can it still be saved?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Our main priority is to eliminate the infection while preserving your natural tooth if possible. I'll order a digital X-ray right away to check the condition of the bone and roots. If the structure is intact, we can perform a root canal procedure to clean out the infected tissue and seal the canals.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need a prescription for antibiotics as well?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Given the facial swelling and your fever, I'll prescribe a course of antibiotics along with anti-inflammatory pain relievers. However, please remember that antibiotics only control the spread—the dental procedure itself is necessary to permanently resolve the issue.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Understood. Is there anything I should do to manage this until the procedure?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Gently rinse with warm salt water and avoid extreme hot or cold temperatures. Most importantly, if you experience any difficulty breathing or sudden swelling towards your eye or neck, head straight to the emergency department.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes total sense. Thank you for the clear explanation, Doctor. Let's go ahead with the X-ray.

grammar.title: Present Perfect
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3 | Subject + have/has + V3 | for + vaqt davomiyligi | since + boshlanish nuqtasi
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect o'tmishda boshlangan, lekin hozirgi holat bilan bog'liq bo'lgan vaziyatni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect используется для ситуации, которая началась в прошлом и связана с настоящим. В данном случае боль началась три дня назад и до сих пор продолжается. У неё температура со вчерашнего дня. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". "Since" gives the starting point ("since yesterday"), "for" the length of time ("for three days") and "ago" counts back from now ("two hours ago"). Exact times ("at about 7:15 this morning") are essential in time-critical conditions such as stroke. Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has been + V-ing | Subject + have/has been + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Tibbiy suhbatlarda bu zamon bemorning davom etayotgan simptomlarini tasvirlashda juda foydali. Signal so'zlar: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect Continuous подчёркивает длительность процесса или симптома, который начался в прошлом и продолжается сейчас. В медицинском английском эта форма часто используется для описания продолжающихся симптомов. Сигнальные слова: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect Continuous describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing (or has just stopped and its effect is visible). It is the key tense for symptom duration: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.

grammar.title: Present Simple
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V1 | Subject + V-s
grammar.signal_words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu yerda Present Simple bemorning ayni paytdagi harakatini emas, umumiy tibbiy fakt yoki odatiy jarayonni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Здесь Present Simple используется для описания общего медицинского факта, закономерности или типичного процесса. Врач объясняет, как обычно развивается инфекция. Инфекция обычно начинается в пульпе. Сигнальные слова: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.

grammar.title: Passive Voice
grammar.structure_pattern: be + V3 | Subject + be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Tibbiy ingliz tilida Passive Voice juda ko'p ishlatiladi, chunki ko'pincha jarayon yoki bemorning holati muhim bo'ladi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: В Passive Voice внимание сосредоточено не на том, кто выполняет действие, а на объекте, который подвергается этому действию. Медицинский английский очень часто использует Passive Voice. Зубной абсцесс вызывается бактериальной инфекцией. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs
grammar.structure_pattern: could + V1 | can + be + V3
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu yerda could ehtimol yoki taxminni bildiradi. Bu yerda can imkoniyatni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Здесь could выражает предположение или возможность. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

grammar.title: Gerund
grammar.structure_pattern: V-ing | have trouble + V-ing | have difficulty + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: biror ishni qilishda qiynalmoq Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: обычно используется форма V-ing. испытывать трудности при выполнении какого-либо действия. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

grammar.title: First Conditional
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, + can/will/may + V1 | If + Present Simple + Imperative
grammar.signal_words: if, unless, as soon as, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: First Conditional real, ehtimoliy kelajakdagi vaziyat va uning natijasini bildiradi. Shifokor ogohlantirish, reja va xavfsizlik ko'rsatmalari uchun ishlatadi: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". "If" dan keyin "will" ishlatilmaydi. Present Simple odatiy, takrorlanuvchi harakatlar, umumiy faktlar va doimiy holatlarni bildiradi. Klinikada odatdagi simptomlar ("The pain usually starts at night"), muntazam dori qabuli va umumiy tibbiy faktlar uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Первый тип условных предложений используется для реального или возможного условия. В придаточной части после if обычно используется Present Simple, даже если речь идёт о будущем. Сигнальные слова: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: First Conditional describes a real, possible future situation and its result. Clinicians use it for warnings, plans and safety-netting: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". Do not use "will" after "if". Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: if, unless, as soon as, when.

grammar.title: Imperative
grammar.structure_pattern: V1 + ... | Please + V1 gapni muloyimroq qiladi.
grammar.signal_words: please, do not, never, always
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Buyruq gaplar to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ko'rsatma va shoshilinch buyruqlar uchun ishlatiladi: "Take a deep breath", "Do not eat or drink anything", "Call an ambulance immediately". Bemorga nisbatan "please" yoki "could you" bilan yumshatiladi. Signal so'zlar: please, do not, never, always.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Повелительное наклонение даёт прямые инструкции и команды в неотложной ситуации: «Take a deep breath», «Do not eat or drink anything», «Call an ambulance immediately». Для пациента смягчается словами «please» или «could you». Сигнальные слова: please, do not, never, always.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Imperatives give direct instructions and emergency commands: "Take a deep breath", "Do not eat or drink anything", "Call an ambulance immediately". "Please" or "could you" softens them for patients. Signal words: please, do not, never, always.

grammar.title: Have to + Passive
grammar.structure_pattern: Passive Voice = be + V3 | have/has to + be + V3 | have to + Passive Voice | Have to + Passive | 1. Symptom + FOR | 2. Symptom + Present Perfect Continuous | 3. Difficulty / Trouble + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: necessity, obligation, prohibition
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bir muncha vaqtdan beri isitmalayotgandek his qilyapman. Signal so'zlar: necessity, obligation, prohibition.

grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Must" expresses strong necessity from the speaker ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — an external rule or requirement. "Mustn't" means it is forbidden, while "don't have to" means it is not necessary. Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: necessity, obligation, prohibition.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. What brings you in today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning, Doctor. I've noticed a sudden sensitivity in one of my molars. It becomes particularly uncomfortable whenever I bite down on something hard or have a cold drink.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Does anything in particular bring on the discomfort?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. Cold drinks seem to bring it on, and sometimes I get a brief, throbbing sensation when I bite on that tooth.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any swelling or tenderness around the tooth?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: There's no noticeable swelling, but the area around the tooth feels slightly tender when I press on it.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. Let me take a closer look. I'll check the tooth for any visible signs of decay and see how it reacts to pressure and temperature.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay, Doctor.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I can see a small cavity on the surface of your molar. There's also some discoloration around the affected area.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean I have dental caries?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, it appears that you have an early stage of dental caries. The decay hasn't reached the deeper layers of the tooth yet, which is a positive sign.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What might have caused it?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Several factors could be involved. Frequent exposure to sugary foods, inadequate brushing, and a lack of fluoride can all contribute to tooth decay.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been having sweet snacks quite often recently. Could that be making the problem worse?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It could. When you frequently consume sugary foods, bacteria in your mouth produce acids that gradually weaken the enamel.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: So, what kind of treatment would I need?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: At this stage, a filling should be enough. I'll remove the decayed part of the tooth. If you feel any pain during the procedure, I'll give you a local anaesthetic injection to make you more comfortable.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. And what can I do to prevent another cavity?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Brush your teeth twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, clean between your teeth regularly, and try to limit sugary snacks between meals.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Would regular dental check-ups help as well?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Absolutely. If cavities are detected early, they can usually be treated before they cause more serious damage.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I'll pay more attention to my oral hygiene from now on.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. We can treat the cavity with a filling before the decay gets any deeper.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right, Doctor. I'm ready to have it treated.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Excellent. We'll get started shortly. Taking care of it now will help protect the tooth from further damage.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate your explanation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're very welcome.

grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + could + V1
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Modal verbs asosiy fe'lga qo'shimcha ma'no beradi: imkoniyat, ehtimol, tavsiya, zarurat va boshqalar. Could — ehtimol / mumkin Should — kerak / ma'qul Can — mumkin / qila olmoq Would — muloyim savol / so'rov Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Can» выражает способность, разрешение и возможность в настоящем («DKA can become life-threatening»); «could» — более мягкий, вежливый вариант («Could you describe the pain?») и способность в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

grammar.title: Conditional — First Conditional
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, will + V1
grammar.signal_words: if, unless, as soon as, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: First Conditional real yoki ehtimoliy kelajakdagi shart va natijani ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Important: If qismidan keyin odatda will ishlatilmaydi. Signal so'zlar: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: First Conditional описывает реальную, возможную ситуацию в будущем и её результат. Врач использует его для предупреждений, планов и рекомендаций по безопасности: «If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately». После «if» «will» не ставится. Present Simple описывает привычные, регулярные действия, общие факты и постоянные состояния. В клинике используется для типичных симптомов («The pain usually starts at night»), регулярного приёма лекарств и общих медицинских фактов. Сигнальные слова: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: First Conditional describes a real, possible future situation and its result. Clinicians use it for warnings, plans and safety-netting: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". Do not use "will" after "if". Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: if, unless, as soon as, when.

common_mistakes.incorrect: If you will feel any pain...

grammar.title: Passive Voice
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + V3 | Modal + Passive | modal + be + V3 | 2. First Conditional: If + Present Simple | 3. Passive Voice: be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Passive Voice'da harakatni kim bajarayotgani emas, harakatning o'zi yoki uning obyekti muhim bo'ladi. Module maqsadi: oldingi modullarda o'rganilgan Present Simple, Present Perfect, Past Simple va Future Simple zamonlarini qisqacha review qilish hamda Dental Caries dialogi asosida Modal Verbs, First Conditional va Passive Voice'ni mustahkamlash. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». First Conditional описывает реальную, возможную ситуацию в будущем и её результат. Врач использует его для предупреждений, планов и рекомендаций по безопасности: «If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately». После «if» «will» не ставится. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". First Conditional describes a real, possible future situation and its result. Clinicians use it for warnings, plans and safety-netting: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". Do not use "will" after "if". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

practice.setting: dental clinic
practice.role_play: The student is the DENTIST. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Oliver Grant
patient_profile.personality_trait: nervous about dental treatment, sensitive to pain

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning, Doctor. I've noticed a sudden sensitivity in one of my molars. It becomes particularly uncomfortable whenever I bite down on something hard or have a cold drink.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. What brings you in today?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning, Doctor. I've noticed a sudden sensitivity in one of my molars. It becomes particularly uncomfortable whenever I bite down on something hard or have a cold drink.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Does anything in particular bring on the discomfort?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. Cold drinks seem to bring it on, and sometimes I get a brief, throbbing sensation when I bite on that tooth.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any swelling or tenderness around the tooth?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: There's no noticeable swelling, but the area around the tooth feels slightly tender when I press on it.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. Let me take a closer look. I'll check the tooth for any visible signs of decay and see how it reacts to pressure and temperature.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay, Doctor.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I can see a small cavity on the surface of your molar. There's also some discoloration around the affected area.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Does that mean I have dental caries?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes, it appears that you have an early stage of dental caries. The decay hasn't reached the deeper layers of the tooth yet, which is a positive sign.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What might have caused it?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Several factors could be involved. Frequent exposure to sugary foods, inadequate brushing, and a lack of fluoride can all contribute to tooth decay.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've been having sweet snacks quite often recently. Could that be making the problem worse?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It could. When you frequently consume sugary foods, bacteria in your mouth produce acids that gradually weaken the enamel.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: So, what kind of treatment would I need?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: At this stage, a filling should be enough. I'll remove the decayed part of the tooth. If you feel any pain during the procedure, I'll give you a local anaesthetic injection to mak…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand. And what can I do to prevent another cavity?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Brush your teeth twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, clean between your teeth regularly, and try to limit sugary snacks between meals.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Would regular dental check-ups help as well?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Absolutely. If cavities are detected early, they can usually be treated before they cause more serious damage.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: That makes sense. I'll pay more attention to my oral hygiene from now on.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good. We can treat the cavity with a filling before the decay gets any deeper.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right, Doctor. I'm ready to have it treated.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Excellent. We'll get started shortly. Taking care of it now will help protect the tooth from further damage.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate your explanation.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Does that mean I have dental caries?
What might have caused it?
Could that be making the problem worse?
So, what kind of treatment would I need?
And what can I do to prevent another cavity?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. Please have a seat. What seems to be bothering you?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good afternoon, Doctor. My gums are becoming quite uncomfortable. They're bleeding whenever I brush my teeth, and the area around my front teeth feels swollen.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. Are you experiencing any pain at the moment?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: There isn't much pain, but my gums feel sore, especially when I'm brushing.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to examine your gums and check for any signs of inflammation. Please open your mouth slightly wider.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Of course.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I can see some redness and swelling along the gum line. Your gums are also bleeding quite easily when I touch them.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is that something serious?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It could become a serious problem if it isn't treated properly. At the moment, the symptoms are consistent with gum inflammation, which is often associated with plaque buildup.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Could poor brushing be the reason?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It might be one of the reasons. Plaque can accumulate around the gum line when the teeth aren't being cleaned thoroughly, and this can lead to irritation and inflammation.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm trying to brush regularly, but I sometimes rush through it because I'm in a hurry.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That could explain why some areas aren't being cleaned effectively. Are you using dental floss or an interdental brush?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm not using either of them regularly. I usually just brush my teeth.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: In that case, food particles and plaque may be remaining between your teeth. These areas are difficult to clean with a toothbrush alone.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What would you recommend?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: First, we'll carry out a professional cleaning to remove the plaque and tartar around your gums. After that, you'll need to improve your daily oral hygiene.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What should I do if my gums continue to bleed after the cleaning?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Some mild bleeding may occur initially, but it should gradually decrease as the inflammation settles down. If the bleeding becomes heavier or continues for a long time, you should come back for another examination.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Should I stop brushing until the bleeding goes away?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: No. You shouldn't stop brushing. Instead, use a soft-bristled toothbrush and brush gently along the gum line.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What about flossing?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You should continue flossing carefully. It may feel uncomfortable at first, but regular cleaning between the teeth will help keep the gums healthier.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is there anything else I should change?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You should reduce sugary snacks and avoid smoking, as both can contribute to gum problems. Drinking enough water can also help maintain a healthier mouth.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: If I follow all these recommendations, will my gums return to normal?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: They should improve considerably if the inflammation is treated and you maintain good oral hygiene. However, if the condition progresses, deeper treatment may be required.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I'm going to take better care of my gums from now on.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. We'll start with the professional cleaning today, and I'll show you the correct brushing and flossing techniques before you leave.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you, Doctor.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Taking action early can help prevent more serious gum disease in the future.

phrasebook.translation_ru: Если зубы недостаточно тщательно чистить, вдоль линии дёсен может скапливаться зубной налёт.

phrasebook.phrase: Are you using dental floss or an interdental brush?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tish ipi yoki tishlar orasini tozalash uchun maxsus cho'tkadan foydalanasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы пользуетесь зубной нитью или межзубной щёткой?
phrasebook.patient_response: I'm not using either of them regularly.
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Ularning hech qaysisidan muntazam foydalanmayman.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Я не пользуюсь регулярно ни тем, ни другим.

phrasebook.phrase: These areas are difficult to clean with a toothbrush alone.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu joylarni faqat tish cho'tkasi bilan tozalash qiyin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Эти участки трудно очистить только зубной щёткой.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll carry out a professional cleaning to remove the plaque and tartar around your gums.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Milklaringiz atrofidagi tish karashi va toshlarini olib tashlash uchun professional tozalash o'tkazamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы проведём профессиональную чистку, чтобы удалить зубной налёт и камень вокруг дёсен.

phrasebook.phrase: You should come back for another examination if the bleeding continues for a long time.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar qonash uzoq vaqt davom etsa, qayta ko'rikdan o'tish uchun kelishingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если кровотечение будет продолжаться долго, вам следует прийти на повторный осмотр.

phrasebook.phrase: You shouldn't stop brushing. Instead, use a soft-bristled toothbrush.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tishlaringizni yuvishni to'xtatmasligingiz kerak. Buning o'rniga yumshoq tukli tish cho'tkasidan foydalaning.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам не следует прекращать чистить зубы. Вместо этого используйте зубную щётку с мягкой щетиной.

phrasebook.phrase: You should continue flossing carefully.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tish ipidan ehtiyotkorlik bilan foydalanishda davom etishingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам следует продолжать осторожно пользоваться зубной нитью.

phrasebook.phrase: You should reduce sugary snacks and avoid smoking.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shirinliklarni kamaytirishingiz va chekishdan saqlanishingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам следует сократить употребление сладостей и избегать курения.
phrasebook.patient_response: If I follow all these recommendations, will my gums return to normal?
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Agar barcha tavsiyalaringizga amal qilsam, milklarim yana normal holatga qaytadimi?
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Если я буду следовать всем этим рекомендациям, мои дёсны вернутся в нормальное состояние?

phrasebook.phrase: They should improve considerably if the inflammation is treated and you maintain good oral hygiene.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar yallig'lanish davolansa va siz yaxshi og'iz gigiyenasiga amal qilsangiz, milklaringiz ancha yaxshilanishi kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если воспаление будет вылечено и вы будете соблюдать хорошую гигиену полости рта, состояние дёсен должно значительно улучшиться.

grammar.title: Present Simple — Quick Review
grammar.structure_pattern: usually / regularly / can + general fact
grammar.signal_words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Simple odatiy holat, umumiy fakt yoki muntazam harakatlar uchun ishlatiladi. Bu joylarni faqat tish cho'tkasi bilan tozalash qiyin. Signal so'zlar: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Эти участки трудно очистить только зубной щёткой. Сигнальные слова: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.

grammar.title: Present Perfect — Quick Review
grammar.structure_pattern: Eslatma: have/has + V3 | for + vaqt
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect avvalgi modullarda batafsil o'rganilgan. Bu modulda uni qayta dars sifatida bermaymiz. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Past Simple — Quick Review
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Past Simple o'tmishda sodir bo'lgan va tugagan voqealar uchun ishlatiladi. Bu dialogda Past Simple deyarli ishlatilmagan. Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple описывает завершённые события в определённое время в прошлом: «The pain started yesterday», «When did you take the last dose?». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: 🔑 yesterday / last night / ago → Past Simple Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

grammar.title: Future Simple — Quick Review
grammar.structure_pattern: will + V1
grammar.signal_words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Future Simple (will) kelajakdagi qaror, va'da yoki kutilayotgan harakat uchun ishlatiladi. Bu dialogda kelajak ma'nosi asosan boshqa future forms orqali berilgan. Signal so'zlar: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Will» выражает решение, принятое в момент речи, обещание, прогноз и успокоение пациента: «I will give you something for the pain», «The swelling will go down in a few days». Сигнальные слова: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.

grammar.title: Present Continuous — New Focus
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Continuous hozirgi paytda davom etayotgan yoki vaqtinchalik jarayonni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Men tishlarimni muntazam yuvishga harakat qilyapman. Signal so'zlar: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Я стараюсь регулярно чистить зубы. Сигнальные слова: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. Signal words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.

examples.sentence: Yana bir misol: My gums are becoming quite uncomfortable.
examples.translation_ru: Мои дёсны становятся довольно чувствительными/доставляют дискомфорт.

grammar.title: BE Going TO — Planned Action
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + going to + V1
grammar.signal_words: now, next, first, then
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Be going to kelajakdagi reja yoki oldindan qabul qilingan niyatni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Bundan buyon milklarimga yaxshiroq g'amxo'rlik qilmoqchiman. Signal so'zlar: now, next, first, then.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: С этого момента я собираюсь лучше заботиться о своих дёснах. Сигнальные слова: now, next, first, then.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Be going to" describes a plan or intention and something about to happen: "I am going to examine your abdomen now", "We are going to run some tests". Clinicians use it to announce each step of the examination. Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: now, next, first, then.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs — Possibility & Advice
grammar.structure_pattern: could + V1
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Modal verbs imkoniyat, ehtimol, maslahat yoki zaruratni ifodalashga yordam beradi. Could — ehtimol / mumkin Might — ehtimol / mumkin Should — kerak / tavsiya May — mumkin / ehtimol Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Can» выражает способность, разрешение и возможность в настоящем («DKA can become life-threatening»); «could» — более мягкий, вежливый вариант («Could you describe the pain?») и способность в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

grammar.title: First Conditional — Real Future Condition
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, will + V1
grammar.signal_words: if, unless, as soon as, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: First Conditional real yoki ehtimoliy kelajakdagi shart va natijani ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Agar barcha tavsiyalaringizga amal qilsam, milklarim yana normal holatga qaytadimi? Important: If qismidan keyin odatda will ishlatilmaydi. Signal so'zlar: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Если я буду следовать всем этим рекомендациям, мои дёсны вернутся в нормальное состояние? Сигнальные слова: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: First Conditional describes a real, possible future situation and its result. Clinicians use it for warnings, plans and safety-netting: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". Do not use "will" after "if". Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: if, unless, as soon as, when.

grammar.title: Passive Voice — Present & Modal Passive
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + being + V3 | Modal + Passive | modal + be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Passive Voice'da harakatni kim bajarayotgani emas, harakatning o'zi yoki uning obyekti muhim bo'ladi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Gerund — Verb + -ing
grammar.structure_pattern: avoid / continue + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ba'zi fe'llardan keyin boshqa fe'l -ing shaklida keladi. Dialogda bu ayniqsa avoid va continue bilan ko'rinadi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Герундий (V-ing) выступает как существительное после глаголов avoid, stop, keep, recommend и предлогов («Avoid eating before the test»). Инфинитив (to + V1) стоит после need, want, decide, advise someone и выражает цель («We need to run some tests», «in order to rule out appendicitis»). Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

examples.sentence: You should avoid smoking.

grammar.title: Infinitive — to + V1
grammar.structure_pattern: 1. Present Continuous: am / is / are + V-ing | 2. Be going to: am / is / are + going to + V1 | 4. First Conditional: If + Present Simple | 5. Passive Voice: be…
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund (V-ing) ot vazifasida keladi va avoid, stop, keep, recommend fe'llari hamda predloglardan keyin ishlatiladi ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitiv (to + V1) need, want, decide, advise someone dan keyin keladi va maqsadni bildiradi ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Present Continuous ayni paytda bo'layotgan yoki vaqtinchalik, o'zgarayotgan holatni bildiradi: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". Shifokorning hozirgi rejasini aytishda ham ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Герундий (V-ing) выступает как существительное после глаголов avoid, stop, keep, recommend и предлогов («Avoid eating before the test»). Инфинитив (to + V1) стоит после need, want, decide, advise someone и выражает цель («We need to run some tests», «in order to rule out appendicitis»). Present Continuous описывает действие в момент речи или временную, меняющуюся ситуацию: «His condition is getting worse», «I am going to examine you now». Также используется для ближайших действий врача. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: 12. IMPORTANT GRAMMAR POINTS — Gum Problems Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good afternoon, Doctor. My gums are becoming quite uncomfortable. They're bleeding whenever I brush my teeth, and the area around my front teeth feels swollen.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: It could become a serious problem if it isn't treated properly. At the moment, the symptoms are consistent with gum inflammation, which is often associated with plaque buildup.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good afternoon. Please have a seat. What seems to be bothering you?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good afternoon, Doctor. My gums are becoming quite uncomfortable. They're bleeding whenever I brush my teeth, and the area around my front teeth feels swollen.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. Are you experiencing any pain at the moment?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: There isn't much pain, but my gums feel sore, especially when I'm brushing.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. I'm going to examine your gums and check for any signs of inflammation. Please open your mouth slightly wider.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Of course.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I can see some redness and swelling along the gum line. Your gums are also bleeding quite easily when I touch them.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is that something serious?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It could become a serious problem if it isn't treated properly. At the moment, the symptoms are consistent with gum inflammation, which is often associated with plaque buildup.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Could poor brushing be the reason?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It might be one of the reasons. Plaque can accumulate around the gum line when the teeth aren't being cleaned thoroughly, and this can lead to irritation and inflammation.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm trying to brush regularly, but I sometimes rush through it because I'm in a hurry.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That could explain why some areas aren't being cleaned effectively. Are you using dental floss or an interdental brush?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm not using either of them regularly. I usually just brush my teeth.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: In that case, food particles and plaque may be remaining between your teeth. These areas are difficult to clean with a toothbrush alone.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What would you recommend?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: First, we'll carry out a professional cleaning to remove the plaque and tartar around your gums. After that, you'll need to improve your daily oral hygiene.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What should I do if my gums continue to bleed after the cleaning?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Some mild bleeding may occur initially, but it should gradually decrease as the inflammation settles down. If the bleeding becomes heavier or continues for a long time, you should…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Should I stop brushing until the bleeding goes away?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: No. You shouldn't stop brushing. Instead, use a soft-bristled toothbrush and brush gently along the gum line.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What about flossing?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You should continue flossing carefully. It may feel uncomfortable at first, but regular cleaning between the teeth will help keep the gums healthier.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is there anything else I should change?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You should reduce sugary snacks and avoid smoking, as both can contribute to gum problems. Drinking enough water can also help maintain a healthier mouth.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: If I follow all these recommendations, will my gums return to normal?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: They should improve considerably if the inflammation is treated and you maintain good oral hygiene. However, if the condition progresses, deeper treatment may be required.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand. I'm going to take better care of my gums from now on.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good. We'll start with the professional cleaning today, and I'll show you the correct brushing and flossing techniques before you leave.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you, Doctor.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. Please take a seat. What brings you in today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good afternoon, Doctor. I've been having a persistent, throbbing ache near the back of my lower jaw for a few days now. It's gotten quite painful to chew, and my jaw feels a bit stiff when I open my mouth.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. Let me take a look. Could you tilt your head back and open your mouth as wide as you comfortably can?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Sure... like this?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Perfect. Looking inside, I can see that your lower back molar hasn't fully come through. Part of it is still covered by a flap of gum tissue, and the surrounding area looks red and swollen.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Oh, is it growing in the wrong direction?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It appears so. The tooth seems to be coming in at an angle, leaning directly toward the neighboring molar. Because there isn't enough space in your jaw, it's unable to erupt properly.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean it's a wisdom tooth?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Exactly, an impacted wisdom tooth. When it doesn't have enough place to emerge normally, we refer to it as being "impacted.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Could this damage the healthy tooth next to it?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, potentially. It can exert constant pressure against the adjacent tooth, which can damage the enamel or lead to decay. Furthermore, that gum flap creates a tight pocket where food and bacteria easily get trapped, making it very difficult to clean.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I've actually noticed an unpleasant taste in my mouth around that area lately. Is that related?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Food debris and bacteria tend to gather under the gum flap, which often leads to localized inflammation—a condition we call pericoronitis—and that frequently causes a bad taste or odor.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I see. What should we do next?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: The next step is to take a panoramic X-ray. This will give us a clear view of the tooth's exact position, its roots, and how close it is to the adjacent tooth and underlying nerves.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need to have it extracted?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Quite possibly. If the X-ray confirms that the tooth is impacted and likely to cause ongoing pain or infection, extraction is usually the safest long-term solution.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What would happen if I decided to leave it alone for now?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If left untreated, the inflammation and pain are very likely to recur. Over time, it could lead to a deeper infection or damage the healthy neighboring tooth.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I definitely don't want it to get any worse. I'd rather take care of it now.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's a wise decision. Let's go ahead and get the X-ray done. Once I review the image, I'll explain the findings and discuss the safest options with you.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right, Doctor. I'm ready.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Great. Follow me to the X-ray room, and we'll get started.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + been + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect Continuous o'tmishda boshlanib hozirgacha davom etayotgan (yoki hozirgina to'xtagan va ta'siri sezilayotgan) harakatni bildiradi. Simptom davomiyligi uchun asosiy zamon: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal so'zlar: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается (или только что закончилось и результат заметен). Ключевое время для длительности симптомов: «How long have you been feeling unwell?» — «I have been coughing for five days». Сигнальные слова: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect Continuous describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing (or has just stopped and its effect is visible). It is the key tense for symptom duration: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.

examples.sentence: I've been having a persistent, throbbing ache near the back of my lower jaw for a few days now.
examples.translation_uz: Bir necha kundan beri pastki jag'imning orqa qismida doimiy, urib turadigan og'riq bo'lyapti.
examples.translation_ru: Уже несколько дней у меня постоянная пульсирующая боль в задней части нижней челюсти.

examples.sentence: I've been having pain for three days.
examples.translation_ru: У меня уже три дня болит.

grammar.title: Modal Verb — Could
grammar.structure_pattern: could + V1 ehtimoliy natijani bildiradi. can + V1 esa imkoniyat yoki umumiy ehtimolni bildirishi mumkin.
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "Can" qobiliyat, ruxsat va hozirgi ehtimollikni bildiradi ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" yumshoqroq, muloyimroq ("Could you describe the pain?") va o'tmishdagi qobiliyatni ifodalaydi. Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Can» выражает способность, разрешение и возможность в настоящем («DKA can become life-threatening»); «could» — более мягкий, вежливый вариант («Could you describe the pain?») и способность в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

grammar.title: Passive Voice
grammar.structure_pattern: be (am/is/are/was/were/will be/has been) + V3 | modal + be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Passive Voice harakatni kim bajarayotganidan ko'ra harakatning o'zi yoki bemor muhim bo'lganda ishlatiladi — tahlillar, muolajalar va davolash rejasi uchun odatiy: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Once + Present Simple → Future Simple
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V1 (he/she/it + V-s) | Do/Does + subject + V1? | will + V1 | will not (won't) + V1
grammar.signal_words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Simple odatiy, takrorlanuvchi harakatlar, umumiy faktlar va doimiy holatlarni bildiradi. Klinikada odatdagi simptomlar ("The pain usually starts at night"), muntazam dori qabuli va umumiy tibbiy faktlar uchun ishlatiladi. "Will" hozir qabul qilingan qaror, va'da, bashorat va bemorni tinchlantirishni ifodalaydi: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal so'zlar: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Simple описывает привычные, регулярные действия, общие факты и постоянные состояния. В клинике используется для типичных симптомов («The pain usually starts at night»), регулярного приёма лекарств и общих медицинских фактов. «Will» выражает решение, принятое в момент речи, обещание, прогноз и успокоение пациента: «I will give you something for the pain», «The swelling will go down in a few days». Сигнальные слова: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.

grammar.title: Would rather + V1
grammar.structure_pattern: NEW / IMPORTANT: Present Perfect Continuous, Modal verbs (Could), Passive Voice, If left untreated, Causative have + object + V3, Once + Present Simple
grammar.signal_words: preference
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: REVIEW: Present Simple, Present Perfect, Past Simple, Future Simple — avvalgi modullarda o'tilgan zamonlar sifatida qisqa takrorlanadi. Signal so'zlar: preference.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Would rather + V1» и «would prefer to + V1» вежливо выражают предпочтение: «I would rather save the tooth than extract it», «Would you prefer a crown or an implant?» Present Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается (или только что закончилось и результат заметен). Ключевое время для длительности симптомов: «How long have you been feeling unwell?» — «I have been coughing for five days». Сигнальные слова: preference.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Would rather + V1" and "would prefer to + V1" express preference politely: "I would rather save the tooth than extract it", "Would you prefer a crown or an implant?" Present Perfect Continuous describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing (or has just stopped and its effect is visible). It is the key tense for symptom duration: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days".

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please, take a seat. What seems to be the problem?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning, Doctor. I've been suffering from an intense ache in one of my bottom back teeth on the right side. The throbbing had been getting worse all day, and it became completely agonizing last night.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. Had you been experiencing any discomfort before the pain reached that level?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I had been feeling a dull ache for about three days, but I had ignored it because I thought it would fade away.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Had you noticed any swelling or sensitivity prior to last night?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, the gum around the tooth had swollen slightly. I had also noticed that the tooth was extremely sensitive to ice-cold drinks.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Had you taken any painkillers before coming to the clinic?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I had swallowed two tablets during the night, but they had barely dullened the pain.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Had you been chewing hard food or had you injured the tooth recently?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I hadn't injured it. But I had been chewing mostly on that side because my left side had been bothering me as well.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to examine the area now. Please tell me if you feel any sharp pain.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I can see significant inflammation. It looks as though the infection had been spreading under the surface and has now reached the root.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is it serious? I'm worried you'll have to extract it.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We'll try our best to save it. Had the tooth received any treatment in the past?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. A dentist had placed a filling there several years ago.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That explains it. The old filling had deteriorated, and bacteria had been entering the inner tooth over time.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: So what is the next step?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: First, we'll take an X-ray to check the exact condition. If the nerve is badly affected, you may need a root canal.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I feel much pain during the procedure?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: No, I'll use a local anesthetic to numb the area. You may feel slight pressure, but no sharp pain.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That's a relief! I had been stressing about the procedure all morning.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's completely natural. However, you shouldn't delay treatment when severe swelling occurs.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. If I had come earlier, would the treatment have been simpler?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, exactly. If you had come when the discomfort first started, we could have treated it much faster. But don't worry, we'll fix it now.

phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Ha. Taxminan 3 kun simillagan og'riqni sezib yurgan edim, lekin e'tibor bermagan edim.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Да. Около трех дней я чувствовал тупую боль, но игнорировал её.

phrasebook.phrase: HAD YOU NOTICED any swelling or sensitivity prior to last night?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /hæd juː ˈnəʊtɪst ˈeni ˈswelɪŋ ɔː ˌsensəˈtɪvəti/
phrasebook.patient_response: Yes, the gum HAD SWOLLEN slightly. I HAD ALSO NOTICED that the tooth was sensitive to cold drinks.
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Ha, milk biroz shishgan edi. Tishim muzdek ichimliklarga sezgir bo'lib qolganini sezgan edim.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Да, десна немного опухла. Я также заметил чувствительность к холодным напиткам.

phrasebook.phrase: HAD YOU TAKEN any painkillers before coming to the clinic?
phrasebook.patient_response: Yes. I HAD SWALLOWED two tablets, but they HAD BARELY DULLENED the pain.
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Ha. Kechasi ikkita tabletka ichgan edim, lekin ular og'riqni deyarli qoldirmadi.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Да. Я выпил две таблетки, но они едва уменьшили боль.

phrasebook.phrase: HAD YOU BEEN CHEWING hard food or HAD YOU INJURED the tooth?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Qattiq yegulik chaynaganmidingiz yoki tishni shikastlaganmidingiz?
phrasebook.patient_response: I HADN'T INJURED it, but I HAD BEEN CHEWING mostly on that side because the other HAD BEEN BOTHERING me.
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Shikastlamagan edim. Lekin aksariyat shu tomonda chaynayotgan edim, chunki chap tomonim ham bezovta qilayotgan edi.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Я не травмировал его, но жевал в основном на этой стороне, так как другая тоже беспокоила.

phrasebook.phrase: It looks as though the infection HAD BEEN SPREADING under the surface and reached the root.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɪt lʊks əz ðəʊði ɪnˈfekʃən hæd biːn ˈspredɪŋ/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ko'rinishidan, infeksiya sirt ostida tarqalayotgan bo'lgan va ildizgacha yetgan.
phrasebook.patient_response: Is it serious? I'm worried you'll have to extract it.
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Bu jiddiy xavfmi? Tishni sug'urib olishingizdan xavotirdaman.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Это серьезно? Я боюсь, что вам придется его удалить.

phrasebook.phrase: HAD THE TOOTH RECEIVED any treatment in the past?
phrasebook.patient_response: Yes. A dentist HAD PLACED a filling there several years ago.
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Ha. Bir necha yil oldin shifokor plomba qo'yib bergan edi.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Да. Несколько лет назад стоматолог поставил туда пломбу.

phrasebook.phrase: The old filling HAD DETERIORATED, and bacteria HAD BEEN ENTERING over time.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Eski plomba yemirilgan va vaqt o'tishi bilan bakteriyalar kirib borgan.
phrasebook.patient_response: So what is the next step?
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Xo'sh, endi navbatdagi qadam nima?
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: So какой следующий шаг?

phrasebook.phrase: I'll use a local anesthetic to numb the area. You shouldn't feel sharp pain.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪl juːz ə ˈləʊkəl ˌænəsˈθetɪk tə nʌm/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Joyni uyushtirish uchun mahalliy anesteziya qilaman. Keskin og'riq bo'lmaydi.
phrasebook.patient_response: That's a relief! I HAD BEEN STRESSING about the procedure all morning.
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Ko'nglim joyiga tushdi! Ertalabdan beri ushbu muolajadan xavotir olib yurgan edim.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Какое облегчение! Я все утро переживал из-за этой процедуры.

phrasebook.phrase: If you HAD COME when the discomfort first started, we could have treated it faster.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɪf juː hæd kʌm wen ðə dɪsˈkʌmfət fɜːst ˈstɑːtɪd/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Diskomfort boshlangan paytda kelganingizda, ancha tezroq davolagan bo'lardik.
phrasebook.patient_response: I understand. If I HAD COME earlier, would the treatment have been simpler?
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Tushundim. Agar vaqtliroq kelganimda, davolash osonroq bo'larmidi?
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Я понимаю. Если бы я пришел раньше, лечение было бы проще?

examples.translation_uz: Tushib ketgan tishning ildiz yuzasiga tegmang va uni qirmang.

examples.translation_ru: Поместите зуб в холодное молоко или физраствор и немедленно доставьте в клинику.
examples.note_ru: Неотложное руководство к действию

common_mistakes.incorrect: You should not touching the tooth root.
common_mistakes.correct: Do not touch the tooth root.
common_mistakes.explanation: Shoshilinch holatda aniq va keskin buyruq: 'Do not + fe'lning 1-shakli'.

common_mistakes.explanation_ru: В экстренной ситуации используется прямой запрет: 'Do not touch'.
common_mistakes.explanation_en: Use the clear, concise imperative 'Do not touch' in emergencies.

grammar.structure_pattern: [Base Verb] + [Object]! | Do not + [Base Verb] + [Object]!
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Shoshilinch tish travmalarida (tish tushib ketganda yoki singanda) bemor yoki ota-onaga tezkor yo'l-yo'riq berishda Buyruq mayli (fe'lning o'zi yoki Do not + fe'l) qo'llaniladi. Signal so'zlar: please, do not, never, always.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: При травме зуба четкие экстренные инструкции даются в повелительном наклонении (глагол без подлежащего или Do not + глагол). Сигнальные слова: please, do not, never, always.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Emergency instructions must be concise and immediate using base imperative forms. Signal words: please, do not, never, always.
