practice.setting: dental clinic
practice.role_play: The student is the DENTIST. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Charlotte Reed
patient_profile.personality_trait: nervous about dental treatment, sensitive to pain

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning, Doctor. I've been suffering from an intense ache in one of my bottom back teeth on the right side. The throbbing had been getting worse all day, and it became completely agonizing last night.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. Please, take a seat. What seems to be the problem?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning, Doctor. I've been suffering from an intense ache in one of my bottom back teeth on the right side. The throbbing had been getting worse all day, and it became completely agonizing last night.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. Had you been experiencing any discomfort before the pain reached that level?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I had been feeling a dull ache for about three days, but I had ignored it because I thought it would fade away.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Had you noticed any swelling or sensitivity prior to last night?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, the gum around the tooth had swollen slightly. I had also noticed that the tooth was extremely sensitive to ice-cold drinks.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Had you taken any painkillers before coming to the clinic?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I had swallowed two tablets during the night, but they had barely dullened the pain.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Had you been chewing hard food or had you injured the tooth recently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I hadn't injured it. But I had been chewing mostly on that side because my left side had been bothering me as well.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. I'm going to examine the area now. Please tell me if you feel any sharp pain.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I can see significant inflammation. It looks as though the infection had been spreading under the surface and has now reached the root.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is it serious? I'm worried you'll have to extract it.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We'll try our best to save it. Had the tooth received any treatment in the past?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. A dentist had placed a filling there several years ago.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That explains it. The old filling had deteriorated, and bacteria had been entering the inner tooth over time.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: So what is the next step?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: First, we'll take an X-ray to check the exact condition. If the nerve is badly affected, you may need a root canal.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I feel much pain during the procedure?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: No, I'll use a local anesthetic to numb the area. You may feel slight pressure, but no sharp pain.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: That's a relief! I had been stressing about the procedure all morning.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That's completely natural. However, you shouldn't delay treatment when severe swelling occurs.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand. If I had come earlier, would the treatment have been simpler?

questions_to_ask_doctor: Is it serious?
So what is the next step?
Will I feel much pain during the procedure?
If I had come earlier, would the treatment have been simpler?

modules.description: Bemor tishini tiklash uchun implant, crown yoki boshqa protez variantlari haqida maslahat so'raydi. Talaba variantlarning afzallik va kamchiliklarini tushuntiradi.

modules.description_ru: Модуль клинического общения: Реставрация и протезирование зубов. Грамматика: Comparatives & Superlatives. Эталонный диалог, 26 терминов, 5 smart-фраз, 1 грамматических тем и симуляция с виртуальным пациентом.
modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Dental Restoration & Prosthetics. Grammar focus: Comparatives & Superlatives. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 26 vocabulary items, 5 smart phrases, 1 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning, Mr. Davis. Looking at your X-rays and recent examination, the root canal treatment on your lower right molar was successful, but the remaining natural tooth structure is heavily compromised. We need to discuss a permanent restorative solution.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you, Doctor. I'm relieved the infection is gone, but I noticed a significant piece of the tooth broke off before the treatment. Is a standard composite filling no longer an option?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, no. Because over 50% of the clinical crown is missing, a simple filling wouldn't withstand normal masticatory forces. I strongly recommend a full-coverage dental crown to restore both its function and structural integrity.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I see. What materials do you offer for crowns, and how do they differ in terms of durability and appearance?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We primarily use Zirconia and Porcelain-Fused-to-Metal (PFM). Zirconia is exceptionally strong, highly biocompatible, and provides a virtually seamless match to your natural tooth shade. PFM is also durable, but over time, a dark metallic line might become visible near the gumline.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes sense. While we are discussing prosthetics, I also have a missing tooth right next to it that was extracted last year. Can we address both issues together?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Absolutely. For the gap, we have two options: a dental bridge or a dental implant. A bridge anchors onto the adjacent healthy teeth, which requires shaving them down. An implant, on the other hand, acts as an artificial root inserted directly into the jawbone, preserving neighboring teeth completely.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Preserving my healthy teeth sounds much better. Is the implant procedure complicated, and how long does osseointegration take?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It's a standard minor surgical procedure. Once placed, osseointegration usually takes about 3 to 4 months to integrate solidly with the bone. In the meantime, we can prepare your molar and fit a Zirconia crown first.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That sounds like a clear plan. Let's proceed with the Zirconia crown for the treated tooth today, and schedule a 3D digital scan for the implant planning next week.

phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Понятно. Какие материалы вы предлагаете и чем они отличаются по долговечности и эстетике?

phrasebook.phrase: Zirconia is exceptionally strong, biocompatible, and provides a seamless match. PFM is durable, but over time, a dark metallic line might become visible near the gumline.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sirkoniy o'ta mustahkam, biologik mos keluvchi va tish rangiga mos tushadi. Metall-keramika ham chidamli, ammo vaqt o'tishi bilan milk chizig'ida metall ko'rinib qolishi mumkin.
phrasebook.patient_response: That makes sense. I also have a missing tooth right next to it. Can we address both issues together?
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Mantiqli. Protezlash haqida gaplashayotgan ekanmiz, o'tgan yili olingan qo'shni tishim ham bor edi. Ikkala muammoni birgalikda hal qilsak bo'ladimi?
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Логично. У меня также отсутствует соседний зуб. Можно ли решить обе проблемы сразу?

phrasebook.phrase: For the gap, we have two options: a dental bridge or a dental implant. A bridge anchors onto adjacent teeth, while an implant acts as an artificial root in the jawbone.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /fə ðə ɡæp wi hæv tuː ˈɒpʃənz.../
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bo'shliq uchun ikkita variant bor: tish ko'prigi yoki dental implantat. Ko'prik yon atrofdagi tishlarga tayanadi, implantat esa jag' suyagiga o'rnatiladigan sun'iy ildizdir.
phrasebook.patient_response: Preserving my healthy teeth sounds much better. Is the implant procedure complicated, and how long does osseointegration take?
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Sog'lom tishlarimni saqlab qolish g'oyasi ma'qulroq. Implantat o'rnatish jarayoni murakkabmi va u suyakka birikishi qancha vaqt oladi?
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Сохранить здоровые зубы предпочтительнее. Сложна ли имплантация и сколько длится оссеоинтеграция?

phrasebook.phrase: It's a standard minor surgical procedure. Osseointegration usually takes about 3 to 4 months. In the meantime, we can fit a Zirconia crown first.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu standart kichik jarrohlik muolajasi. Osseointegratsiya suyak bilan birikishi uchun 3-4 oy vaqt oladi. Ungacha esa birinchi bo'lib Sirkoniy koronkasi o'rnatib turamiz.
phrasebook.patient_response: That sounds like a clear plan. Let's proceed with the Zirconia crown today, and schedule a 3D digital scan for the implant planning next week.
phrasebook.patient_response_uz: Bu juda aniq reja bo'ldi. Keling, bugun Sirkoniy koronkasi tayyorgarligini boshlaymiz va kelasi haftaga implantat uchun 3D skanerlashni belgilaymiz.
phrasebook.patient_response_ru: Звучит как отличный план. Давайте начнем с циркониевой коронки сегодня, а на следующую неделю запланируем 3D-сканирование.

common_mistakes.incorrect: Implants are more better than dentures.
common_mistakes.correct: Implants are much better than dentures.
common_mistakes.explanation: 'Better' so'zi oldidan 'more' qo'yilmaydi; kuchaytirish uchun 'much better' ishlatiladi.
common_mistakes.explanation_uz: 'Better' so'zi oldidan 'more' qo'yilmaydi; kuchaytirish uchun 'much better' ishlatiladi.
common_mistakes.explanation_ru: Сравнительная степень 'better' не сочетается с 'more'. Для усиления используют 'much better'.
common_mistakes.explanation_en: Never combine 'more' with irregular comparatives like 'better'. Use 'much better'.

grammar.structure_pattern: [Option A] + is + more [Adjective] than + [Option B] | [Option] + is the most [Adjective]
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Implant, ko'prik va olinadigan protezlar orasidagi farq, chidamlilik va afzalliklarni solishtirishda 'more + sifat + than' (qiyosiy) hamda 'the most + sifat' (orttirma) darajalari qo'llaniladi. Signal so'zlar: than, the most, much / slightly + comparative, as … as.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Сравнительные формы (more durable than, better than) и превосходная степень (the most natural) помогают пациенту выбрать вид протезирования. Сигнальные слова: than, the most, much / slightly + comparative, as … as.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Comparative and superlative forms objectively contrast dental implants vs bridges vs removable dentures. Signal words: than, the most, much / slightly + comparative, as … as.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning! Welcome to our clinic. What brings you in for a full consultation today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning, Doctor. It's been over a year since my last dental check-up. Recently, I've noticed some mild sensitivity to hot and cold food, and my gums bleed slightly when I brush. I wanted to get a comprehensive evaluation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You made the right decision coming in. A complete check-up is the best way to catch potential issues early. Before we begin the physical examination, do you have any pre-existing medical conditions, allergies, or are you currently taking any medications?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No major medical conditions or allergies, but I do take a daily multivitamin.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Perfect. Let's start with a thorough clinical examination. I'm going to check your teeth, gums, tongue, and the soft tissues in your mouth. I'll also perform an oral cancer screening by gently palpating your jawline and neck area.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Sounds good. Is that standard procedure for a full consultation?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, absolutely. We evaluate not just the teeth, but the overall health of your entire mouth. Now, looking inside... I can see some soft plaque build-up and localized gingival inflammation around your lower incisors, which explains the bleeding. Also, there's a small area of discoloration on your upper right premolar that I want to investigate further.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is it a cavity?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It could be an early-stage carious lesion. Based on my visual examination, we can manage this early on and also schedule a professional dental cleaning to resolve the gum inflammation. We will outline a tailored treatment plan for you right now.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That sounds very clear and structured. Thank you, Doctor!

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: My pleasure! Let's discuss the next steps for your preventive care and get everything scheduled.

grammar.rule_explanation_en: Indirect polite questions create trust and comfort when assessing medical history and dental anxiety. Signal words: Could you tell me…, Do you know…, I wonder….

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning Doctor. I understand you've brought your newborn in because you're concerned about his feeding and skin colour. Could you tell me what has been worrying you?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Good morning, doctor. Yes. He has not been feeding well since yesterday, and his skin looks more yellow than before.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. How old is your baby now?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He is eight days old.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Was he born at full term, or was he premature?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He was born at 39 weeks by vaginal delivery.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Has he had any health problems since birth?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: No major problems. He was doing well until yesterday.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did you first notice that he was becoming yellow?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: I noticed a slight yellow colour on his face about three days ago, but it seems to have become more noticeable over the last two days.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has the yellow colour spread to his chest, abdomen, or legs?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Yes, it has spread down to his chest and stomach.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I understand. How has his feeding changed?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He used to breastfeed every two to three hours, but now he falls asleep very quickly during feeding.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Approximately how long has he been feeding at each breast?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Only about five to ten minutes. Before, he would feed for around fifteen to twenty minutes.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has he been latching on properly?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Not always. Sometimes he seems to have difficulty staying attached.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's important to know. How many wet diapers has he had in the last 24 hours?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: I think about four or five.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: And has he been passing stools normally?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Yes, although his stools have become less frequent since yesterday.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has he had any vomiting, fever, breathing difficulties, or unusual crying?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: No fever or breathing problems. He has been sleepier than usual, though.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has he been difficult to wake for feeds?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Yes. I sometimes have to wake him up, and even then he falls asleep while feeding.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. Has he received any medication or supplements since birth?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: No medication. We have only been breastfeeding him.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has anyone in the family had problems with newborn jaundice or blood disorders?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: His older sister had mild jaundice as a newborn, but it resolved without treatment.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'd like to examine your baby now, including his skin colour, hydration, temperature, breathing, and general condition. I'll also check his weight and the umbilical cord.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Of course, doctor. Is the jaundice dangerous?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Newborn jaundice is quite common, and in many cases it is mild. However, because your baby has become more jaundiced and has been feeding poorly and becoming unusually sleepy, we need to assess him carefully.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Does that mean he may need treatment?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It depends on the examination and, if necessary, his bilirubin level. We shouldn't assume the cause without assessing him properly.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: For now, continue offering breastfeeds regularly and keep track of his wet diapers. If he becomes increasingly difficult to wake, stops feeding, develops a fever, has breathing difficulties, or becomes unusually floppy, seek urgent medical attention.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Thank you, doctor. I'll keep a close eye on him.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're welcome. We'll assess him now and explain the next steps clearly.

grammar.title: Grammar Focus: Present Perfect
grammar.structure_pattern: have/has + past participle
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect o'tmishdagi voqeani hozirgi holat bilan bog'laydi: tajriba, yaqinda bo'lgan voqea yoki hozir muhim bo'lgan natija. Anamnez yig'ishda hozirgacha bo'lgan simptomlar so'raladi: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Hozirgi zamon sifatdoshi (-ing) faol jarayonni ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"), o'tgan zamon sifatdoshi (V3) holat yoki natijani ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately") bildiradi. Ular nisbiy ergash gaplarni qisqartiradi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Причастие настоящего времени (-ing) описывает активный процесс («a spreading infection», «the patient lying in bed»); причастие прошедшего времени (V3) — состояние или результат («an infected wound», «samples taken immediately»). Они сокращают придаточные предложения. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: to ask about events or conditions from birth until now, especially in history-taking. Why it matters clinically: The Present Perfect helps the clinician establish whether a problem has occurred at any point up to the present. Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Grammar Focus: Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: have/has + been + verb-ing
grammar.signal_words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect Continuous o'tmishda boshlanib hozirgacha davom etayotgan (yoki hozirgina to'xtagan va ta'siri sezilayotgan) harakatni bildiradi. Simptom davomiyligi uchun asosiy zamon: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal so'zlar: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается (или только что закончилось и результат заметен). Ключевое время для длительности симптомов: «How long have you been feeling unwell?» — «I have been coughing for five days». Сигнальные слова: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: to emphasize an ongoing or repeated condition/activity and its duration. Signal words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.

examples.sentence: He has not been feeding well since yesterday.
examples.note: The poor feeding started in the past and is still relevant now.

grammar.title: Grammar Focus: Past Simple vs Present Perfect
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were | have / has + V3 | Have/Has + subject + V3?
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Past Simple o'tmishda aniq vaqtda tugagan voqealarni bildiradi: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Vaqt tugagan yoki aniq ko'rsatilgan bo'lsa shu zamon ishlatiladi. Present Perfect o'tmishdagi voqeani hozirgi holat bilan bog'laydi: tajriba, yaqinda bo'lgan voqea yoki hozir muhim bo'lgan natija. Anamnez yig'ishda hozirgacha bo'lgan simptomlar so'raladi: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple описывает завершённые события в определённое время в прошлом: «The pain started yesterday», «When did you take the last dose?». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

examples.sentence: He was born at 39 weeks.
examples.note: Past Simple — Completed event at a definite time.

examples.sentence: I noticed a slight yellow colour three days ago.

Has he received any medication?
examples.note: Present Perfect — Experience up to now.

grammar.title: Grammar Focus: Used to
grammar.structure_pattern: used to + base verb
grammar.signal_words: before, in the past, previously
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "Used to" hozir mavjud bo'lmagan o'tmishdagi odat yoki holatni bildiradi: "I used to smoke twenty cigarettes a day". O'tmishdagi turmush tarzi va avvalgi dorilar haqida so'rashda qulay. Signal so'zlar: before, in the past, previously.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Used to» описывает прошлые привычки или состояния, которых больше нет: «I used to smoke twenty cigarettes a day». Удобно для расспроса о прежнем образе жизни и предыдущих лекарствах. Сигнальные слова: before, in the past, previously.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: to describe a past routine or state that is different now. Contrast: PAST ROUTINE → used to breastfeed / CURRENT CHANGE → now he falls asleep Signal words: before, in the past, previously.

examples.sentence: He used to breastfeed every two to three hours, but now he falls asleep very quickly.

grammar.title: Grammar Focus: Modal Verbs for Advice & Urgency
grammar.structure_pattern: modal (can / could / may / might / must / should / have to) + V1
grammar.signal_words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Modal fe'llar gapga munosabat qo'shadi: ehtimollik (may, might, could), imkoniyat/ruxsat (can, could), maslahat (should, ought to), majburiyat (must, have to) va taqiq (mustn't). Modaldan keyin fe'l doim asosiy shaklda (V1) keladi. Signal so'zlar: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы передают отношение говорящего: возможность (may, might, could), способность/разрешение (can, could), совет (should, ought to), обязанность (must, have to) и запрет (mustn't). После модального глагола всегда стоит начальная форма. Сигнальные слова: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Modal verbs add the speaker's attitude: possibility (may, might, could), ability/permission (can, could), advice (should, ought to), obligation (must, have to) and prohibition (mustn't). The main verb after a modal is always the base form. Signal words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.

examples.sentence: Key forms: should / need to / may / can
We need to assess him carefully." — clinical necessity.
He may need treatment." — possibility, not certainty.
You should seek urgent medical attention." — strong clinical advice.
We can assess his bilirubin level." — clinical possibility/action.

grammar.title: Grammar Focus: First Conditional
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, will + base verb | If + symptom appears
grammar.signal_words: if, unless, as soon as, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: First Conditional real, ehtimoliy kelajakdagi vaziyat va uning natijasini bildiradi. Shifokor ogohlantirish, reja va xavfsizlik ko'rsatmalari uchun ishlatadi: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". "If" dan keyin "will" ishlatilmaydi. Present Simple odatiy, takrorlanuvchi harakatlar, umumiy faktlar va doimiy holatlarni bildiradi. Klinikada odatdagi simptomlar ("The pain usually starts at night"), muntazam dori qabuli va umumiy tibbiy faktlar uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: First Conditional описывает реальную, возможную ситуацию в будущем и её результат. Врач использует его для предупреждений, планов и рекомендаций по безопасности: «If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately». После «if» «will» не ставится. Present Simple описывает привычные, регулярные действия, общие факты и постоянные состояния. В клинике используется для типичных симптомов («The pain usually starts at night»), регулярного приёма лекарств и общих медицинских фактов. Сигнальные слова: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: to give safety-netting advice about a possible future condition. In clinical instructions, the imperative can replace "will": "If X happens, seek medical attention." Signal words: if, unless, as soon as, when.

grammar.title: Grammar Focus: Indirect — Polite Clinical Questions
grammar.structure_pattern: Auxiliary (do/does/did/have/is/are/can) + subject + V? | Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + V?
grammar.signal_words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Yes/No savollar yordamchi fe'l bilan boshlanadi ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-savollar so'roq so'zi bilan ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Ochiq savollar hikoyani, yopiq savollar aniq detallarni yig'adi. Signal so'zlar: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Общие вопросы начинаются со вспомогательного глагола («Do you have any allergies?», «Have you had a fever?»); специальные — с вопросительного слова («How long have you had the pain?», «Where exactly does it hurt?»). Открытые вопросы собирают историю, закрытые — уточняют детали. Сигнальные слова: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Yes/No questions start with an auxiliary ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-questions add a question word ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Open questions gather the story, closed questions confirm details. Signal words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.

Clinical value: Indirect questions sound less abrupt and encourage the parent to provide more information.

medical_condition.exact_diagnosis: Newborn Care & Common Problems in Newborns
medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning, doctor. Yes. He has not been feeding well since yesterday, and his skin looks more yellow than before.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning Doctor. I understand you've brought your newborn in because you're concerned about his feeding and skin colour. Could you tell me what has been worrying you?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning, doctor. Yes. He has not been feeding well since yesterday, and his skin looks more yellow than before.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. How old is your baby now?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He is eight days old.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Was he born at full term, or was he premature?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He was born at 39 weeks by vaginal delivery.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. Has he had any health problems since birth?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No major problems. He was doing well until yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When did you first notice that he was becoming yellow?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I noticed a slight yellow colour on his face about three days ago, but it seems to have become more noticeable over the last two days.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has the yellow colour spread to his chest, abdomen, or legs?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, it has spread down to his chest and stomach.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I understand. How has his feeding changed?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He used to breastfeed every two to three hours, but now he falls asleep very quickly during feeding.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Approximately how long has he been feeding at each breast?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Only about five to ten minutes. Before, he would feed for around fifteen to twenty minutes.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has he been latching on properly?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Not always. Sometimes he seems to have difficulty staying attached.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That's important to know. How many wet diapers has he had in the last 24 hours?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I think about four or five.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: And has he been passing stools normally?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, although his stools have become less frequent since yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has he had any vomiting, fever, breathing difficulties, or unusual crying?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No fever or breathing problems. He has been sleepier than usual, though.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has he been difficult to wake for feeds?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I sometimes have to wake him up, and even then he falls asleep while feeding.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. Has he received any medication or supplements since birth?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No medication. We have only been breastfeeding him.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has anyone in the family had problems with newborn jaundice or blood disorders?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: His older sister had mild jaundice as a newborn, but it resolved without treatment.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. I'd like to examine your baby now, including his skin colour, hydration, temperature, breathing, and general condition. I'll also check his weight and the umbilical cor…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Of course, doctor. Is the jaundice dangerous?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. I notice from the triage notes that your child has been prioritized today due to severe respiratory distress accompanied by a high-grade fever. Could you walk me through what happened overnight and what has been concerning you the most?

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Hello, doctor. He's had a mild cough for three days, but around midnight his temperature suddenly spiked to 39.5°C. Shortly after that, his breathing changed completely—it became extremely fast and shallow. Every time he exhales, he makes this faint grunting noise, and he refuses to take any fluids.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. The combination of rapid breathing, grunting, and fluid refusal requires immediate evaluation. Let's place him on the examination table right now so we can assess his vital signs. (Attaches pulse oximeter) As we wait for the reading, when did you first notice his nostril flaring and the skin pulling in around his ribs?

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Early this morning, around 6:00 AM. I noticed his chest sinking in deeply under his ribs every time he takes a breath. Is he struggling to get enough air? Why is his body reacting like that?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What you're seeing is intercostal retractions and nasal flaring. They occur when a child has to use extra respiratory muscles to force air into inflamed lungs. His pulse oximetry reading shows an oxygen saturation of 89% on room air, which confirms severe hypoxemia. Sister, please set up a pediatric nasal cannula with 2 liters of oxygen right away.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Oh no, 89%? Is that dangerously low? Will the oxygen help him relax his breathing?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Normal saturation should be above 95%, so 89% indicates his lungs aren't transferring enough oxygen into his bloodstream. Supplemental oxygen will relieve that strain quickly. Now, let me listen to his lungs with my stethoscope while he calms down. (Auscultates anterior and posterior chest) Take slow breaths for me, little one... On the right side, particularly over the lower lobe, I can hear distinct localized crepitations and bronchial breath sounds.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Crepitations? Does that mean there is fluid or infection built up inside his lungs? Is this acute pneumonia?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, crepitations sound like faint crackling noises and indicate fluid or inflammatory exudate inside the alveoli—the tiny air sacs in the lungs. Combined with his fever, low oxygen saturation, and prolonged capillary refill time, these findings strongly suggest severe acute bacterial pneumonia.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: I'm so worried. Does this mean he needs to be admitted to the hospital immediately? Will he be okay?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: He does need to be admitted so we can monitor his respiratory status closely. We shouldn't make assumptions about the exact bacterial cause without further diagnostic work, but we need to act swiftly. Our immediate plan is to secure an intravenous line to draw blood for a complete blood count and blood cultures, start empiric IV antibiotic therapy, and provide IV fluid hydration since he hasn't been drinking.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: That makes sense. Will he also need a chest X-ray to see how bad the infection is?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Once his oxygen levels stabilize on the cannula, we'll perform a portable chest X-ray right here in the bay to check the extent of the pulmonary consolidation. How many wet diapers has he had in the last 24 hours, by the way?

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Only two since yesterday evening, and they were barely wet. That's why I was worried he was getting dehydrated on top of everything else.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You were right to bring him in. Decreased urine output is a clear indicator of mild to moderate dehydration in toddlers. The IV fluids will correct that balance while the antibiotics target the infection. We will re-evaluate his respiratory rate, work of breathing, and oxygen levels every 15 minutes.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Thank you so much, doctor. Knowing the exact plan makes me feel much more reassured. Please do whatever is necessary to get his breathing back to normal.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're very welcome. Our team is right here with you, and we'll explain every single step as we proceed with his treatment.

grammar.title: Present Perfect vs. Past Simple
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3 | Have/Has + subject + V3? | Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Tibbiy anamnez olayotganda pasient yoki ota-ona ko'pincha hozirgi ahvolga ta'sir qilayotgan o'tmish voqealari haqida gapiradi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect — Hozirgi lahgagacha davom etayotgan yoki hozirgi holatga bevosita aloqador o'tmishdagi harakatlar uchun. / Для действий в прошлом, которые продолжаются до настоящего момента или непосредственно связаны с ним. Past Simple — Aniq ko'rsatilgan va tugallangan vaqt (aniq soat, sana) haqida gapirilganda. / Для действий, завершившихся в конкретное указанное время в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Present & Past Participles as Adjectives
grammar.structure_pattern: V-ing + noun (active) | V3 + noun (passive) | noun + V-ing / V3 phrase
grammar.signal_words: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Tibbiy ingliz tilida B2 darajasida -ing (Present Participle) va -ed (Past Participle) sifatlaridan keng foydalaniladi. Jarayon yoki simptomning o'zi faol holatda ekanini bildiradi. Yomonlashayotgan / kuchayayotgan yo'tal Ingrayotgan / g'illayotgan tovush Burun teshiklarining kerilishi (nafas zo'riqishi belgisi) Muayyan ta'sir yoki patologiya natijasidagi holat. Lokalizatsiyalashgan (bir joyga to'plangan) qirsillashlar Ustuvorlik berilgan (saralashda oldinga surilgan) bemor Signal so'zlar: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Кряхтящий / стонущий звук Passive State / Result (-ed) — Passiv holat / Пассивное состояние (Результат): Приоритетный пациент (при триаже) Сигнальные слова: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present participles (-ing) describe an active process ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"); past participles (V3) describe a state or result ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately"). They shorten relative clauses. Signal words: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.

examples.sentence: Prolonged capillary refill time
examples.translation_ru: Замедленный симптом "белого пятна" (капиллярный ответ)

grammar.title: Complex Sentence Structures & Relative Clauses
grammar.structure_pattern: noun + who / which / that / whose / where + clause
grammar.signal_words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Aytilmoqchi bo'lgan klinik fikrni aniq va tushunarli qilish uchun nisbiy olmoshlar (where, which, that) orqali murakkab gaplar tuziladi. Talabalar yodlab olishi va muloqotda ishlatishi kerak bo'lgan tayyor klinik birikmalar: Bemor ... simptomi bilan keldi / murojaat qildi Signal so'zlar: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Определительные придаточные добавляют информацию о существительном: «the patient who collapsed at work», «a test which measures kidney function». Ограничительные (defining) пишутся без запятых и уточняют существительное; распространительные (non-defining) выделяются запятыми. Сигнальные слова: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Relative clauses add information about a noun: "the patient who collapsed at work", "a test which measures kidney function". Defining clauses have no commas and identify the noun; non-defining clauses add extra information between commas. Signal words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Could you elaborate on when these symptoms first started and how his condition has progressed over the past 24 hours?

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Hello, doctor. It started yesterday morning with sudden vomiting after breakfast. By last night, he developed frequent, watery diarrhea—at least six or seven episodes. He can't seem to keep any fluids down, and he's becoming increasingly lethargic.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. Frequent vomiting combined with profuse diarrhea can rapidly compromise a toddler's hydration status. Let's place him on the examination table right now to evaluate his vital signs and check for clinical signs of dehydration. When did he last pass urine?

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: That's another thing that's worrying me—his diaper has been completely dry since midnight, which is over ten hours now. Normally, I'd have changed him two or three times by now.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: A lack of urine output for ten hours is a significant clinical indicator of dehydration. Let's assess his mucous membranes, skin turgor, and capillary refill time. (Examines the child) As you can see, his lips and tongue are noticeably dry, his eyes appear slightly sunken, and when I pinch the skin on his abdomen, it recoils slowly rather than snapping back instantly.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Oh dear, does that mean he's severely dehydrated? Is he going to need an intravenous drip immediately?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: He is exhibiting clinical signs of moderate dehydration. Before we resort to invasive procedures like setting up an intravenous line, the standard protocol for moderate acute gastroenteritis is to attempt Oral Rehydration Therapy, or ORT, using a balanced electrolyte solution.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: I tried giving him plain water and diluted apple juice at home, but he threw them right back up. Will the rehydration solution be any different?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's a common issue. Plain water or sugary juices lack the correct sodium-to-glucose ratio needed for intestinal absorption, and giving large volumes at once triggers the gag reflex, inducing further vomiting. With ORT, we administer small, controlled volumes—about 5 to 10 milliliters every 5 minutes using a syringe or spoon.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: I understand. But what if he continues to vomit even with small sips of the solution?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If he tolerates the oral rehydration solution over the next hour, we can gradually increase the volume and avoid hospitalization. However, if he experiences persistent vomiting, marked lethargy, or signs of worsening shock, we will immediately secure IV access to administer an intravenous isotonic saline bolus.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: That makes total sense. Should I also give him any anti-diarrheal or anti-emetic medications to stop the loose stools?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We generally advise against routine over-the-counter anti-diarrheal medications in young children, as they can slow down bowel motility and cause serious adverse effects. However, depending on his nausea, we may consider a single oral dose of ondansetron to control the vomiting and facilitate oral rehydration.

dialogue.label: Parent
dialogue.text: Thank you, doctor. Knowing we have a clear step-by-step plan makes me feel much more confident. Let's start the oral rehydration trial right away.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Excellent. Our nursing staff will guide you through the first few doses, and we will closely monitor his heart rate, capillary refill time, and urine output over the next two hours.

phrasebook.phrase: He's becoming increasingly lethargic.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он становится всё более вялым.

phrasebook.phrase: When did he last pass urine?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Когда он последний раз мочился?

phrasebook.phrase: Let's evaluate his vital signs.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Давайте оценим его жизненно важные показатели.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to check for clinical signs of dehydration.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wi niːd tə tʃek fə ˈklɪnɪkəl saɪnz əv ˌdiːhaɪˈdreɪʃən/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо проверить клинические признаки обезвоживания.

phrasebook.phrase: Let's assess his mucous membranes.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Оценим состояние слизистых оболочек.

phrasebook.phrase: Let's check his skin turgor.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Проверим тургор кожи.

phrasebook.phrase: Let's assess his capillary refill time.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Оценим время капиллярного наполнения.

phrasebook.phrase: His lips and tongue are noticeably dry.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /hɪz lɪps ənd tʌŋ ɑː ˈnəʊtɪsəbli draɪ/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning lablari va tili sezilarli darajada quruq.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Его губы и язык заметно сухие.

phrasebook.phrase: His eyes appear slightly sunken.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Его глаза выглядят слегка запавшими.

phrasebook.phrase: The skin recoils slowly.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Кожа расправляется медленно.

phrasebook.phrase: He is exhibiting clinical signs of moderate dehydration.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /hi ɪz ɪɡˈzɪbɪtɪŋ ˈklɪnɪkəl saɪnz əv ˈmɒdərət ˌdiːhaɪˈdreɪʃən/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Unda o'rtacha darajadagi suvsizlanishning klinik belgilari mavjud.
phrasebook.translation_ru: У него имеются клинические признаки умеренного обезвоживания.

phrasebook.phrase: Before we resort to invasive procedures...
phrasebook.translation_ru: Прежде чем прибегать к инвазивным процедурам...

phrasebook.phrase: The standard protocol is to attempt oral rehydration therapy.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə ˈstændəd ˈprəʊtəkɒl ɪz tə əˈtempt ˈɔːrəl ˌriːhaɪˈdreɪʃən ˈθerəpi/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Standart yondashuv — og'iz orqali regidratatsiya terapiyasini boshlash.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Стандартный подход — попытаться провести оральную регидратационную терапию.

phrasebook.phrase: We administer small, controlled volumes.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz kichik, nazorat qilinadigan hajmlarda beramiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы вводим небольшие контролируемые объёмы.

phrasebook.phrase: If he tolerates the solution...
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar u eritmani yaxshi qabul qilsa...
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если он будет хорошо переносить раствор...

phrasebook.phrase: We can gradually increase the volume.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы можем постепенно увеличить объём.

phrasebook.phrase: If vomiting persists, we will secure IV access.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɪf ˈvɒmɪtɪŋ pəˈsɪsts wi wɪl sɪˈkjʊə ˌaɪˈviː ˈækses/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar qusish davom etsa, vena ichiga kirish yo'lini ochamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если рвота сохраняется, мы обеспечим внутривенный доступ.

phrasebook.phrase: We generally advise against routine use of anti-diarrheal medications.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wi ˈdʒenərəli ədˈvaɪz əˈɡenst ruːˈtiːn juːs əv ˌænti ˌdaɪəˈrɪəl medɪˈkeɪʃənz/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Odatda diareyaga qarshi dorilarni muntazam qo'llashni tavsiya etmaymiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы обычно не рекомендуем рутинное применение противодиарейных препаратов.

phrasebook.phrase: They can cause serious adverse effects.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ular jiddiy nojo'ya ta'sirlarga olib kelishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Они могут вызвать серьёзные побочные эффекты.

phrasebook.phrase: We may consider a single oral dose of ondansetron.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wi meɪ kənˈsɪdə ə ˈsɪŋɡəl ˈɔːrəl dəʊs əv ɒnˈdænsətrɒn/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ondansetronning bir martalik og'iz orqali dozasini ko'rib chiqishimiz mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы можем рассмотреть однократную пероральную дозу ондансетрона.

phrasebook.phrase: This may help control the vomiting.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu qusishni nazorat qilishga yordam berishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это может помочь контролировать рвоту.

grammar.title: Present Perfect
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + past participle | The patient's condition has + past participle + time period.
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ya'ni: suvsizlanish belgilari paydo bo'lgan va bu hozirgi holatga ta'sir qilmoqda. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Причастие настоящего времени (-ing) описывает активный процесс («a spreading infection», «the patient lying in bed»); причастие прошедшего времени (V3) — состояние или результат («an infected wound», «samples taken immediately»). Они сокращают придаточные предложения. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Present participles (-ing) describe an active process ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"); past participles (V3) describe a state or result ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately"). They shorten relative clauses. Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

examples.sentence: He has developed frequent diarrhea.
He has become increasingly lethargic.
His condition has worsened over the past 24 hours.
He has developed signs of dehydration.
His condition has progressed over the past 24 hours.
He has vomited several times.
He has developed watery diarrhea.
His urine output has decreased.
His condition has deteriorated.
He has not been able to keep fluids down.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + been + verb-ing
grammar.signal_words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect Continuous o'tmishda boshlanib hozirgacha davom etayotgan (yoki hozirgina to'xtagan va ta'siri sezilayotgan) harakatni bildiradi. Simptom davomiyligi uchun asosiy zamon: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal so'zlar: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается (или только что закончилось и результат заметен). Ключевое время для длительности симптомов: «How long have you been feeling unwell?» — «I have been coughing for five days». Сигнальные слова: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Focus → duration/ongoing activity Signal words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.

examples.sentence: This tense is particularly useful when an action started in the past and is continuing or has been happening repeatedly until now.
He has been vomiting since yesterday morning.
He has been having frequent episodes of diarrhea.
He has been becoming increasingly lethargic.
He has vomited six times.
He has been vomiting since yesterday.
How long has he been vomiting?
How long has he been having diarrhea?
How long has he been unable to keep fluids down?

grammar.title: Past Simple vs Present Perfect
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were | have / has + V3 | Have/Has + subject + V3?
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu mavzu tibbiy anamnez olishda juda muhim. When did...? → aniq vaqt Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple описывает завершённые события в определённое время в прошлом: «The pain started yesterday», «When did you take the last dose?». Используется, когда время закончилось или названо. Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

examples.sentence: He vomited after breakfast yesterday.
He developed diarrhea last night.
His diaper was dry at midnight.
examples.translation_uz: Hozirgacha davom etayotgan yoki hozirgi holat bilan bog'liq vaziyat:

examples.sentence: He has vomited several times.
He has developed signs of dehydration.
He hasn't passed urine for ten hours.
When did the vomiting start?
How many times has he vomited?
examples.translation_uz: Bu ikki savolning farqi talabalar uchun juda muhim:

examples.sentence: How many times has...?

grammar.title: Present Continuous for Changing Conditions
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + verb-ing | is/are + becoming/getting + adjective
grammar.signal_words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Continuous ayni paytda bo'layotgan yoki vaqtinchalik, o'zgarayotgan holatni bildiradi: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". Shifokorning hozirgi rejasini aytishda ham ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Continuous описывает действие в момент речи или временную, меняющуюся ситуацию: «His condition is getting worse», «I am going to examine you now». Также используется для ближайших действий врача. Сигнальные слова: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. Signal words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.

examples.sentence: Patient's condition changes dynamically.
He is becoming increasingly lethargic.
His condition is getting worse.
His hydration status is deteriorating.
He is becoming lethargic.
He is getting weaker.
The child is becoming increasingly dehydrated.
His urine output is gradually decreasing.
His hydration status can rapidly deteriorate.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs in Clinical English
grammar.structure_pattern: modal (can / could / may / might / must / should / have to) + V1
grammar.signal_words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Modal fe'llar gapga munosabat qo'shadi: ehtimollik (may, might, could), imkoniyat/ruxsat (can, could), maslahat (should, ought to), majburiyat (must, have to) va taqiq (mustn't). Modaldan keyin fe'l doim asosiy shaklda (V1) keladi. Signal so'zlar: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы передают отношение говорящего: возможность (may, might, could), способность/разрешение (can, could), совет (should, ought to), обязанность (must, have to) и запрет (mustn't). После модального глагола всегда стоит начальная форма. Сигнальные слова: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Modal verbs add the speaker's attitude: possibility (may, might, could), ability/permission (can, could), advice (should, ought to), obligation (must, have to) and prohibition (mustn't). The main verb after a modal is always the base form. Signal words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.

examples.sentence: Modal verbs help doctors talk about possibility, advice, necessity and clinical decisions.
Frequent diarrhea can cause dehydration.
Large volumes can trigger further vomiting.
We may consider ondansetron.
He may need intravenous fluids.
He might require hospitalization.
The vomiting might be caused by gastroenteritis.
You should give him small amounts of fluid frequently.
Parents should monitor urine output.
Severe dehydration must be treated promptly.
We must monitor his vital signs closely.

grammar.title: First Conditional — Clinical Management Plans
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, will + verb
grammar.signal_words: if, unless, as soon as, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: First Conditional real, ehtimoliy kelajakdagi vaziyat va uning natijasini bildiradi. Shifokor ogohlantirish, reja va xavfsizlik ko'rsatmalari uchun ishlatadi: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". "If" dan keyin "will" ishlatilmaydi. Present Simple odatiy, takrorlanuvchi harakatlar, umumiy faktlar va doimiy holatlarni bildiradi. Klinikada odatdagi simptomlar ("The pain usually starts at night"), muntazam dori qabuli va umumiy tibbiy faktlar uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: First Conditional описывает реальную, возможную ситуацию в будущем и её результат. Врач использует его для предупреждений, планов и рекомендаций по безопасности: «If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately». После «if» «will» не ставится. Present Simple описывает привычные, регулярные действия, общие факты и постоянные состояния. В клинике используется для типичных симптомов («The pain usually starts at night»), регулярного приёма лекарств и общих медицинских фактов. Сигнальные слова: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Condition → clinical action Signal words: if, unless, as soon as, when.

examples.sentence: This is one of the most important grammar structures in medical communication.
If he tolerates the solution, we will gradually increase the volume.
If vomiting persists, we will secure IV access.
examples.translation_uz: Agar qusish davom etsa, vena ichiga kirish yo'lini ochamiz.
examples.translation_ru: Если рвота сохраняется, мы обеспечим внутривенный доступ.

examples.sentence: If he develops signs of shock, we will start intravenous fluids.
If + condition, we will + clinical action.
Students should memorize this as a clinical communication pattern.

grammar.title: Zero Conditional — General Medical Facts
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, Present Simple
grammar.signal_words: if, when, whenever
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Zero Conditional umumiy haqiqat va tibbiy faktlarni bildiradi: "If children lose too much fluid, they become dehydrated". Ikkala qismda ham Present Simple ishlatiladi. Present Simple odatiy, takrorlanuvchi harakatlar, umumiy faktlar va doimiy holatlarni bildiradi. Klinikada odatdagi simptomlar ("The pain usually starts at night"), muntazam dori qabuli va umumiy tibbiy faktlar uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: if, when, whenever.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Zero Conditional выражает общие истины и медицинские факты: «If children lose too much fluid, they become dehydrated». В обеих частях используется Present Simple. Present Simple описывает привычные, регулярные действия, общие факты и постоянные состояния. В клинике используется для типичных симптомов («The pain usually starts at night»), регулярного приёма лекарств и общих медицинских фактов. Сигнальные слова: if, when, whenever.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Used for facts, mechanisms and general clinical principles. Signal words: if, when, whenever.

examples.sentence: If children lose too much fluid, they become dehydrated.
If a child drinks large amounts quickly, it can trigger vomiting.
If the body loses electrolytes, fluid balance is affected.
If he continues to vomit, we will start IV fluids.
Specific patient + future clinical action.

grammar.title: Passive Voice in Medical English
grammar.structure_pattern: be + past participle
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Passive Voice harakatni kim bajarayotganidan ko'ra harakatning o'zi yoki bemor muhim bo'lganda ishlatiladi — tahlillar, muolajalar va davolash rejasi uchun odatiy: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Hozirgi zamon sifatdoshi (-ing) faol jarayonni ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"), o'tgan zamon sifatdoshi (V3) holat yoki natijani ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately") bildiradi. Ular nisbiy ergash gaplarni qisqartiradi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». Причастие настоящего времени (-ing) описывает активный процесс («a spreading infection», «the patient lying in bed»); причастие прошедшего времени (V3) — состояние или результат («an infected wound», «samples taken immediately»). Они сокращают придаточные предложения. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Present participles (-ing) describe an active process ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"); past participles (V3) describe a state or result ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately"). They shorten relative clauses. Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

examples.sentence: Medical English frequently uses passive structures because the procedure or treatment is more important than the person performing it.
He is monitored closely.
IV access will be secured.
An isotonic saline bolus will be administered.
We will administer an isotonic saline bolus.
The nursing staff will monitor his urine output.
His urine output will be monitored.
Vital signs are monitored.
IV access is secured.
Fluids are administered intravenously.
The patient is closely monitored.
The treatment plan is explained to the parents.

grammar.title: Gerund After Prepositions
grammar.structure_pattern: Preposition + verb-ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund (V-ing) ot vazifasida keladi va avoid, stop, keep, recommend fe'llari hamda predloglardan keyin ishlatiladi ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitiv (to + V1) need, want, decide, advise someone dan keyin keladi va maqsadni bildiradi ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Герундий (V-ing) выступает как существительное после глаголов avoid, stop, keep, recommend и предлогов («Avoid eating before the test»). Инфинитив (to + V1) стоит после need, want, decide, advise someone и выражает цель («We need to run some tests», «in order to rule out appendicitis»). Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

examples.sentence: In medical English, verbs often come after prepositions in the -ing form.
Before resorting to invasive procedures...
After receiving oral rehydration...
Without causing further vomiting...

grammar.title: Cause and Effect
grammar.structure_pattern: because / since / as + clause | due to / because of + noun | although / while + clause | therefore / as a result + clause
grammar.signal_words: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bog'lovchilar klinik faktlarni mantiqan bog'laydi: sabab (because, since, due to), natija (therefore, as a result, so), qarama-qarshilik (although, however, while) va vaqt (when, while, as soon as). Ular qisqa gaplarni aniq klinik tushuntirishga aylantiradi. Signal so'zlar: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Связующие слова логически соединяют клинические факты: причина (because, since, due to), следствие (therefore, as a result, so), противопоставление (although, however, while) и время (when, while, as soon as). Они превращают короткие фразы в ясное клиническое объяснение. Сигнальные слова: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Connectors link clinical facts logically: cause (because, since, due to), result (therefore, as a result, so), contrast (although, however, while) and time (when, while, as soon as). They turn short statements into clear clinical explanations. Signal words: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.

examples.sentence: Clinical English needs clear ways to explain why something happens.
He is dehydrated because he has been losing fluids through vomiting and diarrhea.
His dehydration is due to excessive fluid loss.
Profuse diarrhea can cause significant fluid loss, leading to dehydration.
Persistent vomiting may cause fluid depletion, resulting in dehydration.
Large volumes of fluid can trigger further vomiting.
Severe fluid loss can compromise hydration status.

grammar.title: Clinical Question Formation
grammar.structure_pattern: Auxiliary (do/does/did/have/is/are/can) + subject + V? | Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + V?
grammar.signal_words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Yes/No savollar yordamchi fe'l bilan boshlanadi ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-savollar so'roq so'zi bilan ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Ochiq savollar hikoyani, yopiq savollar aniq detallarni yig'adi. Signal so'zlar: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Общие вопросы начинаются со вспомогательного глагола («Do you have any allergies?», «Have you had a fever?»); специальные — с вопросительного слова («How long have you had the pain?», «Where exactly does it hurt?»). Открытые вопросы собирают историю, закрытые — уточняют детали. Сигнальные слова: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Yes/No questions start with an auxiliary ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-questions add a question word ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Open questions gather the story, closed questions confirm details. Signal words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.

examples.sentence: Students should be able to transform statements into professional clinical questions.
He last passed urine ten hours ago.
When did he last pass urine?
examples.translation_ru: Когда он последний раз мочился?

examples.sentence: He has been vomiting since yesterday.
How long has he been vomiting?
He has had six episodes of diarrhea.
How many episodes of diarrhea has he had?
His condition has worsened over the last 24 hours.

grammar.title: Key Grammar Patterns to Memorize
grammar.structure_pattern: The patient will be + past participle.
grammar.signal_words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "Will" hozir qabul qilingan qaror, va'da, bashorat va bemorni tinchlantirishni ifodalaydi: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Hozirgi zamon sifatdoshi (-ing) faol jarayonni ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"), o'tgan zamon sifatdoshi (V3) holat yoki natijani ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately") bildiradi. Ular nisbiy ergash gaplarni qisqartiradi. Signal so'zlar: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Will» выражает решение, принятое в момент речи, обещание, прогноз и успокоение пациента: «I will give you something for the pain», «The swelling will go down in a few days». Причастие настоящего времени (-ing) описывает активный процесс («a spreading infection», «the patient lying in bed»); причастие прошедшего времени (V3) — состояние или результат («an infected wound», «samples taken immediately»). Они сокращают придаточные предложения. Сигнальные слова: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Present participles (-ing) describe an active process ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"); past participles (V3) describe a state or result ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately"). They shorten relative clauses. Signal words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please have a seat. I understand you've brought your son in because of a fever and a skin rash. Could you tell me what concerns you most?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Good morning, doctor. Yes. He has a high temperature, and a red rash appeared on his chest and back. The rash seems to be spreading to his arms and legs as well.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. Is the rash itchy, painful, or uncomfortable in any way?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He says the rash is quite itchy. He keeps scratching these areas on his arms. That is what worries me because some of the spots look irritated.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I understand. Does he have a cough, a runny nose, or a sore throat?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He has a sore throat and a runny nose. He also complains of a headache.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Let me examine him. I'm going to look at the rash closely. These spots are small and pink, while those on his legs are slightly larger. I also notice a few areas where the skin looks irritated.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Doctor, could this be an infection?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, an infectious illness is one possibility. We need to consider several causes, including a viral infection and a bacterial infection. Each type of rash has certain characteristics that can help us identify its cause.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Does this rash look like measles or chickenpox?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: This rash does not have the typical appearance of chickenpox. With chickenpox, we usually expect a mixture of spots, fluid-filled blisters, and crusted lesions. The lesions often appear at different stages.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: What about measles?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Measles can cause a widespread rash together with fever and respiratory symptoms. However, the distribution and appearance of the rash are important. We also need to ask about each child's vaccination history and possible exposure to infection.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He has received every routine childhood vaccination according to his schedule.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That is useful information. Has anyone in his school or family had a similar illness recently?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Yes. A boy in his class had a fever and rash last week. The school informed parents about an infectious illness.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That information is important. We should also check the inside of his mouth and the lymph nodes in his neck. Please let me know if any of these areas are painful.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He says this side of his neck feels slightly tender.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. I can feel a mildly enlarged lymph node on the right side. I'll examine the rest of his skin as well.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Does he need an antibiotic?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. An antibiotic is appropriate only for a bacterial infection that requires antibiotic treatment. If the illness is viral, antibiotics will not treat the underlying cause.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: I understand. What should we do now?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: First, we'll carry out a careful examination and assess his symptoms. We may also arrange a throat swab if clinically indicated. In the meantime, give him plenty of fluids and avoid scratching the affected areas.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Thank you, doctor. I feel much less worried now.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Please monitor the rash closely. If any new or unusual symptoms appear, contact us promptly. We'll explain each step of his management clearly.
