phrasebook.phrase: Could you tell me what worries you most?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /kʊd juː tel miː wɒt ˈwʌriz juː məʊst/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizni eng ko'p nima tashvishlantirayotganini aytib bera olasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Можете рассказать, что вас больше всего беспокоит?

phrasebook.phrase: I understand you have concerns about his speech and overall development.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tushunishimcha, siz uning nutqi va umumiy rivojlanishidan xavotirdasiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я понимаю, что вас беспокоят его речь и общее развитие.

phrasebook.phrase: I'd like to ask you a few questions about his developmental milestones.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men sizdan uning rivojlanish bosqichlari haqida bir nechta savol so'ramoqchiman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я хотел(а) бы задать вам несколько вопросов об этапах его развития.

phrasebook.phrase: Does he respond when you call his name?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он реагирует, когда вы называете его по имени?

phrasebook.phrase: Does he point to objects that he wants?
phrasebook.translation_uz: U xohlagan narsalarini barmog'i bilan ko'rsatadimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он показывает пальцем на предметы, которые хочет?

phrasebook.phrase: How would you describe his communication skills?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning muloqot ko'nikmalarini qanday ta'riflagan bo'lardingiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Как бы вы описали его коммуникативные навыки?

phrasebook.phrase: He uses gestures to communicate.
phrasebook.translation_uz: U muloqot qilish uchun imo-ishoralardan foydalanadi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он использует жесты для общения.

phrasebook.phrase: He makes eye contact with his parents.
phrasebook.translation_uz: U ota-onasi bilan ko'z orqali aloqa qiladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он поддерживает зрительный контакт с родителями.

phrasebook.phrase: I'd like to assess his receptive and expressive language.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men uning tushunish va ifodali nutqini baholamoqchiman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я хотел(а) бы оценить его понимание речи и экспрессивную речь.

phrasebook.phrase: Receptive language refers to his ability to understand what other people say.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tushunish nutqi bolaning boshqalar aytgan gaplarni tushunish qobiliyatini anglatadi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Понимание речи означает способность ребёнка понимать речь других людей.

phrasebook.phrase: I'd also like to ask about his motor development.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shuningdek, uning motor rivojlanishi haqida ham so'ramoqchiman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я также хотел(а) бы спросить о его моторном развитии.

phrasebook.phrase: Is he able to walk, run, and climb independently?
phrasebook.translation_uz: U mustaqil yura, yugura va tirmasha oladimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он может самостоятельно ходить, бегать и лазать?

phrasebook.phrase: Does he need any assistance with movement?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нужна ли ему помощь при движении?

phrasebook.phrase: We should assess his motor skills as well.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning harakat ko'nikmalarini ham baholashimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам также необходимо оценить его двигательные навыки.

phrasebook.phrase: Have you noticed any loss of skills that he previously had?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ilgari egallagan ko'nikmalaridan birortasi yo'qolganini sezganmisiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы замечали утрату каких-либо навыков, которыми он раньше обладал?

phrasebook.phrase: We would pay particular attention to significant muscle weakness.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz sezilarli mushak zaifligiga alohida e'tibor qaratamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы уделяем особое внимание выраженной мышечной слабости.

phrasebook.phrase: Abnormal movements may require further neurological assessment.
phrasebook.translation_uz: G'ayritabiiy harakatlar qo'shimcha nevrologik baholashni talab qilishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Патологические движения могут потребовать дополнительного неврологического обследования.

phrasebook.phrase: We would also be concerned about seizures or problems with coordination.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shuningdek, tutqanoq xurujlari yoki koordinatsiya bilan bog'liq muammolar ham bizni xavotirga soladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нас также могут беспокоить судорожные приступы или проблемы с координацией.

phrasebook.phrase: I'd also like to ask about his hearing.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shuningdek, uning eshitish qobiliyati haqida so'ramoqchiman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я также хотел(а) бы спросить о его слухе.

phrasebook.phrase: Has he had a hearing assessment?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он проходил обследование слуха?

phrasebook.phrase: A hearing assessment would be useful.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Обследование слуха было бы полезным.

phrasebook.phrase: Hearing difficulties can affect speech development.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Eshitishdagi qiyinchiliklar nutq rivojlanishiga ta'sir qilishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нарушения слуха могут влиять на развитие речи.

phrasebook.phrase: We can consider a neurological assessment if necessary.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Zarur bo'lsa, nevrologik baholashni ko'rib chiqishimiz mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: При необходимости мы можем рассмотреть неврологическое обследование.

phrasebook.phrase: A developmental specialist may also be helpful.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Rivojlanish bo'yicha mutaxassis ham foydali bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Специалист по развитию также может быть полезен.

phrasebook.phrase: We can arrange a specialist assessment if we identify any concerning signs.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar xavotirli belgilarni aniqlasak, mutaxassis ko'rigini tashkil qilishimiz mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если мы выявим тревожные признаки, мы можем организовать обследование специалистом.

phrasebook.phrase: Further neurological assessment may be required.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Qo'shimcha nevrologik baholash talab qilinishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Может потребоваться дополнительное неврологическое обследование.

phrasebook.phrase: Spend time communicating with him during everyday activities.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Kundalik mashg'ulotlar davomida u bilan muloqot qilishga vaqt ajrating.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Уделяйте время общению с ним во время повседневных занятий.

phrasebook.phrase: Use simple language when communicating with him.
phrasebook.translation_uz: U bilan muloqotda sodda tildan foydalaning.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Используйте простой язык при общении с ним.

phrasebook.phrase: Give him opportunities to express his needs.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Unga o'z ehtiyojlarini ifodalash uchun imkoniyat bering.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Давайте ему возможность выражать свои потребности.

phrasebook.phrase: Respond to the gestures and sounds that he uses.
phrasebook.translation_uz: U ishlatadigan imo-ishoralar va tovushlarga javob bering.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Реагируйте на жесты и звуки, которые он использует.

phrasebook.phrase: A speech delay does not necessarily indicate a neurological disorder.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Nutqning kechikishi har doim ham nevrologik buzilishni anglatmaydi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Задержка речи не обязательно указывает на неврологическое нарушение.

phrasebook.phrase: Children develop at different rates.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Дети развиваются с разной скоростью.

phrasebook.phrase: It is too early to make that conclusion.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bunday xulosaga kelish uchun hali juda erta.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пока слишком рано делать такой вывод.

phrasebook.phrase: What matters now is identifying the areas that need support.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hozir eng muhimi, yordam talab qiladigan sohalarni aniqlashdir.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сейчас важно определить области, которые нуждаются в поддержке.

grammar.title: Relative Clauses
grammar.structure_pattern: person + who + verb | thing + which + clause
grammar.signal_words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Relative Clause — gapdagi shaxs, narsa, joy yoki egalik haqida qo'shimcha ma'lumot beruvchi ergash gap. 2. WHO — odamlar uchun 4. THAT — odamlar yoki narsalar uchun Signal so'zlar: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Relative Clause — это придаточная часть предложения, которая даёт дополнительную информацию о человеке, предмете, месте или принадлежности. Сигнальные слова: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Relative clause is a part of a sentence that gives additional information about a person, thing, place, or possession. WHO → mainly people THAT → people + things Signal words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.

examples.sentence: WHO is used for people.
A developmental specialist is a doctor who assesses several areas of child development.
examples.translation_uz: Rivojlanish bo'yicha mutaxassis — bolaning rivojlanishining bir nechta sohalarini baholaydigan shifokor.
examples.translation_ru: Специалист по развитию — это врач, который оценивает несколько областей развития ребёнка.

examples.sentence: Children who have significant muscle weakness may require further neurological assessment.
examples.translation_uz: Sezilarli mushak zaifligi bo'lgan bolalar qo'shimcha nevrologik baholashga muhtoj bo'lishi mumkin.
examples.translation_ru: Детям, у которых имеется выраженная мышечная слабость, может потребоваться дополнительное неврологическое обследование.

examples.sentence: a specialist who...
WHICH is used for things, conditions, symptoms, tests, or concepts.
His speech delay, which concerns his mother, requires further assessment.
examples.translation_uz: Uning onasini xavotirga solayotgan nutq kechikishi qo'shimcha baholashni talab qiladi.
examples.translation_ru: Задержка речи, которая беспокоит его мать, требует дальнейшей оценки.

examples.sentence: A hearing assessment, which can identify hearing difficulties, may be useful.
examples.translation_uz: Eshitishni baholash, eshitishdagi qiyinchiliklarni aniqlashi mumkin va foydali bo'lishi mumkin.
examples.translation_ru: Оценка слуха, которая может выявить нарушения слуха, может быть полезной.

examples.translation_ru: Ребёнку, которому требуется дополнительная поддержка, необходимо регулярное обследование.

examples.sentence: The assessment that we recommend can provide useful information.
examples.translation_uz: Biz tavsiya qilayotgan baholash foydali ma'lumot berishi mumkin.
examples.translation_ru: Обследование, которое мы рекомендуем, может предоставить полезную информацию.

grammar.title: WHO vs Which vs That
grammar.structure_pattern: person + whose + noun + verb | place + where + clause
grammar.signal_words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Relative Clauses ikki gapni bitta gapga birlashtirish imkonini beradi. 7. WHOSE — egalikni bildiradi Odam yoki narsaning kimga tegishli ekanini bildiradi. 8. WHERE — joylar uchun Signal so'zlar: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Определительные придаточные добавляют информацию о существительном: «the patient who collapsed at work», «a test which measures kidney function». Ограничительные (defining) пишутся без запятых и уточняют существительное; распространительные (non-defining) выделяются запятыми. Сигнальные слова: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Relative clauses add information about a noun: "the patient who collapsed at work", "a test which measures kidney function". Defining clauses have no commas and identify the noun; non-defining clauses add extra information between commas. Signal words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.

grammar.title: Non-Defining Relative Clause
grammar.structure_pattern: noun + who / which / that / whose / where + clause
grammar.signal_words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu turdagi Relative Clause asosiy shaxs yoki narsa haqida qo'shimcha ma'lumot beradi. Bunday gaplarda ko'pincha vergul ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Определительные придаточные добавляют информацию о существительном: «the patient who collapsed at work», «a test which measures kidney function». Ограничительные (defining) пишутся без запятых и уточняют существительное; распространительные (non-defining) выделяются запятыми. Сигнальные слова: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Relative clauses add information about a noun: "the patient who collapsed at work", "a test which measures kidney function". Defining clauses have no commas and identify the noun; non-defining clauses add extra information between commas. Signal words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.

practice.setting: paediatric outpatient clinic / children's emergency department (the doctor talks to the parent)
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the MOTHER of the sick child (speak about your child in the third person).

patient_profile.name: Emma Hale
patient_profile.personality_trait: worried parent, wants clear explanations

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning, doctor. I'm mainly worried about his speech. He is almost two years old, but he uses only a few words. He also sometimes seems less responsive than other children his age.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: A speech delay does not necessarily indicate a neurological disorder. There are several factors that can affect language development. We need to assess the child as a whole rather than focus on one developmental area.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. Please have a seat. I understand you've brought your son because you have some concerns about his speech and overall development. Could you tell me what worries you…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning, doctor. I'm mainly worried about his speech. He is almost two years old, but he uses only a few words. He also sometimes seems less responsive than other children his age.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. Let me ask you a few questions about his developmental milestones. Does he respond when you call his name?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, he usually looks at me when I call him. He also understands simple instructions, which is reassuring.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That is useful information. What about his communication skills? Does he point to objects that he wants?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. He points to things that he wants and uses gestures to communicate. He also makes eye contact with us.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good. Those are important social-communication skills. I'd also like to ask about his motor development. Is he able to walk, run, and climb independently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. He walks and runs without assistance. He can also climb onto a chair and come down safely.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Excellent. Have you noticed any loss of skills that he previously had?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I haven't noticed any loss of skills. My main concern is his speech, which seems delayed compared with other children.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Understood. We should assess the areas of development that are relevant to his age. I'd like to evaluate his receptive language, which refers to his ability to understand what oth…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Could this mean that he has a neurological problem?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: A speech delay does not necessarily indicate a neurological disorder. There are several factors that can affect language development. We need to assess the child as a whole rather…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What kind of neurological signs would concern you?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We would pay particular attention to children who have significant muscle weakness, abnormal movements, seizures, problems with coordination, or a loss of developmental skills. Th…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He has never had a seizure, and I haven't noticed any unusual movements.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That is reassuring. I'd also like to ask about his hearing, because hearing difficulties can affect speech development. Has he had a hearing assessment?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, he hasn't. We haven't arranged one yet.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: In that case, a hearing assessment would be useful. A child who has difficulty hearing certain sounds may have problems developing clear speech.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Should we see a neurologist as well?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We can consider a neurological assessment if we identify any signs that require specialist review. A developmental specialist, who can assess several areas of child development, m…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What should we do at home while we are waiting for the assessment?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Spend time communicating with him during everyday activities. Use simple language, give him opportunities to express his needs, and respond to the gestures and sounds that he uses.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Should we be worried that he will never speak normally?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It is too early to make that conclusion. Children develop at different rates, and the reasons for speech delay can vary considerably. What matters now is identifying the areas tha…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you, doctor. I feel much less worried now.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please have a seat. All right you've brought your daughter because she has been experiencing wheezing and breathing difficulty. Could you tell me what concerns you most?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Good morning, doctor. She started coughing during the night, and her breathing became noticeably faster. She also made a whistling sound when she breathed, especially while lying down.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. Has the breathing difficulty developed gradually, or has it become severe quite rapidly?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: It developed gradually at first, but it became much worse during the early morning. She also seemed unusually tired because she was struggling to breathe comfortably.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to examine her carefully. I'll check her respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and chest movements while she is breathing.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Doctor, could this be asthma?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Asthma is one possibility, although we need to assess her carefully before making a diagnosis. Wheezing can occur for several reasons, including asthma, viral infections, and allergic reactions.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: She sometimes develops a runny nose and itchy eyes when she is around cats. Could that be related?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's useful to know. It could be relevant because exposure to an allergen may trigger respiratory symptoms in some children. We need to ask about possible triggers and examine her respiratory system carefully.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: She has never had an episode this severe before. What should I do if her breathing becomes worse?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If her breathing becomes increasingly difficult, you should seek urgent medical attention. You should also watch for signs such as difficulty speaking, marked chest retractions, bluish lips, or severe weakness.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: I see. She seems to be breathing a little more comfortably now.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. That is reassuring. Her oxygen saturation is acceptable at the moment, although I can still hear mild expiratory wheezing. We'll continue to monitor her closely while we assess the possible cause.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Will she need an inhaler?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: She may need a bronchodilator if the clinical assessment supports bronchospasm. We'll administer the appropriate treatment carefully and then reassess her breathing.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: How quickly should we expect an improvement?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If the medication is effective, her breathing should gradually become easier. We'll reassess her respiratory rate and oxygen saturation after treatment rather than relying only on how she feels.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Could an allergy be responsible for this episode?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It is possible, especially if her symptoms appear after exposure to a specific trigger. However, we should not assume that an allergy is the only cause because viral respiratory infections can also produce wheezing.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: She often becomes congested when the weather changes, although she usually remains active.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's an important detail. We'll consider both allergic and respiratory causes while evaluating her symptoms. If we identify a consistent trigger, we can discuss ways to reduce her exposure to it.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: What can we do at home to prevent another episode?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Keep a record of situations in which her symptoms become worse, particularly if they occur after contact with animals, dust, smoke, or strong fragrances. Avoiding known triggers can reduce the risk of further episodes.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Should she avoid physical activity?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. Although exercise can trigger symptoms in some children with asthma, regular physical activity is generally important. The key is to manage the condition appropriately and follow the treatment plan recommended for her.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Thank you, doctor. I feel much calmer now.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're welcome. We'll continue to observe her carefully. If her breathing deteriorates rapidly, or if she develops severe respiratory distress, she needs urgent medical assessment.

phrasebook.phrase: Could you tell me what concerns you most?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizni eng ko'p nima tashvishlantirayotganini aytib bera olasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Можете рассказать, что вас больше всего беспокоит?

phrasebook.phrase: Has the breathing difficulty developed gradually, or has it become severe quite rapidly?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Nafas olishdagi qiyinchilik asta-sekin rivojlandimi yoki juda tez og'irlashdimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Затруднённое дыхание развивалось постепенно или довольно быстро стало тяжёлым?

phrasebook.phrase: Does she make a whistling sound when she breathes?
phrasebook.translation_uz: U nafas olayotganda hushtaksimon tovush chiqadimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: У неё появляется свистящий звук при дыхании?

phrasebook.phrase: Could you describe when the symptoms become worse?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Belgilar qachon kuchayishini tasvirlab bera olasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Можете описать, когда симптомы усиливаются?

phrasebook.phrase: Has she been exposed to any possible allergens?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Она подвергалась воздействию возможных аллергенов?

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to examine her carefully.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я внимательно её осмотрю.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll check her respiratory rate and oxygen saturation.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men uning nafas olish tezligi va kislorod saturatsiyasini tekshiraman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я проверю частоту дыхания и сатурацию кислорода.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll also assess her chest movements while she is breathing.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Nafas olayotganda ko'krak qafasi harakatlarini ham baholayman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я также оценю движения грудной клетки во время дыхания.

phrasebook.phrase: I can still hear mild expiratory wheezing.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men hali ham yengil ekspirator xirillashni eshityapman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я всё ещё слышу лёгкие экспираторные хрипы.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll continue to monitor her closely.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz uni yaqindan kuzatishda davom etamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы продолжим внимательно за ней наблюдать.

phrasebook.phrase: Asthma is one possibility.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Астма является одной из возможных причин.

phrasebook.phrase: Wheezing can occur for several reasons.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Xirillash bir nechta sabablarga ko'ra yuzaga kelishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Свистящее дыхание может возникать по нескольким причинам.

phrasebook.phrase: Exposure to an allergen may trigger respiratory symptoms.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Allergen ta'siri nafas olish bilan bog'liq belgilarni qo'zg'atishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Воздействие аллергена может вызвать респираторные симптомы.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to consider both allergic and respiratory causes.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz allergik va respirator sabablarning ikkalasini ham ko'rib chiqishimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо учитывать как аллергические, так и респираторные причины.

phrasebook.phrase: We should not assume that an allergy is the only cause.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Allergiya yagona sabab deb taxmin qilmasligimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не следует предполагать, что аллергия является единственной причиной.

phrasebook.phrase: She may need a bronchodilator if the clinical assessment supports bronchospasm.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar klinik baholash bronxospazmni ko'rsatsa, unga bronxlarni kengaytiruvchi dori kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если клиническая оценка подтвердит бронхоспазм, ей может потребоваться бронходилататор.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll administer the appropriate treatment carefully.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz tegishli davolashni ehtiyotkorlik bilan amalga oshiramiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы осторожно проведём соответствующее лечение.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll reassess her breathing after treatment.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Davolashdan keyin uning nafas olishini qayta baholaymiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: После лечения мы повторно оценим её дыхание.

phrasebook.phrase: Her breathing should gradually become easier.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning nafas olishi asta-sekin yengillashishi kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Её дыхание должно постепенно улучшаться.

phrasebook.phrase: You should seek urgent medical attention if her breathing becomes increasingly difficult.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar uning nafas olishi tobora qiyinlashsa, shoshilinch tibbiy yordamga murojaat qilishingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если её дыхание становится всё более затруднённым, необходимо срочно обратиться за медицинской помощью.

phrasebook.phrase: Watch for signs of severe respiratory distress.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Следите за признаками выраженной дыхательной недостаточности.

phrasebook.phrase: Look out for marked chest retractions or bluish lips.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ko'krak qafasining yaqqol ichkariga tortilishi yoki lablarning ko'karishiga e'tibor bering.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Обращайте внимание на выраженное втяжение грудной клетки или синюшность губ.

phrasebook.phrase: Difficulty speaking can be a warning sign.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Gapirishdagi qiyinchilik xavfli belgi bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Затруднение речи может быть тревожным признаком.

phrasebook.phrase: Rapid deterioration requires urgent medical assessment.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tez yomonlashuv shoshilinch tibbiy baholashni talab qiladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Быстрое ухудшение состояния требует срочного медицинского обследования.

phrasebook.phrase: Keep a record of situations in which her symptoms become worse.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning belgilari kuchayadigan holatlarni qayd qilib boring.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Ведите записи о ситуациях, при которых её симптомы усиливаются.

phrasebook.phrase: Pay particular attention to possible triggers.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ehtimoliy qo'zg'atuvchi omillarga alohida e'tibor bering.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Обращайте особое внимание на возможные триггеры.

phrasebook.phrase: Avoid known triggers whenever possible.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ma'lum bo'lgan qo'zg'atuvchi omillardan imkon qadar saqlaning.
phrasebook.translation_ru: По возможности избегайте известных триггеров.

phrasebook.phrase: Contact with animals may trigger her symptoms.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hayvonlar bilan aloqa uning belgilarini qo'zg'atishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Контакт с животными может провоцировать её симптомы.

phrasebook.phrase: We can discuss ways to reduce her exposure to triggers.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz uning triggerlar ta'siriga uchrashini kamaytirish usullarini muhokama qilishimiz mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы можем обсудить способы уменьшения воздействия триггеров.

grammar.title: Adverbs
grammar.structure_pattern: adjective + -ly (rapidly, gradually, carefully) | verb + adverb | adverb + adjective
grammar.signal_words: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Adverb — fe'l, sifat yoki boshqa ravishni qanday, qachon, qanchalik yoki qanday tarzda bajarilishini bildiradi. Ravish harakatning qanday, qanchalik yoki qanday tarzda bajarilishini bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Наречие описывает, как, насколько или каким образом происходит действие. Сигнальные слова: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Adverbs describe how, when or to what degree something happens: "Her breathing became worse rapidly", "The condition is gradually improving". Adverbs of degree (slightly, significantly, increasingly) make clinical descriptions precise. Signal words: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.

grammar.title: Rapidly
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Rapidly harakat yoki holatning juda tez sodir bo'lishini bildiradi.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rapidly указывает на то, что действие или изменение происходит очень быстро.

examples.sentence: Her breathing became worse rapidly.
examples.translation_ru: Её дыхание быстро ухудшилось.

examples.sentence: If his breathing deteriorates rapidly, he needs urgent medical assessment.
examples.translation_uz: Agar uning nafas olishi tez yomonlashsa, unga shoshilinch tibbiy baholash kerak.
examples.translation_ru: Если его дыхание быстро ухудшается, ему требуется срочное медицинское обследование.

grammar.title: Gradually
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gradually o'zgarish yoki rivojlanishning asta-sekin sodir bo'lishini bildiradi.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Gradually показывает, что изменение или процесс происходит постепенно.

examples.sentence: Her breathing became gradually easier after treatment.
examples.translation_uz: Davolashdan keyin uning nafas olishi asta-sekin yengillashdi.
examples.translation_ru: После лечения её дыхание постепенно стало легче.

examples.sentence: The symptoms may improve gradually.
examples.translation_ru: Симптомы могут постепенно улучшаться.

grammar.title: Carefully
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Carefully harakatning ehtiyotkorlik bilan yoki sinchiklab bajarilishini bildiradi.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Carefully показывает, что действие выполняется внимательно или осторожно.

examples.sentence: I'm going to examine her carefully.
examples.translation_ru: Я внимательно её осмотрю.

examples.sentence: We need to assess her respiratory system carefully.
examples.translation_uz: Biz uning nafas olish tizimini sinchiklab baholashimiz kerak.
examples.translation_ru: Нам необходимо тщательно оценить её дыхательную систему.

examples.sentence: The medication should be administered carefully.
examples.translation_ru: Препарат следует вводить осторожно.

examples.sentence: Her symptoms improved gradually.

examples.translation_ru: Её дыхание стало заметно более частым.

examples.sentence: She became increasingly tired.
examples.translation_ru: Она становилась всё более уставшей.

grammar.title: Adverbial Clauses
grammar.structure_pattern: adjective + -ly (rapidly, gradually, carefully) | verb + adverb | adverb + adjective | because / since / as + clause | due to / because of + noun | although / while + clause | therefore / as a result + clause
grammar.signal_words: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Adverbial clause — asosiy gapdagi harakatning sababi, qarama-qarshiligi, vaqti, sharti yoki boshqa holatini tushuntiruvchi qo'shimcha gap. Signal so'zlar: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Adverbial clause — придаточное обстоятельственное предложение, которое объясняет причину, противопоставление, время, условие или обстоятельство действия в главном предложении. because — chunki — потому что while — paytida / bir vaqtda — пока, в то время как Сигнальные слова: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Adverbs describe how, when or to what degree something happens: "Her breathing became worse rapidly", "The condition is gradually improving". Adverbs of degree (slightly, significantly, increasingly) make clinical descriptions precise. Connectors link clinical facts logically: cause (because, since, due to), result (therefore, as a result, so), contrast (although, however, while) and time (when, while, as soon as). They turn short statements into clear clinical explanations. Signal words: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.

grammar.title: Because
grammar.structure_pattern: Main clause + because + reason
grammar.signal_words: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Because biror hodisaning sababini ko'rsatadi. Signal so'zlar: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Because используется для объяснения причины действия или состояния. Сигнальные слова: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Connectors link clinical facts logically: cause (because, since, due to), result (therefore, as a result, so), contrast (although, however, while) and time (when, while, as soon as). They turn short statements into clear clinical explanations. Signal words: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.

examples.sentence: She seemed unusually tired because she was struggling to breathe comfortably.
examples.translation_uz: U odatdagidan ko'ra ancha charchagandek ko'rindi, chunki u bemalol nafas olishga qiynalayotgan edi.
examples.translation_ru: Она казалась необычно уставшей, потому что ей было трудно нормально дышать.

examples.sentence: Exposure to an allergen may trigger respiratory symptoms because some children are sensitive to specific triggers.
examples.translation_uz: Allergen ta'siri nafas olish bilan bog'liq belgilarni qo'zg'atishi mumkin, chunki ayrim bolalar ma'lum triggerlarga sezgir bo'ladi.
examples.translation_ru: Воздействие аллергена может вызвать респираторные симптомы, потому что некоторые дети чувствительны к определённым триггерам.

grammar.title: Because of + Noun
grammar.structure_pattern: because + subject + verb | because of + noun
grammar.signal_words: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Because dan keyin to'liq gap keladi. Because of dan keyin esa ot yoki ot birikmasi keladi. Signal so'zlar: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Связующие слова логически соединяют клинические факты: причина (because, since, due to), следствие (therefore, as a result, so), противопоставление (although, however, while) и время (when, while, as soon as). Они превращают короткие фразы в ясное клиническое объяснение. Сигнальные слова: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.

They turn short statements into clear clinical explanations. Signal words: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.

examples.sentence: She was tired because she was struggling to breathe.
examples.translation_uz: U nafas olishga qiynalayotgani sababli charchagan edi.

examples.sentence: She was tired because of breathing difficulty.
examples.translation_uz: U nafas olishdagi qiyinchilik sababli charchagan edi.

grammar.title: Although — Garchi
grammar.structure_pattern: because / since / as + clause | due to / because of + noun | although / while + clause | therefore / as a result + clause
grammar.signal_words: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Although qarama-qarshi yoki kutilmagan holatni ko'rsatadi. Signal so'zlar: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Although используется, когда необходимо показать контраст или неожиданное обстоятельство. Сигнальные слова: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Connectors link clinical facts logically: cause (because, since, due to), result (therefore, as a result, so), contrast (although, however, while) and time (when, while, as soon as). They turn short statements into clear clinical explanations. Signal words: because, due to, therefore, as a result, although, while, so that.

examples.sentence: Although + clause, main clause.
Although exercise can trigger symptoms in some children, regular physical activity is generally important.
examples.translation_uz: Garchi jismoniy mashqlar ayrim bolalarda simptomlarni qo'zg'atishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, muntazam jismoniy faollik odatda muhim.
examples.translation_ru: Хотя физическая нагрузка может вызывать симптомы у некоторых детей, регулярная физическая активность в целом важна.

examples.sentence: Although her oxygen saturation is acceptable, we need to monitor her closely.
examples.translation_uz: Garchi uning kislorod saturatsiyasi qoniqarli bo'lsa-da, uni yaqindan kuzatishimiz kerak.
examples.translation_ru: Хотя сатурация кислорода у неё удовлетворительная, нам необходимо внимательно за ней наблюдать.

grammar.title: While

examples.translation_uz: Mumkin bo'lgan sababni baholayotganimizda, uni yaqindan kuzatishda davom etamiz.
examples.translation_ru: Пока мы оцениваем возможную причину, мы продолжим внимательно наблюдать за ней.

examples.sentence: I'll check her oxygen saturation while I examine her chest.

examples.translation_ru: Пока я осматриваю её грудную клетку, я проверю сатурацию кислорода.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: She often becomes congested when the weather changes, although she usually remains active.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Not necessarily. Although exercise can trigger symptoms in some children with asthma, regular physical activity is generally important. The key is to manage the condition appropri…

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Common Pediatric Emergencies. Grammar focus: Reported Speech — The mother said that…, The doctor explained that…. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 50 vocabulary items, 30 smart phrases, 10 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.
modules.grammar_focus: Reported Speech — The mother said that…, The doctor explained that…

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please bring the child over here. I understand that he requires urgent assessment. Could you tell me what happened?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Good morning, doctor. He suddenly became very weak at home. He also complained of severe abdominal pain and then became unusually sleepy.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. When did you first become concerned about his condition?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: About an hour ago. He said that his stomach hurt badly, and then he became less responsive. I called an ambulance immediately.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You did the right thing. What did the emergency team tell you on the way here?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: The paramedic said that his blood pressure was low and that his pulse was unusually fast. She also said that he needed urgent medical assessment.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Nurse, could you check his vital signs again and tell me the results?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: His heart rate is 138 beats per minute, and his blood pressure is below the expected range for his age. His oxygen saturation is acceptable at the moment.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Please continue monitoring him closely. The nurse reported that his heart rate was significantly elevated, so we need to assess the possible cause without delay.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Doctor, could this be something serious?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, it could indicate a significant acute problem, although we need further assessment before we determine the cause. The important thing is that he is receiving urgent care now.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Before we came here, he told me that he felt dizzy and that he could not stand properly.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That is important information. You said that he could not stand properly. Did he lose consciousness at any point?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: No, he did not lose consciousness, but he became very drowsy and seemed confused.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. The mother reported that the child had become drowsy and confused, but she did not report any loss of consciousness.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Doctor, he also has diabetes. Could that be related to his condition?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, it could be relevant. What was his blood glucose level when you checked it?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: His father checked it at home and said that the glucose level was very low.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Nurse, please check his blood glucose immediately.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: His blood glucose is 2.4 mmol/L.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That is significantly low. The nurse has confirmed that his blood glucose is below the normal range. We need to treat the hypoglycaemia promptly.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Is he going to be all right?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We are taking immediate steps to stabilize him. I cannot predict the outcome yet, but we are monitoring him closely and responding to his condition.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: What are you going to do now?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I'll explain each step clearly. First, we need to correct his low blood glucose. We will also monitor his airway, breathing, circulation, neurological status, and vital signs.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: The paramedic told me that his condition could become worse very quickly.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: The paramedic was right to emphasize that. In an acute pediatric emergency, a child's condition can deteriorate rapidly, so continuous monitoring is essential.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Doctor, his blood glucose is improving after treatment, and he is becoming more responsive.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. The nurse reports that his blood glucose is improving and that his level of consciousness is also improving.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He is opening his eyes now and responding to me.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That is reassuring. We will continue observation and repeat the necessary assessments. I also want to identify why his blood glucose became so low.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: His father said that he did not eat much today because he had no appetite.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That information may be relevant. The father reported that the child had eaten very little, which could have contributed to the low blood glucose, especially given his diabetes.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: What should we do after he becomes stable?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Once his condition is stable, we will review his medication, food intake, blood glucose monitoring, and recent symptoms. We will also explain the warning signs that require immediate medical attention.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Thank you, doctor. I feel much calmer now.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're welcome. You acted quickly, and that was important. We will continue to monitor him closely and explain any further findings to you.

phrasebook.phrase: Could you tell me what happened?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Можете рассказать, что произошло?

phrasebook.phrase: When did you become concerned about his condition?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Когда вы начали беспокоиться о его состоянии?

phrasebook.phrase: The mother reported that the child had become unusually sleepy.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ona bolaning odatdagidan ko'ra juda uyquchan bo'lib qolganini ma'lum qildi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мать сообщила, что ребёнок стал необычно сонливым.

phrasebook.phrase: The father reported that the child had eaten very little.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ota bolaning juda kam ovqatlanganini ma'lum qildi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Отец сообщил, что ребёнок очень мало ел.

phrasebook.phrase: Did he lose consciousness at any point?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он терял сознание в какой-либо момент?

phrasebook.phrase: I'll check his vital signs immediately.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men uning hayotiy ko'rsatkichlarini darhol tekshiraman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я немедленно проверю его жизненные показатели.

phrasebook.phrase: Please check his blood glucose immediately.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Iltimos, uning qondagi glyukoza darajasini darhol tekshiring.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пожалуйста, немедленно проверьте уровень глюкозы в его крови.

phrasebook.phrase: His heart rate is significantly elevated.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning yurak urish tezligi sezilarli darajada oshgan.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Частота его сердечных сокращений значительно повышена.

phrasebook.phrase: His blood pressure is below the expected range for his age.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning qon bosimi yoshi uchun kutiladigan me'yordan past.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Его артериальное давление ниже ожидаемого для его возраста.

phrasebook.phrase: His oxygen saturation is acceptable at the moment.
phrasebook.translation_ru: В данный момент его сатурация кислорода удовлетворительная.

phrasebook.phrase: The paramedic said that his blood pressure was low.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Feldsher uning qon bosimi past ekanini aytdi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Фельдшер сказал, что у него низкое артериальное давление.

phrasebook.phrase: The paramedic reported that his pulse was unusually fast.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Feldsher uning pulsi odatdagidan tez ekanini ma'lum qildi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Фельдшер сообщил, что его пульс был необычно частым.

phrasebook.phrase: The nurse reported that his heart rate was significantly elevated.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hamshira uning yurak urish tezligi sezilarli darajada oshganini ma'lum qildi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Медсестра сообщила, что частота его сердечных сокращений была значительно повышена.

phrasebook.phrase: The doctor explained that urgent treatment was necessary.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Врач объяснил, что необходимо срочное лечение.

phrasebook.phrase: The nurse confirmed that his blood glucose was improving.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hamshira uning qondagi glyukoza darajasi yaxshilanayotganini tasdiqladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Медсестра подтвердила, что уровень глюкозы в его крови улучшался.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to assess him without delay.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо обследовать его без промедления.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to stabilize him first.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сначала нам необходимо стабилизировать его состояние.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to treat the hypoglycaemia promptly.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо своевременно лечить гипогликемию.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll monitor his airway, breathing, and circulation.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz uning nafas yo'llari, nafas olishi va qon aylanishini kuzatamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем контролировать его дыхательные пути, дыхание и кровообращение.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll continue to monitor him closely.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz uni yaqindan kuzatishda davom etamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы продолжим внимательно наблюдать за ним.

phrasebook.phrase: This could indicate a significant acute problem.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu jiddiy o'tkir muammoni ko'rsatishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это может указывать на серьёзную острую проблему.

phrasebook.phrase: We need further assessment before determining the cause.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sababini aniqlashdan oldin qo'shimcha baholash kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо дополнительное обследование, прежде чем определить причину.

phrasebook.phrase: We are taking immediate steps to stabilize him.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz uning holatini barqarorlashtirish uchun darhol choralar ko'ryapmiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы принимаем немедленные меры для стабилизации его состояния.

phrasebook.phrase: I cannot predict the outcome yet.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пока я не могу предсказать исход.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll explain any further findings to you.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Keyingi aniqlangan ma'lumotlarning barchasini sizga tushuntiramiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы объясним вам все дальнейшие результаты обследования.

phrasebook.phrase: You did the right thing by calling an ambulance immediately.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tez yordamni darhol chaqirganingiz to'g'ri bo'lgan.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы правильно сделали, что сразу вызвали скорую помощь.

phrasebook.phrase: He is receiving urgent care now.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hozir unga shoshilinch tibbiy yordam ko'rsatilmoqda.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сейчас он получает неотложную медицинскую помощь.

phrasebook.phrase: We are monitoring him closely.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы внимательно наблюдаем за ним.

phrasebook.phrase: That is reassuring.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это обнадёживает.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll keep you informed about his condition.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning holati haqida sizni xabardor qilib boramiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем информировать вас о его состоянии.

grammar.title: Say → Said
grammar.structure_pattern: The mother said that + information | The father said that + information | The nurse said that + information | The paramedic said that + information
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Reported Speech'da say ko'pincha o'tgan shaklda said bo'ladi.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Reported Speech'da say ko'pincha o'tgan shaklda said bo'ladi.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Structure: The mother said that + information | The father said that + information | The nurse said that + information | The paramedic said that + information.

examples.sentence: The mother said, "He feels dizzy.
The mother said that he felt dizzy.
examples.translation_ru: Мать сказала, что у него кружится голова.

grammar.title: Tell → Told
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + told + person + that + sentence
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Tell odatda kimga aytilganini ko'rsatishni talab qiladi. 5. SAY va TELL farqi
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Tell odatda kimga aytilganini ko'rsatishni talab qiladi. 5. SAY va TELL farqi
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Structure: Subject + told + person + that + sentence.

grammar.title: Direct Speech → Reported Speech
grammar.structure_pattern: said (that) + clause with tense shifted back | told + object + (that) … | asked + if / wh-word …
grammar.signal_words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Eng muhim o'zgarishlardan biri — gapning shakli o'zgaradi. Signal so'zlar: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Косвенная речь передаёт чужие слова без цитирования: «My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction». Времена обычно сдвигаются назад (is → was, has → had, will → would); вопросы передаются через «if» или вопросительное слово с прямым порядком слов. Сигнальные слова: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: 1. "is" → "was" 2. "are" → "were" 3. "can" → "could" Signal words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.

grammar.title: "will" → "would"
grammar.structure_pattern: said + that + sentence
grammar.signal_words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: 9. Pronouns — olmoshlarning o'zgarishi Reported Speech'da I, my, we, our kabi olmoshlar vaziyatga qarab o'zgaradi. 10. "THAT" — bog'lovchisi Reported Speech'da that juda ko'p ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Will» выражает решение, принятое в момент речи, обещание, прогноз и успокоение пациента: «I will give you something for the pain», «The swelling will go down in a few days». Сигнальные слова: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.

Сигнальные слова: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Reported Speech relays what someone said without quoting: "My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction". Tenses usually shift back (is → was, has → had, will → would); questions use "if" or a wh-word with statement word order. Signal words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.

practice.setting: paediatric outpatient clinic / children's emergency department (the doctor talks to the parent)
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the MOTHER of the sick child (speak about your child in the third person).

patient_profile.name: Lucy Ward
patient_profile.personality_trait: worried parent, wants clear explanations

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning, doctor. He suddenly became very weak at home. He also complained of severe abdominal pain and then became unusually sleepy.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: Yes, it could indicate a significant acute problem, although we need further assessment before we determine the cause. The important thing is that he is receiving urgent care now.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. Please bring the child over here. I understand that he requires urgent assessment. Could you tell me what happened?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning, doctor. He suddenly became very weak at home. He also complained of severe abdominal pain and then became unusually sleepy.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. When did you first become concerned about his condition?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: About an hour ago. He said that his stomach hurt badly, and then he became less responsive. I called an ambulance immediately.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You did the right thing. What did the emergency team tell you on the way here?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: The paramedic said that his blood pressure was low and that his pulse was unusually fast. She also said that he needed urgent medical assessment.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. Nurse, could you check his vital signs again and tell me the results?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: His heart rate is 138 beats per minute, and his blood pressure is below the expected range for his age. His oxygen saturation is acceptable at the moment.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Please continue monitoring him closely. The nurse reported that his heart rate was significantly elevated, so we need to assess the possible cause without delay.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Doctor, could this be something serious?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes, it could indicate a significant acute problem, although we need further assessment before we determine the cause. The important thing is that he is receiving urgent care now.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Before we came here, he told me that he felt dizzy and that he could not stand properly.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That is important information. You said that he could not stand properly. Did he lose consciousness at any point?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, he did not lose consciousness, but he became very drowsy and seemed confused.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. The mother reported that the child had become drowsy and confused, but she did not report any loss of consciousness.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Doctor, he also has diabetes. Could that be related to his condition?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes, it could be relevant. What was his blood glucose level when you checked it?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: His father checked it at home and said that the glucose level was very low.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Nurse, please check his blood glucose immediately.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: His blood glucose is 2.4 mmol/L.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That is significantly low. The nurse has confirmed that his blood glucose is below the normal range. We need to treat the hypoglycaemia promptly.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is he going to be all right?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We are taking immediate steps to stabilize him. I cannot predict the outcome yet, but we are monitoring him closely and responding to his condition.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What are you going to do now?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I'll explain each step clearly. First, we need to correct his low blood glucose. We will also monitor his airway, breathing, circulation, neurological status, and vital signs.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: The paramedic told me that his condition could become worse very quickly.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: The paramedic was right to emphasize that. In an acute pediatric emergency, a child's condition can deteriorate rapidly, so continuous monitoring is essential.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Doctor, his blood glucose is improving after treatment, and he is becoming more responsive.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good. The nurse reports that his blood glucose is improving and that his level of consciousness is also improving.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He is opening his eyes now and responding to me.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That is reassuring. We will continue observation and repeat the necessary assessments. I also want to identify why his blood glucose became so low.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: His father said that he did not eat much today because he had no appetite.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Doctor, could this be something serious?
Could that be related to his condition?
Is he going to be all right?
What are you going to do now?
What should we do after he becomes stable?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please have a seat. As I know you've brought your son because of abdominal pain and constipation. Please tell me in details?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Good morning, doctor. He has been complaining of abdominal pain, and he has difficulty passing stool. His abdomen also seems swollen at times.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. Could you describe the pain and tell me where he feels it most strongly?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He usually points to the lower part of his abdomen. The pain seems to become worse before he tries to use the toilet.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. How often does he usually pass stool, and what does the stool look like?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He passes stool only every few days, and it is usually very hard and difficult to pass. Sometimes he tries for a long time.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask a few more questions to determine whether constipation is the main cause of his symptoms. Has he had any vomiting, fever, or blood in the stool?

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He has no fever, but he sometimes feels nauseous. I noticed a small amount of blood on the toilet paper once.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That may occur when hard stool causes a small anal fissure. However, we need to examine him carefully to assess the abdomen and rule out other causes of abdominal pain.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Doctor, could this be something more serious?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It is possible, although constipation is a common cause of abdominal discomfort in children. We need to assess him properly before reaching a conclusion.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: What will you do during the examination?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: First, I'm going to examine his abdomen to check for tenderness, distension, or any palpable mass. I also want to assess his hydration status and general condition.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Will he need any tests?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We may need further investigations depending on the examination. The purpose is to determine whether there is an underlying condition that requires additional treatment.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He doesn't drink much water during the day. Could that make the constipation worse?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, inadequate fluid intake can contribute to hard stools. We should also review his diet to identify factors that may be affecting his bowel habits.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: He prefers bread, rice, and sweets, and he rarely eats fruit or vegetables.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That information is useful. We need to assess his dietary pattern in order to identify areas that require improvement.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: What can we do at home to help him?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Encourage him to drink enough fluids and offer more fibre-rich foods, such as fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. It is also helpful to establish regular toilet routines to encourage healthy bowel habits.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Should I give him a laxative?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: A laxative may be appropriate in some cases, but the choice and dose should be based on his age, symptoms, and clinical assessment. We need to determine the most suitable treatment rather than giving medication without proper assessment.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: How long will it take for him to feel better?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That depends on the severity and cause of the constipation. Our immediate goal is to relieve his discomfort, soften the stool, and prevent the problem from becoming recurrent.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Are there any warning signs that I should watch for?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes. Seek urgent medical attention if he develops severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, significant abdominal swelling, blood in the stool, or marked weakness.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: I understand. What should we do if the symptoms improve?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Continue the recommended diet and fluid intake, and monitor his bowel habits. We can arrange a follow-up assessment to evaluate his progress and adjust the treatment if necessary.

dialogue.label: Mother
dialogue.text: Thank you, doctor.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're welcome. We'll examine him carefully, determine the likely cause of his symptoms, and explain the treatment plan clearly.

grammar.structure_pattern: to + verb
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Infinitive tibbiy ingliz tilida "nima maqsadda?" degan savolga javob berishi mumkin. 3. "To determine" — aniqlash uchun Determine — tibbiy ingliz tilida juda muhim fe'l. to determine = aniqlamoq / определить to determine the cause — sababni aniqlamoq to determine the diagnosis — tashxisni aniqlamoq to determine the severity — og'irlik darajasini aniqlamoq to determine the appropriate treatment — mos davolashni aniqlamoq to determine whether further tests are necessary — qo'shimcha tekshiruvlar zarurligini aniqlamoq 4. "To assess" — baholash uchun 5. "To identify" — aniqlab olish Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: to identify = aniqlamoq / выявить, определить Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

practice.setting: paediatric outpatient clinic / children's emergency department (the doctor talks to the parent)
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the MOTHER of the sick child (speak about your child in the third person).

patient_profile.name: Sarah Mitchell
patient_profile.personality_trait: worried parent, wants clear explanations

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning, doctor. He has been complaining of abdominal pain, and he has difficulty passing stool. His abdomen also seems swollen at times.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: You're welcome. We'll examine him carefully, determine the likely cause of his symptoms, and explain the treatment plan clearly.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. Please have a seat. As I know you've brought your son because of abdominal pain and constipation. Please tell me in details?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning, doctor. He has been complaining of abdominal pain, and he has difficulty passing stool. His abdomen also seems swollen at times.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. Could you describe the pain and tell me where he feels it most strongly?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He usually points to the lower part of his abdomen. The pain seems to become worse before he tries to use the toilet.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. How often does he usually pass stool, and what does the stool look like?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He passes stool only every few days, and it is usually very hard and difficult to pass. Sometimes he tries for a long time.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. I'd like to ask a few more questions to determine whether constipation is the main cause of his symptoms. Has he had any vomiting, fever, or blood in the stool?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He has no fever, but he sometimes feels nauseous. I noticed a small amount of blood on the toilet paper once.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That may occur when hard stool causes a small anal fissure. However, we need to examine him carefully to assess the abdomen and rule out other causes of abdominal pain.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Doctor, could this be something more serious?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It is possible, although constipation is a common cause of abdominal discomfort in children. We need to assess him properly before reaching a conclusion.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What will you do during the examination?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: First, I'm going to examine his abdomen to check for tenderness, distension, or any palpable mass. I also want to assess his hydration status and general condition.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will he need any tests?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We may need further investigations depending on the examination. The purpose is to determine whether there is an underlying condition that requires additional treatment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He doesn't drink much water during the day. Could that make the constipation worse?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes, inadequate fluid intake can contribute to hard stools. We should also review his diet to identify factors that may be affecting his bowel habits.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He prefers bread, rice, and sweets, and he rarely eats fruit or vegetables.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That information is useful. We need to assess his dietary pattern in order to identify areas that require improvement.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What can we do at home to help him?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Encourage him to drink enough fluids and offer more fibre-rich foods, such as fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. It is also helpful to establish regular toilet routines to enco…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Should I give him a laxative?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: A laxative may be appropriate in some cases, but the choice and dose should be based on his age, symptoms, and clinical assessment. We need to determine the most suitable treatmen…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: How long will it take for him to feel better?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That depends on the severity and cause of the constipation. Our immediate goal is to relieve his discomfort, soften the stool, and prevent the problem from becoming recurrent.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Are there any warning signs that I should watch for?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. Seek urgent medical attention if he develops severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, significant abdominal swelling, blood in the stool, or marked weakness.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand. What should we do if the symptoms improve?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Continue the recommended diet and fluid intake, and monitor his bowel habits. We can arrange a follow-up assessment to evaluate his progress and adjust the treatment if necessary.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you, doctor.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Doctor, could this be something more serious?
What will you do during the examination?
Will he need any tests?
Could that make the constipation worse?
What can we do at home to help him?

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Patient Admission & Nursing Assessment. Grammar focus: Question Forms & Clinical Questions. Includes a reference nurse–patient dialogue, 31 vocabulary items, 11 smart phrases, 24 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning. My name is Anna, and I'm one of the nurses on duty today. Could you please tell me your full name?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning. My name is Akmal Karimov.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you, Mr. Karimov. Could you also tell me your date of birth?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's 14 March 1985.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. Before we begin, could I confirm why you have come to the hospital today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been feeling unwell since this morning. I have severe abdominal pain, and I feel very weak.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Where exactly do you feel the pain?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Mostly in the lower part of my abdomen.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: How would you describe the pain? Is it sharp, cramping, or more of a constant discomfort?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's quite sharp, and it becomes worse when I move.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: On a scale from zero to ten, how severe is the pain?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I would say about eight.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: All right. Have you experienced this type of pain before?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I haven't.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you had any nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, or difficulty passing stool?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've felt nauseous, but I haven't vomited. I also haven't passed stool today.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any blood in your stool or urine?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I haven't noticed any blood.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Do you have any known allergies to medicines, foods, or other substances?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm allergic to penicillin.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. That is important information. Are you currently taking any regular medication?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I take medication for high blood pressure.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: What medication do you take, and what dose do you normally take?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I take amlodipine, 5 milligrams once a day.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. Do you have any other medical conditions that we should know about?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I have hypertension, but I don't have any other major problems.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to check your vital signs now. Could you sit comfortably here, please?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Of course.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: What is your current level of pain?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's still about eight.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I see. Your temperature is 37.8 degrees Celsius, your heart rate is slightly elevated, and your blood pressure is above the expected range.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is that serious?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: These findings require further assessment, but there is no need to panic. I'll report your condition to the doctor and continue to monitor you closely.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What will happen next?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The doctor will assess you, and we may need some blood tests or imaging studies to determine the cause of the abdominal pain.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need to stay in the hospital?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: It depends on the medical assessment and your test results. For now, please remain here and let us know immediately if the pain becomes worse.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Do you have any questions or concerns before I leave?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, thank you.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You're welcome. The information will be given to the medical team, and I'll continue to monitor your condition.
