grammar.title: Question Forms
grammar.structure_pattern: Auxiliary (do/does/did/have/is/are/can) + subject + V? | Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + V?
grammar.signal_words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: English tilida klinik muloqotda savollar bemorning shikoyatlari, simptomlari, dori-darmonlari, allergiyalari va tibbiy anamnezini aniqlash uchun juda muhim. O'zbekcha: Ingliz tilida savollar bemordan kerakli klinik ma'lumotlarni aniq va professional tarzda olish uchun ishlatiladi. Yes/No Questions — Ha/Yo'q savollar — Общие вопросы WH-Questions — Maxsus so'roq savollari — Специальные вопросы Open Questions — Ochiq savollar — Открытые вопросы Closed Questions — Yopiq savollar — Закрытые вопросы Questions with How — How bilan tuziladigan savollar — Вопросы с How Clinical Information Questions — Klinik ma'lumotni aniqlovchi savollar — Вопросы для сбора клинической информации Signal so'zlar: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Русский: В английском языке вопросы используются для получения необходимой клинической информации от пациента точно и профессионально. Сигнальные слова: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Yes/No questions start with an auxiliary ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-questions add a question word ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Open questions gather the story, closed questions confirm details. Signal words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.

grammar.title: Yes/No Questions
grammar.structure_pattern: Auxiliary (do/does/did/have/is/are/can) + subject + V? | Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + V?
grammar.signal_words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu savollarga odatda Yes yoki No bilan javob berish mumkin. O'zbekcha: Bunday savollar bemorning ma'lum bir simptom, holat yoki xususiyatga ega yoki ega emasligini tez aniqlash uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Общие вопросы / вопросы "да/нет" Русский: Такие вопросы используются для быстрого уточнения наличия или отсутствия определённого симптома, состояния или фактора риска. Сигнальные слова: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Yes/No questions start with an auxiliary ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-questions add a question word ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Open questions gather the story, closed questions confirm details. Signal words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.

practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Mr. Karimov
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning. My name is Akmal Karimov.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. My name is Anna, and I'm one of the nurses on duty today. Could you please tell me your full name?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning. My name is Akmal Karimov.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you, Mr. Karimov. Could you also tell me your date of birth?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It's 14 March 1985.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. Before we begin, could I confirm why you have come to the hospital today?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've been feeling unwell since this morning. I have severe abdominal pain, and I feel very weak.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I'm sorry to hear that. Where exactly do you feel the pain?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Mostly in the lower part of my abdomen.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How would you describe the pain? Is it sharp, cramping, or more of a constant discomfort?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It's quite sharp, and it becomes worse when I move.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: On a scale from zero to ten, how severe is the pain?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I would say about eight.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. Have you experienced this type of pain before?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I haven't.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you had any nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, or difficulty passing stool?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've felt nauseous, but I haven't vomited. I also haven't passed stool today.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any blood in your stool or urine?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I haven't noticed any blood.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you have any known allergies to medicines, foods, or other substances?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm allergic to penicillin.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. That is important information. Are you currently taking any regular medication?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I take medication for high blood pressure.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What medication do you take, and what dose do you normally take?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I take amlodipine, 5 milligrams once a day.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. Do you have any other medical conditions that we should know about?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I have hypertension, but I don't have any other major problems.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. I'm going to check your vital signs now. Could you sit comfortably here, please?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Of course.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What is your current level of pain?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It's still about eight.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. Your temperature is 37.8 degrees Celsius, your heart rate is slightly elevated, and your blood pressure is above the expected range.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is that serious?

questions_to_ask_doctor: Is that serious?
What will happen next?
Will I need to stay in the hospital?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning, Mr. Azizov. I'm Anna, the nurse on duty. How are you feeling this morning?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning. I'm feeling a little weak, and I sometimes feel dizzy when I stand up.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I see. Does the dizziness happen often, or only occasionally?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It happens quite often, especially in the morning.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you for telling me. Do you usually feel dizzy after getting out of bed?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, I usually feel dizzy for a few minutes after I get up.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to check your vital signs now. Have you had anything to eat or drink this morning?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've only had a small glass of water. I don't usually eat very much in the morning.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I understand. Do you normally drink enough water during the day?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Probably not. I sometimes forget to drink water when I'm busy.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That may be important. We'll keep an eye on your hydration status. I'm going to measure your temperature first.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Your temperature is 37.6 degrees Celsius. It's slightly above the normal range, so I'll check it again later.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean I have a fever?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. A slightly elevated temperature does not always indicate a significant fever. We need to monitor it over time.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What about my blood pressure?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Your blood pressure is 100 over 65, which is slightly low for you. Do you normally have low blood pressure?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No. My blood pressure is usually around 120 over 80.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I see. Your heart rate is also a little faster than usual. I'll record these findings and continue to monitor you closely.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: How often will you check my vital signs?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We'll check them regularly. For now, I'll monitor your blood pressure and heart rate every four hours, or more frequently if your condition changes.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What should I do if I feel dizzy again?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Please call us immediately. Don't get out of bed suddenly. Sit up slowly and wait for a moment before standing.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right. I'll do that.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any other symptoms today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I occasionally feel nauseous, but I don't have any chest pain or difficulty breathing.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That's useful information. Are you taking your regular medication as prescribed?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, I usually take my medication in the morning.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good. Have you taken today's dose?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, I took it about an hour ago.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'll document that in your nursing notes. I'll also inform the doctor about your blood pressure, heart rate, dizziness, and temperature.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Do you think my condition is serious?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: At the moment, there are no signs that require you to panic, but we should monitor you carefully. If your dizziness becomes more severe, if you faint, develop chest pain, or have difficulty breathing, tell us immediately.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll come back to check your vital signs again in four hours. In the meantime, please rest, drink fluids if you are allowed to, and call us if you feel worse.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you for explaining everything.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You're welcome. We'll continue to monitor your condition and keep you informed about any changes.

phrasebook.phrase: How are you feeling this morning?

phrasebook.translation_ru: Как вы себя чувствуете сегодня утром?

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to check your vital signs.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪm ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə tʃek jɔː ˈvaɪtl saɪnz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я собираюсь проверить ваши жизненные показатели.

phrasebook.phrase: I'd like to ask you a few questions.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪd laɪk tə ɑːsk juː ə fjuː ˈkwestʃənz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я хотела бы задать вам несколько вопросов.

phrasebook.phrase: Does it happen often?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это происходит часто?

phrasebook.phrase: Does it happen occasionally?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это происходит время от времени?

phrasebook.phrase: How often do you feel dizzy?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Как часто у вас кружится голова?

phrasebook.phrase: When does it usually happen?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Когда это обычно происходит?

phrasebook.phrase: How long does it usually last?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Как долго это обычно длится?

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to measure your temperature.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я измерю вашу температуру.

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to check your blood pressure.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪm ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə tʃek jɔː blʌd ˈpreʃə/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я проверю ваше артериальное давление.

phrasebook.phrase: Your blood pressure is slightly low.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Ваше артериальное давление немного низкое.

phrasebook.phrase: Your heart rate is slightly elevated.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Ваша частота сердечных сокращений немного повышена.

phrasebook.phrase: Your temperature is slightly above normal.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Ваша температура немного выше нормы.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll monitor you closely.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем внимательно за вами наблюдать.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll monitor your vital signs regularly.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем регулярно контролировать ваши жизненные показатели.

phrasebook.phrase: We may need to monitor you more frequently.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː meɪ niːd tə ˈmɒnɪtə juː mɔː ˈfriːkwəntli/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizni tez-tezroq kuzatishimiz kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Возможно, нам потребуется наблюдать за вами чаще.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll check your vital signs again later.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪl tʃek jɔː ˈvaɪtl saɪnz əˈɡen ˈleɪtə/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Позже я снова проверю ваши жизненные показатели.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll continue to monitor your condition.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы продолжим наблюдать за вашим состоянием.

phrasebook.phrase: Please remain in bed for now.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пока оставайтесь в постели.

phrasebook.phrase: Don't get out of bed suddenly.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не вставайте с постели резко.

phrasebook.phrase: Sit up slowly.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Медленно сядьте.

phrasebook.phrase: Wait for a moment before standing.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Немного подождите перед тем, как встать.

phrasebook.phrase: Please call us immediately if you feel worse.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /pliːz kɔːl ʌs ɪˈmiːdiətli ɪf juː fiːl wɜːs/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar ahvolingiz yomonlashsa, darhol bizni chaqiring.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Немедленно позвоните нам, если вам станет хуже.

phrasebook.phrase: Are you taking any regular medication?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы принимаете какие-либо постоянные лекарства?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you taking your medication as prescribed?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɑː juː ˈteɪkɪŋ jɔː ˌmedɪˈkeɪʃən əz prɪˈskraɪbd/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы принимаете лекарства согласно назначению врача?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you taken today's dose?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы приняли сегодняшнюю дозу?

phrasebook.phrase: When did you take your medication?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Когда вы приняли лекарство?

phrasebook.phrase: There is no need to panic.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не нужно паниковать.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to monitor you carefully.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо внимательно за вами наблюдать.

phrasebook.phrase: Please let us know if your condition changes.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /pliːz let ʌs nəʊ ɪf jɔː kənˈdɪʃən tʃeɪndʒɪz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите нам, если ваше состояние изменится.

phrasebook.phrase: Tell us immediately if you develop chest pain.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /tel ʌs ɪˈmiːdiətli ɪf juː dɪˈveləp tʃest peɪn/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ko'krak og'rig'i paydo bo'lsa, darhol bizga ayting.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Немедленно сообщите нам, если у вас появится боль в груди.

phrasebook.phrase: Tell us if you have difficulty breathing.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /tel ʌs ɪf juː hæv ˈdɪfɪkəlti ˈbriːðɪŋ/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите нам, если у вас возникнет затруднённое дыхание.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll report your condition to the doctor.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪl rɪˈpɔːt jɔː kənˈdɪʃən tə ðə ˈdɒktə/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я сообщу врачу о вашем состоянии.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll document these findings.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я задокументирую эти показатели.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll record this in your nursing notes.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪl rɪˈkɔːd ðɪs ɪn jɔː ˈnɜːsɪŋ nəʊts/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я внесу это в ваши сестринские записи.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll inform the doctor about these findings.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪl ɪnˈfɔːm ðə ˈdɒktə əˈbaʊt ðiːz ˈfaɪndɪŋz/

phrasebook.translation_ru: Я сообщу врачу об этих показателях.

grammar.title: With Main verb
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + adverb + main verb | usually / often / sometimes / normally / occasionally + main verb | Subject + be + adverb | every + singular time expression
grammar.signal_words: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: 3. "Be" Fe'li bilan Agar gapda am / is / are bo'lsa, chastota ravishi odatda be fe'lidan keyin keladi. 4. "Usually", "Often", "Sometimes" bilan savollar 5. "Every" bilan vaqt ifodalari Every — har bir / har. every morning — har tongda — каждое утро every evening — har oqshom — каждый вечер every night — har kecha — каждую ночь every four hours — har to'rt soatda — каждые четыре часа Bu iboralar harakatning necha marta bajarilishini bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: every week — har hafta — каждую неделю bir marta — один раз один раз в день ikki marta — два раза два раза в день uch marta — три раза три раза в день Сигнальные слова: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Adverbs describe how, when or to what degree something happens: "Her breathing became worse rapidly", "The condition is gradually improving". Adverbs of degree (slightly, significantly, increasingly) make clinical descriptions precise. "Since" gives the starting point ("since yesterday"), "for" the length of time ("for three days") and "ago" counts back from now ("two hours ago"). Exact times ("at about 7:15 this morning") are essential in time-critical conditions such as stroke. Signal words: rapidly, gradually, carefully, slightly, significantly, increasingly.

grammar.title: Clinical Question Pattern: "How often...?"
grammar.structure_pattern: Auxiliary (do/does/did/have/is/are/can) + subject + V? | Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + V?
grammar.signal_words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Yes/No savollar yordamchi fe'l bilan boshlanadi ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-savollar so'roq so'zi bilan ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Ochiq savollar hikoyani, yopiq savollar aniq detallarni yig'adi. Signal so'zlar: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Общие вопросы начинаются со вспомогательного глагола («Do you have any allergies?», «Have you had a fever?»); специальные — с вопросительного слова («How long have you had the pain?», «Where exactly does it hurt?»). Открытые вопросы собирают историю, закрытые — уточняют детали. Сигнальные слова: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Yes/No questions start with an auxiliary ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-questions add a question word ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Open questions gather the story, closed questions confirm details. Signal words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.

grammar.title: Time expression + clinical action
grammar.structure_pattern: since + starting point (since yesterday) | for + period (for three days) | period + ago (two hours ago)
grammar.signal_words: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "Since" boshlanish nuqtasini ("since yesterday"), "for" davomiylikni ("for three days"), "ago" hozirdan orqaga sanashni ("two hours ago") bildiradi. Aniq vaqt ("at about 7:15 this morning") insult kabi vaqt-kritik holatlarda juda muhim. Signal so'zlar: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Since» указывает точку начала («since yesterday»), «for» — продолжительность («for three days»), «ago» — отсчёт назад от настоящего («two hours ago»). Точное время («at about 7:15 this morning») критично при инсульте и других неотложных состояниях. Сигнальные слова: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Since" gives the starting point ("since yesterday"), "for" the length of time ("for three days") and "ago" counts back from now ("two hours ago"). Exact times ("at about 7:15 this morning") are essential in time-critical conditions such as stroke. Signal words: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.

practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Mr. Azizov
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning. I'm feeling a little weak, and I sometimes feel dizzy when I stand up.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: Not necessarily. A slightly elevated temperature does not always indicate a significant fever. We need to monitor it over time.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning, Mr. Azizov. I'm Anna, the nurse on duty. How are you feeling this morning?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning. I'm feeling a little weak, and I sometimes feel dizzy when I stand up.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. Does the dizziness happen often, or only occasionally?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It happens quite often, especially in the morning.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you for telling me. Do you usually feel dizzy after getting out of bed?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, I usually feel dizzy for a few minutes after I get up.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. I'm going to check your vital signs now. Have you had anything to eat or drink this morning?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've only had a small glass of water. I don't usually eat very much in the morning.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I understand. Do you normally drink enough water during the day?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Probably not. I sometimes forget to drink water when I'm busy.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That may be important. We'll keep an eye on your hydration status. I'm going to measure your temperature first.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Your temperature is 37.6 degrees Celsius. It's slightly above the normal range, so I'll check it again later.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Does that mean I have a fever?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Not necessarily. A slightly elevated temperature does not always indicate a significant fever. We need to monitor it over time.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What about my blood pressure?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Your blood pressure is 100 over 65, which is slightly low for you. Do you normally have low blood pressure?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning, Ms. Dilnoza. I'm Anna, your nurse. I've come to give you your prescribed medication.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning. Is this the medicine for my blood pressure?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. This is the medication prescribed for you. Before I give it to you, I need to check the medication chart and make sure everything is correct.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What exactly do you need to check?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I must check the medication name, the prescribed dose, the route of administration, and the scheduled time. I also need to make sure that the medication has been prescribed for you.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I took my regular medicine at home this morning. Could that be a problem?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: It could be important. You must tell us about any medication you have already taken today. We need this information to avoid giving you an unnecessary additional dose.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I took one tablet at about eight o'clock.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'll document that information and check your medication chart before proceeding.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Do I have to take this medication now?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: According to the prescription, you should take it at this time. You should take it exactly as prescribed unless the doctor changes the order.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Can I take it with juice?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You should take it with water unless you have been given different instructions. Water is usually the safest choice for taking medication.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What if I have difficulty swallowing the tablet?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You should tell me before taking it. You must not crush, split, or chew the tablet unless we confirm that it is safe to do so.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Why is that important?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Some tablets are designed to release the medication slowly or in a specific part of the digestive system. Changing the tablet may affect how the medication works.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I see. What should I do if I feel unwell after taking it?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You should tell us immediately. You may experience a mild side effect, but severe or unexpected symptoms must be assessed by a healthcare professional.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What kind of symptoms would be serious?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Severe dizziness, fainting, difficulty breathing, severe weakness, or any sudden change in your condition should be reported immediately.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Can I take another tablet if I think the first one hasn't worked?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: No. You must not take an additional dose on your own. The medication dose has been prescribed for a specific reason, and taking more than prescribed may be harmful.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Even if I still have symptoms?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. You should contact the healthcare team rather than changing the dose yourself.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What happens if a patient receives the wrong medication?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That would be a medication error and must be reported immediately. The patient must be assessed, and the medical team must be informed according to the hospital's safety procedure.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: So you have to check everything before giving medication?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Exactly. We must follow the medication-safety procedure every time. We should never rely only on memory or assume that a medication is correct.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes sense.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I've completed the necessary checks. Here is your medication. Please take it with some water.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good. Please remain seated for a few minutes. If you feel dizzy or unwell, you should call me.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I will.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll document the medication administration in your nursing record. If you have any questions or concerns about your medication, you can always ask us before taking it.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you for explaining everything so carefully.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Medication safety is our priority, and we must make sure that every medication is administered correctly and safely.

grammar.structure_pattern: modal (can / could / may / might / must / should / have to) + V1
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Qoidalar, xavfsizlik, majburiyat va ruxsatni ifodalovchi modal fe'llar Ushbu modulda quyidagi modal fe'llar asosiy grammatik birlik sifatida o'rganiladi: 2. MODAL VERBS NIMA? Modal fe'llar asosiy fe'lga qo'shimcha ma'no beradi. Ular: Hamshiralikda modal fe'llar juda muhim, chunki hamshira bemorga ko'rsatma beradi, xavfsizlik qoidalarini tushuntiradi va ehtiyot choralarini aytadi. Signal so'zlar: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы для выражения правил, безопасности, обязанности и разрешения Модальные глаголы — это вспомогательные глаголы, которые выражают: В сестринской практике модальные глаголы особенно важны, поскольку медсестра часто даёт пациенту инструкции, объясняет правила безопасности и предупреждает о возможных рисках. Сигнальные слова: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Modal Verbs for Rules, Safety, Obligation & Permission must not / mustn't should not / shouldn't Modal verbs are auxiliary verbs that express: Modal verbs are especially important in nursing because nurses frequently give instructions, explain safety procedures, and communicate precautions. Signal words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.signal_words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission

grammar.title: Modal + Infinitive
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + modal verb + base verb | Ega + modal fe'l + asosiy fe'l
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ko'pchilik modal fe'llardan keyin fe'lning asosiy shakli ishlatiladi va uning oldidan to kelmaydi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: После большинства модальных глаголов используется начальная форма глагола без to. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

grammar.title: Must
grammar.structure_pattern: must + V1 | have to / has to + V1 | mustn't + V1 (prohibition) | don't have to + V1 (not necessary)
grammar.signal_words: necessity, obligation, prohibition
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Must kuchli majburiyat yoki xavfsizlik nuqtayi nazaridan bajarilishi shart bo'lgan harakatni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: necessity, obligation, prohibition.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: must = должен / обязан Сигнальные слова: necessity, obligation, prohibition.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Must" expresses strong necessity from the speaker ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — an external rule or requirement. "Mustn't" means it is forbidden, while "don't have to" means it is not necessary. Signal words: necessity, obligation, prohibition.

grammar.rule_explanation_ru: must not = нельзя / запрещено Сигнальные слова: necessity, obligation, prohibition.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Must" expresses strong necessity from the speaker ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — an external rule or requirement. "Mustn't" means it is forbidden, while "don't have to" means it is not necessary. Signal words: necessity, obligation, prohibition.

grammar.title: Should
grammar.structure_pattern: should / ought to + V1 | shouldn't + V1
grammar.signal_words: advice, recommendation
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: should = kerak / ma'qul / tavsiya etiladi Should odatda maslahat, tavsiya yoki to'g'ri deb hisoblangan harakatni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: advice, recommendation.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: should = следует / стоит Сигнальные слова: advice, recommendation.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Should" and "ought to" give advice and recommendations — the most common way to tell a patient what to do: "You should drink plenty of fluids", "You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice". Signal words: advice, recommendation.

grammar.title: Can
grammar.structure_pattern: can / could + V1 | Can you …? | Could you …, please?
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: can = mumkin / qila olmoq Tibbiy muloqotda can ruxsat yoki bemorga mavjud imkoniyatni bildirish uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: can = можно / мочь Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

grammar.structure_pattern: may / might + V1 | may / might + have + V3 (past possibility)
grammar.signal_words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu Can I...? ga qaraganda rasmiyroq va professionalroq. Signal so'zlar: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «May» и «might» выражают возможность и осторожное клиническое суждение: «It may be an infection», «You might need to stay in hospital». «May» также даёт вежливое разрешение. «Might have + V3» — возможное событие в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. Signal words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.

grammar.rule_explanation_en: "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. grammar.title: Could
grammar.structure_pattern: can / could + V1 | Can you …? | Could you …, please?
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "Can" qobiliyat, ruxsat va hozirgi ehtimollikni bildiradi ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" yumshoqroq, muloyimroq ("Could you describe the pain?") va o'tmishdagi qobiliyatni ifodalaydi. Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Can» выражает способность, разрешение и возможность в настоящем («DKA can become life-threatening»); «could» — более мягкий, вежливый вариант («Could you describe the pain?») и способность в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs
grammar.structure_pattern: modal (can / could / may / might / must / should / have to) + V1
grammar.signal_words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Modal fe'llar gapga munosabat qo'shadi: ehtimollik (may, might, could), imkoniyat/ruxsat (can, could), maslahat (should, ought to), majburiyat (must, have to) va taqiq (mustn't). Modaldan keyin fe'l doim asosiy shaklda (V1) keladi. Signal so'zlar: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы передают отношение говорящего: возможность (may, might, could), способность/разрешение (can, could), совет (should, ought to), обязанность (must, have to) и запрет (mustn't). После модального глагола всегда стоит начальная форма. Сигнальные слова: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Modal verbs add the speaker's attitude: possibility (may, might, could), ability/permission (can, could), advice (should, ought to), obligation (must, have to) and prohibition (mustn't). The main verb after a modal is always the base form. Signal words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.

grammar.title: Must vs Should
grammar.structure_pattern: must + V1 | have to / has to + V1 | mustn't + V1 (prohibition) | don't have to + V1 (not necessary) | should / ought to + V1 | shouldn't + V1
grammar.signal_words: necessity, obligation, prohibition
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "Must" so'zlovchining qat'iy talabini bildiradi ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — tashqi qoida yoki talab. "Mustn't" — taqiqlangan, "don't have to" esa — shart emas. "Should" va "ought to" maslahat va tavsiya beradi — bemorga nima qilish kerakligini aytishning eng keng tarqalgan usuli: "You should drink plenty of fluids", "You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice". Signal so'zlar: necessity, obligation, prohibition.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Must» выражает строгую необходимость со стороны говорящего («You must take the full course of antibiotics»); «have to» — внешнее правило или требование. «Mustn't» — запрещено, «don't have to» — не обязательно. «Should» и «ought to» выражают совет и рекомендацию — самый частый способ сказать пациенту, что делать: «You should drink plenty of fluids», «You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice». Сигнальные слова: necessity, obligation, prohibition.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Must" expresses strong necessity from the speaker ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — an external rule or requirement. "Mustn't" means it is forbidden, while "don't have to" means it is not necessary. "Should" and "ought to" give advice and recommendations — the most common way to tell a patient what to do: "You should drink plenty of fluids", "You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice". Signal words: necessity, obligation, prohibition.

grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Must" expresses strong necessity from the speaker ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — an external rule or requirement. "Mustn't" means it is forbidden, while "don't have to" means it is not necessary. Signal words: necessity, obligation, prohibition.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs and the passive form
grammar.structure_pattern: modal + be + past participle
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: ⚠️ Bu modulda asosiy grammatik fokus modal fe'llarning faol gapdagi qo'llanishidir. Biroq klinik hujjatlarda quyidagi konstruktsiya ko'p uchrashi mumkin: Bu konstruktsiya klinik hujjatlar va protokollarda juda ko'p uchraydi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». Причастие настоящего времени (-ing) описывает активный процесс («a spreading infection», «the patient lying in bed»); причастие прошедшего времени (V3) — состояние или результат («an infected wound», «samples taken immediately»). Они сокращают придаточные предложения. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Present participles (-ing) describe an active process ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"); past participles (V3) describe a state or result ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately"). They shorten relative clauses. Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Quick Reference — Tezkor Jadval
grammar.structure_pattern: must + V | must not + V | should + V | should not + V | have to + V | don't have to + V | can + V | cannot + V | may + V | might + V | could + V
grammar.signal_words: necessity, obligation, prohibition
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "Must" so'zlovchining qat'iy talabini bildiradi ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — tashqi qoida yoki talab. "Mustn't" — taqiqlangan, "don't have to" esa — shart emas. "Should" va "ought to" maslahat va tavsiya beradi — bemorga nima qilish kerakligini aytishning eng keng tarqalgan usuli: "You should drink plenty of fluids", "You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice". Signal so'zlar: necessity, obligation, prohibition.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Must» выражает строгую необходимость со стороны говорящего («You must take the full course of antibiotics»); «have to» — внешнее правило или требование. «Mustn't» — запрещено, «don't have to» — не обязательно. «Should» и «ought to» выражают совет и рекомендацию — самый частый способ сказать пациенту, что делать: «You should drink plenty of fluids», «You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice». Сигнальные слова: necessity, obligation, prohibition.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Must" expresses strong necessity from the speaker ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — an external rule or requirement. "Mustn't" means it is forbidden, while "don't have to" means it is not necessary. "Should" and "ought to" give advice and recommendations — the most common way to tell a patient what to do: "You should drink plenty of fluids", "You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice". Signal words: necessity, obligation, prohibition.

grammar.title: Top 15 Modal Verb Sentences for Nurses
grammar.structure_pattern: modal (can / could / may / might / must / should / have to) + V1
grammar.signal_words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Modal fe'llar gapga munosabat qo'shadi: ehtimollik (may, might, could), imkoniyat/ruxsat (can, could), maslahat (should, ought to), majburiyat (must, have to) va taqiq (mustn't). Modaldan keyin fe'l doim asosiy shaklda (V1) keladi. Signal so'zlar: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы передают отношение говорящего: возможность (may, might, could), способность/разрешение (can, could), совет (should, ought to), обязанность (must, have to) и запрет (mustn't). После модального глагола всегда стоит начальная форма. Сигнальные слова: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Modal verbs add the speaker's attitude: possibility (may, might, could), ability/permission (can, could), advice (should, ought to), obligation (must, have to) and prohibition (mustn't). The main verb after a modal is always the base form. Signal words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.

practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Ms. Dilnoza
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning. Is this the medicine for my blood pressure?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning, Ms. Dilnoza. I'm Anna, your nurse. I've come to give you your prescribed medication.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning. Is this the medicine for my blood pressure?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. This is the medication prescribed for you. Before I give it to you, I need to check the medication chart and make sure everything is correct.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What exactly do you need to check?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I must check the medication name, the prescribed dose, the route of administration, and the scheduled time. I also need to make sure that the medication has been prescribed for yo…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I took my regular medicine at home this morning. Could that be a problem?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It could be important. You must tell us about any medication you have already taken today. We need this information to avoid giving you an unnecessary additional dose.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand. I took one tablet at about eight o'clock.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. I'll document that information and check your medication chart before proceeding.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Do I have to take this medication now?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: According to the prescription, you should take it at this time. You should take it exactly as prescribed unless the doctor changes the order.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Can I take it with juice?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You should take it with water unless you have been given different instructions. Water is usually the safest choice for taking medication.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What if I have difficulty swallowing the tablet?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You should tell me before taking it. You must not crush, split, or chew the tablet unless we confirm that it is safe to do so.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Why is that important?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Some tablets are designed to release the medication slowly or in a specific part of the digestive system. Changing the tablet may affect how the medication works.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I see. What should I do if I feel unwell after taking it?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You should tell us immediately. You may experience a mild side effect, but severe or unexpected symptoms must be assessed by a healthcare professional.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What kind of symptoms would be serious?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Severe dizziness, fainting, difficulty breathing, severe weakness, or any sudden change in your condition should be reported immediately.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Can I take another tablet if I think the first one hasn't worked?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: No. You must not take an additional dose on your own. The medication dose has been prescribed for a specific reason, and taking more than prescribed may be harmful.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Even if I still have symptoms?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. You should contact the healthcare team rather than changing the dose yourself.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What happens if a patient receives the wrong medication?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That would be a medication error and must be reported immediately. The patient must be assessed, and the medical team must be informed according to the hospital's safety procedure.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: So you have to check everything before giving medication?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Exactly. We must follow the medication-safety procedure every time. We should never rely only on memory or assume that a medication is correct.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: That makes sense.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I've completed the necessary checks. Here is your medication. Please take it with some water.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Is this the medicine for my blood pressure?
What exactly do you need to check?
Could that be a problem?
Do I have to take this medication now?
Can I take it with juice?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning. I'm Anna, the nurse on duty. I've come to check the wound on your leg and change the dressing.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning. Thank you. The wound has been a little painful since yesterday.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I see. Can you tell me whether you have noticed any redness, swelling, or discharge around the wound?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: There is some redness around it, and I noticed a small amount of yellowish discharge this morning.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you for telling me. I'll need to examine the area carefully. Please sit comfortably and keep the affected leg still.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right. Is the redness a sign of an infection?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: It can be a sign of infection, but we need to assess the wound carefully before making a conclusion. I'll check the skin around the wound, the amount of discharge, and whether there is any swelling.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: The area also feels warmer than the skin around it.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That is useful information. An increase in local temperature, together with redness, swelling, or discharge, may require further assessment.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will you change the dressing?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: First, I'm going to perform hand hygiene and prepare the necessary equipment. I'll then remove the old dressing carefully and inspect the wound.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will it hurt when you remove it?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You may feel some discomfort, especially if the dressing has become attached to the wound. I'll remove it slowly and carefully.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Before I start, I need to make sure that the equipment is clean and that everything we need is ready. We must also maintain a clean technique throughout the procedure.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Ok. Is this important ?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Of course, the microorganisms can enter an open wound and cause an infection. Good wound care helps reduce the risk of infection and supports normal healing.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Should I keep the wound covered all the time?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That depends on the type of wound, its condition, and the treatment plan. You should follow the instructions given by the healthcare team.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Can I change the dressing myself at home?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You may be able to do so if you have been given the correct instructions and the wound is suitable for home care. However, you should not touch the wound with unclean hands or use an unclean dressing.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What should I do if I notice more discharge?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You should contact a healthcare professional if the discharge increases, develops an unpleasant smell, or changes in appearance. You should also report increasing pain, redness, swelling, or fever.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What about the dressing? How often should it be changed?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The frequency depends on the wound condition and the prescribed treatment. We should change it according to the care plan, rather than changing it unnecessarily.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is there anything else I should remember?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. Keep the wound area clean and dry as instructed. Do not apply any cream, powder, or other substance unless it has been recommended by a healthcare professional.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right. I'll remember that.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I've finished examining the wound. There is some redness and a small amount of discharge, so I'll document the findings and inform the doctor.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean I have an infection?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. These findings need to be assessed in context. The doctor may decide whether any further treatment or investigation is necessary.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you for explaining everything.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Proper wound care and infection prevention are important parts of your recovery. Please let us know if the wound becomes more painful or if you develop a fever or any other new symptom.

grammar.title: Present Perfect
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3 | Subject + have/has + V3
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect yaqinda sodir bo'lgan yoki o'tmishda boshlangan, lekin natijasi hozirgi vaziyat bilan bog'liq bo'lgan holatlarni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect используется для описания действия, которое произошло недавно или в прошлом, но имеет связь с настоящей ситуацией или результатом. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Present Simple
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V1 | He / She / It + V-s/es
grammar.signal_words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Simple umumiy tibbiy faktlar, odatlar, klinik holatlar va doimiy haqiqatlarni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Simple используется для выражения общих медицинских фактов, постоянных состояний, привычных действий и закономерностей. Сигнальные слова: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.

grammar.title: Modal Verb — Can
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + can + V1 | Subject + may + V1
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Can imkoniyat yoki biror narsa sodir bo'lishi mumkinligini bildiradi. ⚠️ Can dan keyin fe'lning boshlang'ich shakli keladi. May biror holatning ehtimoliy ekanligini bildiradi. Tibbiy ingliz tilida tashxisni qat'iy tasdiqlamasdan, ehtiyotkorlik bilan fikr bildirish uchun juda foydali. Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Can выражает возможность или способность; в медицинском контексте часто означает, что определённое состояние может произойти. May выражает вероятность. В медицинском английском он часто используется для осторожного выражения предположения, когда диагноз ещё не подтверждён. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

grammar.title: Need to — Necessity
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + need to + V1
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Need to biror ishni bajarish zarurligini bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Need to используется для выражения необходимости выполнить определённое действие. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

grammar.title: Should — Medical Advice
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + should + V1 | should not + V1
grammar.signal_words: advice, recommendation
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Should bemorga maslahat, tavsiya yoki kerakli harakatni aytish uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: advice, recommendation.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Should используется для выражения совета, рекомендации или правильного действия, особенно при консультировании пациента. Сигнальные слова: advice, recommendation.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Should" and "ought to" give advice and recommendations — the most common way to tell a patient what to do: "You should drink plenty of fluids", "You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice". Signal words: advice, recommendation.

grammar.title: Passive Voice
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Passive Voice harakatni kim bajarganidan ko'ra, harakatning o'zi yoki unga uchragan obyekt muhim bo'lganda ishlatiladi. Tibbiyotda Passive Voice juda ko'p ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важно само действие или объект действия, а не тот, кто его выполняет. Пассивный залог очень часто используется в медицинском английском. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: First Conditional
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, ... will/should/may + V1 | If + Present Simple, + will/should/may + V1
grammar.signal_words: if, unless, as soon as, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: First Conditional kelajakda yuz berishi mumkin bo'lgan real shart va uning natijasini ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: First Conditional используется для описания реального или возможного условия в будущем и его результата. Сигнальные слова: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: First Conditional describes a real, possible future situation and its result. Clinicians use it for warnings, plans and safety-netting: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". Do not use "will" after "if". Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: if, unless, as soon as, when.

grammar.title: Preposition + Gerund
grammar.structure_pattern: before / after / without / by + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Before, after, without, by kabi predloglardan keyin fe'l kelganda ko'pincha V-ing shakli ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: После предлогов before, after, without, by перед глаголом обычно используется форма V-ing. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

grammar.title: There Is — There Are
grammar.structure_pattern: There is + singular / uncountable noun | There are + plural noun
grammar.signal_words: some, any, much, many, a lot of, a little, a few, several
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: There is / There are biror joyda narsa yoki klinik belgi mavjudligini bildirish uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: some, any, much, many, a lot of, a little, a few, several.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: There is / There are используются, чтобы сообщить о наличии чего-либо или какого-либо клинического признака. Сигнальные слова: some, any, much, many, a lot of, a little, a few, several.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Countable nouns can be counted (symptoms, tablets, episodes) and take many/a few; uncountable nouns (pain, blood, fluid, information) take much/a little and have no plural. "Some" is used in statements and offers, "any" in questions and negatives: "Do you have any pain?" Signal words: some, any, much, many, a lot of, a little, a few, several.

grammar.title: Amount of — Number of

grammar.title: High-Value Clinical Grammar Patterns
grammar.structure_pattern: Have you + V3...? | can + V1 | may + V1 | need to + V1 | should + V1 | should not + V1 | if + Present Simple | will be + V3 | whether + clause | before + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Talaba quyidagi strukturalardan foydalanib bemorga maslahat beradi: Siz ... qilishingiz kerak. Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Can» выражает способность, разрешение и возможность в настоящем («DKA can become life-threatening»); «could» — более мягкий, вежливый вариант («Could you describe the pain?») и способность в прошлом. «May» и «might» выражают возможность и осторожное клиническое суждение: «It may be an infection», «You might need to stay in hospital». «May» также даёт вежливое разрешение. «Might have + V3» — возможное событие в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)

patient_profile.name: Grace Hughes
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning. Thank you. The wound has been a little painful since yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. I'm Anna, the nurse on duty. I've come to check the wound on your leg and change the dressing.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning. Thank you. The wound has been a little painful since yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. Can you tell me whether you have noticed any redness, swelling, or discharge around the wound?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: There is some redness around it, and I noticed a small amount of yellowish discharge this morning.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you for telling me. I'll need to examine the area carefully. Please sit comfortably and keep the affected leg still.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right. Is the redness a sign of an infection?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It can be a sign of infection, but we need to assess the wound carefully before making a conclusion. I'll check the skin around the wound, the amount of discharge, and whether the…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: The area also feels warmer than the skin around it.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That is useful information. An increase in local temperature, together with redness, swelling, or discharge, may require further assessment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will you change the dressing?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: First, I'm going to perform hand hygiene and prepare the necessary equipment. I'll then remove the old dressing carefully and inspect the wound.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will it hurt when you remove it?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You may feel some discomfort, especially if the dressing has become attached to the wound. I'll remove it slowly and carefully.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Before I start, I need to make sure that the equipment is clean and that everything we need is ready. We must also maintain a clean technique throughout the procedure.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Ok. Is this important ?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Of course, the microorganisms can enter an open wound and cause an infection. Good wound care helps reduce the risk of infection and supports normal healing.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Should I keep the wound covered all the time?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That depends on the type of wound, its condition, and the treatment plan. You should follow the instructions given by the healthcare team.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Can I change the dressing myself at home?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You may be able to do so if you have been given the correct instructions and the wound is suitable for home care. However, you should not touch the wound with unclean hands or use…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What should I do if I notice more discharge?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You should contact a healthcare professional if the discharge increases, develops an unpleasant smell, or changes in appearance. You should also report increasing pain, redness, s…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What about the dressing? How often should it be changed?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: The frequency depends on the wound condition and the prescribed treatment. We should change it according to the care plan, rather than changing it unnecessarily.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is there anything else I should remember?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. Keep the wound area clean and dry as instructed. Do not apply any cream, powder, or other substance unless it has been recommended by a healthcare professional.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right. I'll remember that.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I've finished examining the wound. There is some redness and a small amount of discharge, so I'll document the findings and inform the doctor.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Does that mean I have an infection?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Not necessarily. These findings need to be assessed in context. The doctor may decide whether any further treatment or investigation is necessary.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you for explaining everything.

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Pain Assessment & Management. Grammar focus: Comparatives & Superlatives. Includes a reference nurse–patient dialogue, 37 vocabulary items, 53 smart phrases, 16 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning, Mr. Jhon. How are you feeling today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning. I'm not feeling very well. The pain has become worse since last night.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me where the pain is strongest?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: The pain is strongest in my lower back. It is also spreading to my abdomen.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Is the pain in your back more severe than the pain in your abdomen?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. The back pain is much stronger than the abdominal pain.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I see. How would you describe the pain? Is it sharp, dull, burning, or aching?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It is mostly a dull, aching pain, but sometimes it becomes sharper.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: When is the pain most severe — during the day or at night?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It is usually worse at night. Last night was probably the worst night I've had recently.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: On a scale from zero to ten, where zero means no pain and ten means the worst pain imaginable, how would you rate your pain now?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: At the moment, it is about seven out of ten. Yesterday, it was around five.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: So, your pain is more intense today than it was yesterday.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, definitely. It is much more difficult to tolerate today.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Does anything make the pain better or worse?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Sitting makes it worse. Walking is also difficult, but lying down is slightly more comfortable.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Is the pain worse when you move than when you are resting?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. Movement makes the pain considerably worse.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you taken your prescribed pain medication?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, I took it two hours ago, but it hasn't helped very much.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Is the medication less effective than it was before?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I think so. It used to control the pain better.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you for telling me. Your pain seems to be more severe and less well controlled than it was previously.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Nurse, does this mean that my cancer is getting worse?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. An increase in pain does not always mean that the disease itself has progressed. We need to assess your symptoms carefully and report any changes to the doctor.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What can we do to make the pain easier to manage?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll document your pain level and inform the doctor. The doctor may review your current pain medication and decide whether your treatment needs to be adjusted.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm worried that stronger pain medicine will make me too sleepy.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I understand. Some stronger medicines can cause more drowsiness, but the doctor will choose the most appropriate treatment for you. We'll also monitor you closely for any side effects.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is there anything I can do to make the pain less severe?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Try to find the position that is most comfortable for you. Avoid movements that make the pain significantly worse, and let us know if the pain changes or becomes stronger.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I just want the pain to become less severe.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Of course. We'll do our best to keep your pain as well controlled as possible. Please tell me immediately if the pain becomes significantly worse, changes in character, or is no longer controlled by your medication.
