practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Henry Cole
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Yes, I can hear you. I suddenly feel very weak and dizzy.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Sir, can you hear me? Please stay calm and do not try to get up.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, I can hear you. I suddenly feel very weak and dizzy.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. Stay where you are and try to breathe slowly. Do not move until we assess your condition.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What is happening to me?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I'm going to check your vital signs first. Please keep your arm still so I can measure your blood pressure accurately.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I feel like I might faint.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Tell me immediately if you feel that you are going to lose consciousness. Try to keep your eyes open and focus on my voice.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'll try.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good. Lie back carefully and raise your legs slightly. I need you to remain in this position while I check your pulse and oxygen saturation.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: My chest feels uncomfortable.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Where exactly do you feel the discomfort? Point to the area with one finger.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Right here, in the middle of my chest.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Does the pain spread to your arm, shoulder, back, neck, or jaw?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It feels like it is spreading to my left arm.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I understand. Do not eat or drink anything for now. I'm going to inform the doctor immediately.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Am I going to be all right?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We are going to monitor you closely and provide the necessary care. Try not to worry. Just keep breathing slowly and remain still.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm having trouble breathing now.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Sit upright if you can do so safely. Take slow, controlled breaths. Do not walk or stand up without assistance.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I feel very weak.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That's why I want you to stay in bed. I'm going to attach the monitor to check your heart rate and oxygen level.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What should I do if I feel worse?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Press the call button and tell us immediately. If you feel severe chest pain, become extremely dizzy, or have increasing difficulty breathing, report it at once.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Should I try to take deep breaths?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Take slow, controlled breaths rather than very deep breaths. Try to remain as calm as possible.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good. Keep your arm relaxed and do not remove the monitoring equipment. I need to reassess your vital signs in a few minutes.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you for helping me.

Should I try to take deep breaths?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning, Sir. How are you feeling this morning?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning. I'm feeling not so good. My hip still hurts, and I find it difficult to move in bed.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I understand. Since you had surgery, it is important to maintain good hygiene and prevent complications from staying in bed for too long. Would you like me to help you with your morning hygiene?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, please. I'd like to wash, but I'm worried about moving my hip.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That's understandable. I'll help you without putting unnecessary pressure on your operated side. Before we start, I need to check your skin, especially the areas that are exposed to prolonged pressure.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What areas are you going to check?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll check your heels, ankles, hips, lower back, and the area around your buttocks. These areas are more likely to develop pressure injuries when a patient has limited mobility.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I see. My lower back feels a little uncomfortable.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you for telling me. Let me have a look. I can see some mild redness over your sacral area, but there is no open wound. We need to prevent the redness from getting worse.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is it serious?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Not at this stage, but we need to take it seriously. Regular repositioning can help reduce pressure on the area. I'd like to turn you slightly onto your side.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will that hurt my hip?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: It may cause some discomfort, but I'll help you move slowly and carefully. Please don't try to turn yourself suddenly.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: First, bend your unaffected knee slightly. Now, try to move your shoulders and upper body together with me. Good. I'm supporting your operated leg while we turn.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That's uncomfortable, but I can manage it.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good. We've changed your position successfully. I'm going to place a pillow between your knees to keep your hip in a safe position and reduce pressure.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That feels more comfortable.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Excellent. Now, let's continue with your hygiene. I'll help you wash your face and upper body first. You can try washing your hands and face yourself if you feel strong enough.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'd like to do that myself.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Of course. Maintaining as much independence as possible is important for your recovery. Let me know if you start feeling tired or dizzy.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I will.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: After washing, we'll change your gown and make sure your bed is clean and dry. Keeping the skin clean and dry helps prevent irritation and infection.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Do I need to move again?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes, but only with assistance. We also need to encourage safe movement to prevent stiffness and improve circulation.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm afraid of putting weight on my operated leg.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That's understandable. You should not put weight on it until the doctor or physiotherapist says it is safe. For now, we can practice moving your unaffected leg and doing some gentle ankle movements.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: How often should I move my ankle?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Try moving your ankle up and down several times each hour while you're awake, unless you've been given different instructions. Gentle movement can help improve circulation and reduce the risk of complications.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What about getting out of bed?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We'll help you sit on the edge of the bed when it is safe to do so. You must not get up without assistance because you may become dizzy or lose your balance.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Before helping you stand, I'll check your blood pressure and make sure you're feeling well enough. We'll also make sure the floor is clear and your walking aid is within reach.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes me feel safer.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good. Remember, asking for help is not a sign of weakness. It helps you stay safe while recovering.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you. I was worried that I would have to stay in bed all the time.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: No. Our goal is to help you become more mobile gradually and safely. Staying in one position for too long can increase the risk of pressure injuries, muscle stiffness, and other complications.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: So, moving a little is actually important?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Exactly. Regular repositioning, maintaining good hygiene, keeping your skin dry, and doing safe exercises can all help prevent complications.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I'll try to move more and ask for help when I need it.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That's excellent. Please tell me if you notice any new redness, pain, swelling, numbness, or discomfort, especially around areas under pressure.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I will.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good. We'll continue checking your skin and mobility regularly and adjust your care plan if necessary.

phrasebook.phrase: Would you like me to help you with your morning hygiene?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wʊd juː laɪk miː tə help juː.../
phrasebook.translation_ru: Хотите, чтобы я помог вам с утренней гигиеной?

phrasebook.phrase: I'll help you with your personal hygiene.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll help you wash your face and upper body.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yuzingiz va yuqori tanangizni yuvishingizga yordam beraman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я помогу вам умыться и помыть верхнюю часть тела.

phrasebook.phrase: You can try washing yourself.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы можете попробовать помыться самостоятельно.

phrasebook.phrase: Let me know if you feel tired or dizzy.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Charchasangiz yoki boshingiz aylansa, menga ayting.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите мне, если почувствуете усталость или головокружение.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll change your gown after washing.
phrasebook.translation_ru: После мытья мы сменим вашу больничную одежду.

phrasebook.phrase: I need to check your skin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мне нужно проверить вашу кожу.

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to check the areas exposed to pressure.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я проверю участки, подвергающиеся давлению.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll check your heels, ankles, hips, and lower back.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tovonlaringiz, to'piqlaringiz, sonlaringiz va belingizni tekshiraman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я проверю ваши пятки, лодыжки, бёдра и поясницу.

phrasebook.phrase: I can see some mild redness over your sacral area.

phrasebook.phrase: There is no open wound.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to prevent the redness from getting worse.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Qizarish kuchayib ketishining oldini olishimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам нужно предотвратить усиление покраснения.

phrasebook.phrase: Regular repositioning can help reduce pressure.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Muntazam holatni o'zgartirish bosimni kamaytirishga yordam beradi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Регулярное изменение положения помогает уменьшить давление.

phrasebook.phrase: I'd like to turn you slightly onto your side.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я хотел бы немного повернуть вас на бок.

phrasebook.phrase: Please don't try to turn yourself suddenly.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пожалуйста, не пытайтесь резко повернуться самостоятельно.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll help you move slowly and carefully.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sekin va ehtiyotkorlik bilan harakatlanishingizga yordam beraman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я помогу вам двигаться медленно и осторожно.

phrasebook.phrase: I'm supporting your operated leg.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я поддерживаю вашу оперированную ногу.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll place a pillow between your knees.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я положу подушку между вашими коленями.

phrasebook.phrase: This will help reduce pressure.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Это поможет уменьшить давление.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to encourage safe movement.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо поощрять безопасное движение.

phrasebook.phrase: Try to move slowly and carefully.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sekin va ehtiyotkorlik bilan harakatlanishga harakat qiling.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Постарайтесь двигаться медленно и осторожно.

phrasebook.phrase: You should not put weight on your operated leg.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Operatsiya qilingan oyog'ingizga og'irlik tushirmasligingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не следует переносить вес на оперированную ногу.

phrasebook.phrase: Try moving your ankle up and down.
phrasebook.translation_uz: To'pig'ingizni yuqoriga va pastga harakatlantirib ko'ring.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Попробуйте двигать лодыжкой вверх и вниз.

phrasebook.phrase: Gentle movement can improve circulation.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yengil harakat qon aylanishini yaxshilashi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Лёгкие движения могут улучшить кровообращение.

phrasebook.phrase: Movement can reduce the risk of complications.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Движение может снизить риск осложнений.

phrasebook.category: Assisting With Getting Out Of Bed
phrasebook.phrase: We'll help you sit on the edge of the bed.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizga yotoq chetiga o'tirishga yordam beramiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы поможем вам сесть на край кровати.

phrasebook.category: Assisting With Getting Out Of Bed
phrasebook.phrase: Do not get up without assistance.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не вставайте без помощи.

phrasebook.category: Assisting With Getting Out Of Bed
phrasebook.phrase: You may become dizzy when you stand up.
phrasebook.translation_ru: При вставании у вас может возникнуть головокружение.

phrasebook.category: Assisting With Getting Out Of Bed
phrasebook.phrase: I'll check your blood pressure first.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сначала я проверю ваше артериальное давление.

phrasebook.category: Assisting With Getting Out Of Bed
phrasebook.phrase: Make sure the floor is clear.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Polning bo'sh va xavfsiz ekanligiga ishonch hosil qiling.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Убедитесь, что пол свободен от препятствий.

phrasebook.category: Assisting With Getting Out Of Bed
phrasebook.phrase: Keep your walking aid within reach.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yurish vositangiz qo'l yetadigan joyda bo'lsin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Держите средство для ходьбы под рукой.

phrasebook.phrase: Maintaining your independence is important for your recovery.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сохранение самостоятельности важно для вашего восстановления.

phrasebook.phrase: You can do as much as you feel able to do.
phrasebook.translation_uz: O'zingizni qodir his qilganingizcha ishni o'zingiz bajaring.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы можете делать столько, сколько чувствуете себя в состоянии выполнить.

phrasebook.phrase: Asking for help is not a sign of weakness.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Просить о помощи — не признак слабости.

phrasebook.phrase: Our goal is to help you become more mobile gradually and safely.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bizning maqsadimiz sizni asta-sekin va xavfsiz tarzda harakatchanroq qilish.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Наша цель — помочь вам постепенно и безопасно восстановить подвижность.

phrasebook.phrase: You should ask for assistance whenever you need it.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Qachon yordam kerak bo'lsa, yordam so'rashingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы должны просить о помощи всякий раз, когда она вам необходима.

phrasebook.phrase: Please tell me if you notice any new redness.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите мне, если заметите новое покраснение.

phrasebook.phrase: Tell me if you develop any pain or swelling.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Og'riq yoki shish paydo bo'lsa, menga ayting.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите мне, если появится боль или отёк.

phrasebook.phrase: Let me know if you experience numbness.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите мне, если почувствуете онемение.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll continue checking your skin regularly.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz teringizni muntazam tekshirishda davom etamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы продолжим регулярно проверять вашу кожу.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll monitor your mobility closely.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем внимательно наблюдать за вашей подвижностью.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll adjust your care plan if necessary.
phrasebook.translation_ru: При необходимости мы скорректируем план ухода.

phrasebook.phrase: I need to check your skin, especially the areas exposed to pressure.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Teringizni, ayniqsa bosim ostida qoladigan joylarni tekshirishim kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мне нужно проверить вашу кожу, особенно участки, подвергающиеся давлению.

phrasebook.phrase: Maintaining as much independence as possible is important for your recovery.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Imkon qadar mustaqillikni saqlash tiklanishingiz uchun muhim.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сохранение максимально возможной самостоятельности важно для вашего восстановления.

phrasebook.phrase: Keeping the skin clean and dry helps prevent irritation and infection.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Terini toza va quruq saqlash tirnashish va infeksiyaning oldini olishga yordam beradi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Поддержание кожи в чистоте и сухости помогает предотвратить раздражение и инфекцию.

phrasebook.phrase: You should not put weight on your operated leg until the doctor says it is safe.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shifokor xavfsiz deb aytmaguncha operatsiya qilingan oyog'ingizga og'irlik tushirmasligingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не следует переносить вес на оперированную ногу, пока врач не разрешит это.

phrasebook.phrase: Please tell me if you notice any new redness, pain, swelling, or numbness.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yangi qizarish, og'riq, shish yoki uvishish sezsangiz, menga ayting.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите мне, если заметите новое покраснение, боль, отёк или онемение.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll continue checking your skin and mobility regularly.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz teringiz va harakatchanligingizni muntazam tekshirishda davom etamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы продолжим регулярно проверять вашу кожу и подвижность.

grammar.title: Gerund — V-ing
grammar.structure_pattern: Verb + -ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund — fe'lning -ing shakli bo'lib, gapda ot vazifasida ishlatiladi. U gapning egasi sifatida, ayrim fe'llardan va predloglardan keyin qo'llanadi. maintain → maintaining — saqlash — поддержание Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rule | Qoida | Правило Герундий — это форма глагола с окончанием -ing, которая выполняет функцию существительного. Он может использоваться в качестве подлежащего, после определённых глаголов и предлогов. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

grammar.title: Gerund As the Subject
grammar.structure_pattern: verb + V-ing (avoid, stop, keep, recommend) | verb + to + V1 (need, want, decide, advise sb to)
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund gapda ega vazifasida kelishi mumkin. Bunday holatda u ko'pincha "-ish" ma'nosini beradi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rule | Qoida | Правило Герундий может выступать в качестве подлежащего. В русском языке он часто переводится существительным или отглагольным существительным. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: A gerund can be used as the subject of a sentence. Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

examples.sentence: V-ing + verb + ...
Maintaining good hygiene is important for your recovery.
examples.translation_uz: Yaxshi gigiyenani saqlash tiklanishingiz uchun muhim.
examples.translation_ru: Поддержание хорошей гигиены важно для вашего восстановления.

examples.sentence: Regular repositioning is important for preventing pressure injuries.
examples.translation_uz: Bemorning holatini muntazam o'zgartirib turish bosim yaralarining oldini olish uchun muhim.
examples.translation_ru: Регулярное изменение положения пациента важно для профилактики пролежней.

grammar.title: Gerund After Prepositions
grammar.structure_pattern: before + V-ing | after + V-ing | without + V-ing | about + V-ing | of + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund (V-ing) ot vazifasida keladi va avoid, stop, keep, recommend fe'llari hamda predloglardan keyin ishlatiladi ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitiv (to + V1) need, want, decide, advise someone dan keyin keladi va maqsadni bildiradi ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rule | Qoida | Правило После предлогов обычно используется V-ing, а не инфинитив с to. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: After a preposition, we normally use a gerund, not an infinitive. Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

grammar.title: Before + Gerund
grammar.structure_pattern: verb + V-ing (avoid, stop, keep, recommend) | verb + to + V1 (need, want, decide, advise sb to)
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "before" dan keyin bu holatda -ing shakli ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rule | Qoida | Правило Конструкция before + V-ing используется для обозначения действия, которое происходит до другого действия. После before в данной конструкции используется форма -ing. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

examples.sentence: Use before + V-ing to describe an action that happens earlier.
Before starting, I need to check your skin.
examples.translation_ru: Перед началом мне нужно проверить вашу кожу.

examples.sentence: Before moving the patient, check the bed.
examples.translation_ru: Перед перемещением пациента проверьте кровать.

grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rule | Qoida | Правило Конструкция after + V-ing используется, когда одно действие происходит после другого. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). examples.sentence: Use after + V-ing when one action happens after another action.
After washing, we'll change your gown.
examples.translation_ru: После мытья мы сменим вашу больничную одежду.

examples.sentence: After checking the skin, we repositioned the patient.
examples.translation_uz: Terini tekshirgandan keyin bemorning holatini o'zgartirdik.
examples.translation_ru: После проверки кожи мы изменили положение пациента.

Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rule | Qoida | Правило Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). examples.sentence: Use without + V-ing to say that something happens without doing another action.
examples.translation_ru: Конструкция without + V-ing означает выполнение действия без совершения другого действия.

examples.sentence: I'll help you without putting unnecessary pressure on your operated side.
examples.translation_uz: Operatsiya qilingan tomoningizga ortiqcha bosim bermasdan sizga yordam beraman.
examples.translation_ru: Я помогу вам, не оказывая излишнего давления на оперированную сторону.

examples.sentence: Do not get up without asking for assistance.
examples.translation_ru: Не вставайте, не попросив помощи.

grammar.title: About + Gerund
grammar.structure_pattern: verb + V-ing (avoid, stop, keep, recommend) | verb + to + V1 (need, want, decide, advise sb to)
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: About predlogidan keyin biror harakat haqida gapirilganda V-ing ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rule | Qoida | Правило После предлога about, когда речь идёт о действии, используется форма V-ing. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: After the preposition about, use a gerund when talking about an action. Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

examples.sentence: I'm worried about moving my hip.
examples.translation_ru: Я беспокоюсь из-за движения бедра.

grammar.title: Gerund After Certain Verbs
grammar.structure_pattern: continue + V-ing | keep + V-ing | practice + V-ing | avoid + V-ing | finish + V-ing | consider + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ayrim fe'llardan keyin V-ing ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Rule | Qoida | Правило После некоторых глаголов используется V-ing. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

practice.module: Patient Hygiene, Mobility & Pressure Injury Prevention
practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Charlotte Reed
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.exact_diagnosis: Patient Hygiene, Mobility & Pressure Injury Prevention
medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning. I'm feeling not so good. My hip still hurts, and I find it difficult to move in bed.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: I'll check your heels, ankles, hips, lower back, and the area around your buttocks. These areas are more likely to develop pressure injuries when a patient has limited mobility.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning, Sir. How are you feeling this morning?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning. I'm feeling not so good. My hip still hurts, and I find it difficult to move in bed.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I understand. Since you had surgery, it is important to maintain good hygiene and prevent complications from staying in bed for too long. Would you like me to help you with your m…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, please. I'd like to wash, but I'm worried about moving my hip.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That's understandable. I'll help you without putting unnecessary pressure on your operated side. Before we start, I need to check your skin, especially the areas that are exposed…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What areas are you going to check?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I'll check your heels, ankles, hips, lower back, and the area around your buttocks. These areas are more likely to develop pressure injuries when a patient has limited mobility.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I see. My lower back feels a little uncomfortable.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you for telling me. Let me have a look. I can see some mild redness over your sacral area, but there is no open wound. We need to prevent the redness from getting worse.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is it serious?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Not at this stage, but we need to take it seriously. Regular repositioning can help reduce pressure on the area. I'd like to turn you slightly onto your side.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will that hurt my hip?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It may cause some discomfort, but I'll help you move slowly and carefully. Please don't try to turn yourself suddenly.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: First, bend your unaffected knee slightly. Now, try to move your shoulders and upper body together with me. Good. I'm supporting your operated leg while we turn.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: That's uncomfortable, but I can manage it.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good. We've changed your position successfully. I'm going to place a pillow between your knees to keep your hip in a safe position and reduce pressure.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: That feels more comfortable.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Excellent. Now, let's continue with your hygiene. I'll help you wash your face and upper body first. You can try washing your hands and face yourself if you feel strong enough.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'd like to do that myself.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Of course. Maintaining as much independence as possible is important for your recovery. Let me know if you start feeling tired or dizzy.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I will.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: After washing, we'll change your gown and make sure your bed is clean and dry. Keeping the skin clean and dry helps prevent irritation and infection.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Do I need to move again?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes, but only with assistance. We also need to encourage safe movement to prevent stiffness and improve circulation.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm afraid of putting weight on my operated leg.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That's understandable. You should not put weight on it until the doctor or physiotherapist says it is safe. For now, we can practice moving your unaffected leg and doing some gent…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: How often should I move my ankle?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Try moving your ankle up and down several times each hour while you're awake, unless you've been given different instructions. Gentle movement can help improve circulation and red…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What about getting out of bed?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We'll help you sit on the edge of the bed when it is safe to do so. You must not get up without assistance because you may become dizzy or lose your balance.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand.

questions_to_ask_doctor: What areas are you going to check?
Is it serious?
Will that hurt my hip?
Do I need to move again?
How often should I move my ankle?

modules.description_ru: Модуль клинического общения: Общение с пациентами и родственниками. Грамматика: Reported Speech. Эталонный диалог, 57 терминов, 50 smart-фраз, 20 грамматических тем и симуляция с виртуальным пациентом.
modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Communication with Patients & Relatives. Grammar focus: Reported Speech. Includes a reference nurse–patient dialogue, 57 vocabulary items, 50 smart phrases, 20 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. Are you the patient's relatives?

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Yes. I'm his wife, and this is his brother. We were told that he is in a coma. We're very worried about him.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I understand that this is a very difficult situation for you. Please try to remain calm. I'll explain what we know at the moment.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: The doctor told us that his condition was serious. Does that mean he is getting worse?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The doctor said that his condition was serious, but he also said that the team was monitoring him closely and providing all the necessary treatment.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: His brother said that he had complained of a severe headache yesterday. Could that have been a warning sign?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: It could have been related to his condition, but we cannot say for certain without reviewing his medical history and test results.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Before he became unconscious, he told me that he felt very dizzy and that his vision was getting blurry.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. That information is important. Did he say whether he had any difficulty speaking or moving one side of his body?

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Yes. He said that he felt weakness in his right arm, and he told me that he was having difficulty speaking.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I see. I'll make sure the doctor knows exactly what you have told me.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: His brother said that he suddenly collapsed a few minutes later. Is that correct?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. According to the information we received, he lost consciousness suddenly. The emergency team was called immediately, and he was brought here for further assessment and treatment.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: We are frightened. The doctor said that they had found something on his brain scan. What did he mean?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The doctor explained that the scan had shown an abnormality in the brain. He said that further assessment was necessary to determine exactly what had happened and what treatment would be most appropriate.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Does that mean he had a stroke?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The doctors are considering that possibility, but I don't want to give you information that has not yet been confirmed. The doctor will discuss the diagnosis with you once all the results have been reviewed.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Can he hear us?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We cannot know for certain how much a patient in a coma can hear or understand. However, you can speak to him calmly and reassure him that you are here.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: His mother told me that we should keep talking to him because he might be able to hear us.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That is understandable. You can talk to him in a calm and familiar voice. You can tell him that his family is here and that he is receiving treatment.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: What about his condition now? Has anything changed?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: His vital signs are being monitored continuously. The doctor said that his condition had remained stable over the last few hours, but he is still critically ill.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Does "stable" mean that he is improving?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. In this situation, stable means that there has not been a significant deterioration at the moment. The medical team will continue to monitor him closely.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: The doctor told us that the next twenty-four hours would be important. Is that still the case?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. He said that the next twenty-four hours would be particularly important for monitoring his neurological status and response to treatment.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: What can we do for him?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The most important thing is to remain calm and follow the medical team's instructions. You can also provide us with any information about his medical history, medications, allergies, or recent symptoms that may be relevant.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: He takes medication for high blood pressure. His doctor told him that he needed to take it regularly, but sometimes he forgot.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. Please tell me the name of the medication if you know it. I'll document the information and inform the medical team.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: We just want to know if he has a chance of recovering.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I understand why you are asking. At this stage, it is difficult to predict the outcome. The doctor will explain his prognosis after assessing his condition and response to treatment.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Thank you for explaining everything to us. We were afraid that nobody would tell us what was happening.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You're welcome. I know this is extremely stressful for you. If you have any questions, please ask. We will keep you informed about any significant changes in his condition.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Thank you. We'll stay with him.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Of course. Please speak to him calmly and let us know if you remember any other information about what happened before he lost consciousness.

phrasebook.translation_ru: Ему было трудно говорить.

phrasebook.category: Discussing Symptoms Before Loss Of Consciousness
phrasebook.phrase: He suddenly lost consciousness.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он внезапно потерял сознание.

phrasebook.phrase: The scan showed an abnormality in the brain.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə skæn ʃəʊd ən ˌæbnɔːˈmæləti ɪn ðə breɪn/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Tekshiruv miyada patologik o'zgarish borligini ko'rsatdi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сканирование выявило патологическое изменение в головном мозге.

phrasebook.phrase: Further assessment is necessary.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Необходимо дополнительное обследование.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to determine exactly what happened.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː niːd tə dɪˈtɜːmɪn ɪɡˈzæktli wɒt ˈhæpənd/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Nima sodir bo'lganini aniq aniqlashimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо точно определить, что произошло.

phrasebook.phrase: The doctors are considering the possibility of a stroke.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə ˈdɒktəz ɑː kənˈsɪdərɪŋ ðə ˌpɒsəˈbɪləti əv ə strəʊk/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Врачи рассматривают возможность инсульта.

phrasebook.phrase: The diagnosis has not yet been confirmed.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə ˌdaɪəɡˈnəʊsɪs hæz nɒt jet biːn kənˈfɜːmd/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Диагноз ещё не подтверждён.

phrasebook.phrase: You can speak to him calmly.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Siz u bilan xotirjam gaplashishingiz mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы можете спокойно с ним разговаривать.

phrasebook.phrase: You can reassure him that you are here.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /juː kən ˌriːəˈʃʊə hɪm ðæt juː ɑː hɪə/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Unga yonida ekanligingizni bildirib, uni tinchlantirishingiz mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы можете успокоить его и сказать, что вы рядом.

phrasebook.phrase: We will keep you informed.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем держать вас в курсе.

phrasebook.phrase: Please let us know if you remember anything else.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /pliːz let ʌs nəʊ ɪf juː rɪˈmembər ˈeniθɪŋ els/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yana biror narsani eslasangiz, bizga ayting.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пожалуйста, сообщите нам, если вспомните что-нибудь ещё.

phrasebook.phrase: Stable does not necessarily mean improving.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Стабильное состояние не обязательно означает улучшение.

phrasebook.phrase: There has not been a significant deterioration.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðeər hæz nɒt biːn ə sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt dɪˌtɪəriəˈreɪʃən/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Значительного ухудшения пока не наблюдается.

phrasebook.phrase: We will continue to monitor him closely.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː wɪl kənˈtɪnjuː tə ˈmɒnɪtə hɪm ˈkləʊsli/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы продолжим внимательно наблюдать за ним.

phrasebook.phrase: It is difficult to predict the outcome at this stage.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɪt ɪz ˈdɪfɪkəlt tə prɪˈdɪkt ði ˈaʊtkʌm æt ðɪs steɪdʒ/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hozirgi bosqichda natijani oldindan aytish qiyin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: На данном этапе трудно предсказать исход.

phrasebook.phrase: It is too early to give a definite prognosis.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɪt ɪz tuː ˈɜːli tə ɡɪv ə ˈdefɪnət prɒɡˈnəʊsɪs/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Aniq prognoz berish uchun hali juda erta.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пока слишком рано давать точный прогноз.

phrasebook.phrase: The doctor will discuss his prognosis with you.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə ˈdɒktə wɪl dɪˈskʌs hɪz prɒɡˈnəʊsɪs wɪð juː/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shifokor siz bilan uning prognozini muhokama qiladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Врач обсудит с вами его прогноз.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to assess his response to treatment.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː niːd tə əˈses hɪz rɪˈspɒns tə ˈtriːtmənt/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо оценить его реакцию на лечение.

phrasebook.phrase: Can you tell me about his medical history?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /kən juː tel miː əˈbaʊt hɪz ˈmedɪkəl ˈhɪstəri/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning kasallik tarixi haqida ayta olasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Можете рассказать мне о его медицинском анамнезе?

phrasebook.phrase: Does he take any regular medication?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он регулярно принимает какие-либо лекарства?

phrasebook.phrase: Does he have any known allergies?
phrasebook.translation_ru: У него есть известные аллергии?

phrasebook.phrase: Please tell me the name of the medication.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /pliːz tel miː ðə neɪm əv ðə ˌmedɪˈkeɪʃən/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пожалуйста, скажите название лекарства.

phrasebook.phrase: That information may be relevant to his treatment.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðæt ˌɪnfəˈmeɪʃən meɪ biː ˈreləvənt tə hɪz ˈtriːtmənt/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu ma'lumot uning davolashi uchun muhim bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Эта информация может иметь значение для его лечения.

phrasebook.phrase: I understand that this is a very difficult situation for you.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men bu sizlar uchun juda og'ir vaziyat ekanini tushunaman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я понимаю, что для вас это очень тяжёлая ситуация.

phrasebook.phrase: The doctor said that his condition was serious.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shifokor uning ahvoli og'ir ekanini aytdi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Врач сказал, что его состояние тяжёлое.

phrasebook.phrase: Further assessment is necessary to determine exactly what happened.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Nima sodir bo'lganini aniq aniqlash uchun qo'shimcha tekshiruv zarur.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Необходимо дополнительное обследование, чтобы точно определить, что произошло.

phrasebook.phrase: I don't want to give you information that has not yet been confirmed.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hali tasdiqlanmagan ma'lumotni sizga aytishni istamayman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я не хочу сообщать вам информацию, которая ещё не подтверждена.

phrasebook.phrase: We are monitoring him closely and providing the necessary treatment.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz uni yaqindan kuzatyapmiz va zarur davolashni ko'rsatyapmiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы внимательно наблюдаем за ним и проводим необходимое лечение.

phrasebook.phrase: The doctor will explain his prognosis after assessing his condition.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shifokor uning ahvolini baholagandan so'ng prognozini tushuntiradi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Врач объяснит прогноз после оценки его состояния.

phrasebook.phrase: Please provide us with any relevant information about his medical history.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Iltimos, uning kasallik tarixi haqida tegishli bo'lgan har qanday ma'lumotni bizga bering.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пожалуйста, сообщите нам любую важную информацию о его медицинском анамнезе.

phrasebook.phrase: You can speak to him in a calm and familiar voice.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Siz u bilan xotirjam va tanish ovozda gaplashishingiz mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы можете разговаривать с ним спокойным и знакомым голосом.

phrasebook.phrase: We will keep you informed about any significant changes.

grammar.title: Direct Speech vs Reported Speech
grammar.structure_pattern: said (that) + clause with tense shifted back | told + object + (that) … | asked + if / wh-word …
grammar.signal_words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Direct Speech — to'g'ridan-to'g'ri gap. Reported Speech — boshqa kishining gapini mazmunan yetkazish. Signal so'zlar: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Direct Speech — прямая речь. Reported Speech — косвенная речь. Сигнальные слова: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Reported Speech relays what someone said without quoting: "My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction". Tenses usually shift back (is → was, has → had, will → would); questions use "if" or a wh-word with statement word order. Signal words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.

grammar.title: Key Formula
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + said + (that) + reported clause | Subject + told + object + (that) + reported clause
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Statement — Darak gap
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Statement — Darak gap
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Structure: Subject + said + (that) + reported clause | Subject + told + object + (that) + reported clause.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs
grammar.structure_pattern: modal (can / could / may / might / must / should / have to) + V1
grammar.signal_words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Modal fe'llar gapga munosabat qo'shadi: ehtimollik (may, might, could), imkoniyat/ruxsat (can, could), maslahat (should, ought to), majburiyat (must, have to) va taqiq (mustn't). Modaldan keyin fe'l doim asosiy shaklda (V1) keladi. Signal so'zlar: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы передают отношение говорящего: возможность (may, might, could), способность/разрешение (can, could), совет (should, ought to), обязанность (must, have to) и запрет (mustn't). После модального глагола всегда стоит начальная форма. Сигнальные слова: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Modal verbs add the speaker's attitude: possibility (may, might, could), ability/permission (can, could), advice (should, ought to), obligation (must, have to) and prohibition (mustn't). The main verb after a modal is always the base form. Signal words: possibility, advice, necessity, permission.

grammar.title: Time Expressions (since / for / ago)
grammar.structure_pattern: since + starting point (since yesterday) | for + period (for three days) | period + ago (two hours ago)
grammar.signal_words: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Reported Speech'da vaqt va joy bildiruvchi so'zlar ham o'zgarishi mumkin. Signal so'zlar: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Since» указывает точку начала («since yesterday»), «for» — продолжительность («for three days»), «ago» — отсчёт назад от настоящего («two hours ago»). Точное время («at about 7:15 this morning») критично при инсульте и других неотложных состояниях. Сигнальные слова: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Since" gives the starting point ("since yesterday"), "for" the length of time ("for three days") and "ago" counts back from now ("two hours ago"). Exact times ("at about 7:15 this morning") are essential in time-critical conditions such as stroke. Signal words: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.

grammar.title: Wh-Questions
grammar.structure_pattern: asked + question word + subject + verb
grammar.signal_words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Yes/No savollar yordamchi fe'l bilan boshlanadi ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-savollar so'roq so'zi bilan ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Ochiq savollar hikoyani, yopiq savollar aniq detallarni yig'adi. Signal so'zlar: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Общие вопросы начинаются со вспомогательного глагола («Do you have any allergies?», «Have you had a fever?»); специальные — с вопросительного слова («How long have you had the pain?», «Where exactly does it hurt?»). Открытые вопросы собирают историю, закрытые — уточняют детали. Сигнальные слова: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Yes/No questions start with an auxiliary ("Do you have any allergies?", "Have you had a fever?"); Wh-questions add a question word ("How long have you had the pain?", "Where exactly does it hurt?"). Open questions gather the story, closed questions confirm details. Signal words: what, when, where, how long, how often, do you, have you.

grammar.title: Reported Commands
grammar.structure_pattern: tell + object + to + V1 | tell + object + not to + V1
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund (V-ing) ot vazifasida keladi va avoid, stop, keep, recommend fe'llari hamda predloglardan keyin ishlatiladi ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitiv (to + V1) need, want, decide, advise someone dan keyin keladi va maqsadni bildiradi ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Герундий (V-ing) выступает как существительное после глаголов avoid, stop, keep, recommend и предлогов («Avoid eating before the test»). Инфинитив (to + V1) стоит после need, want, decide, advise someone и выражает цель («We need to run some tests», «in order to rule out appendicitis»). Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

grammar.title: Dialogdagi Reported Speech Tahlili
grammar.structure_pattern: said (that) + clause with tense shifted back | told + object + (that) … | asked + if / wh-word …

grammar.title: Reported Speech
grammar.structure_pattern: said (that) + clause with tense shifted back | told + object + (that) … | asked + if / wh-word …
grammar.signal_words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Tibbiy muloqotda Reported Speech juda muhim, chunki hamshira: bemorning aytganlarini shifokorga yetkazadi; qarindoshlarning bergan ma'lumotlarini qayd qiladi; shifokorning tushuntirishlarini bemor yoki qarindoshlarga yetkazadi; boshqa tibbiyot xodimining ko'rsatmalarini yetkazadi; bemorning oldingi shikoyatlarini hujjatlashtiradi. Signal so'zlar: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Косвенная речь передаёт чужие слова без цитирования: «My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction». Времена обычно сдвигаются назад (is → was, has → had, will → would); вопросы передаются через «if» или вопросительное слово с прямым порядком слов. Сигнальные слова: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Reported Speech relays what someone said without quoting: "My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction". Tenses usually shift back (is → was, has → had, will → would); questions use "if" or a wh-word with statement word order. Signal words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.

practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the RELATIVE.

patient_profile.name: Jack Turner
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Yes. I'm his wife, and this is his brother. We were told that he is in a coma. We're very worried about him.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good afternoon. Are you the patient's relatives?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I'm his wife, and this is his brother. We were told that he is in a coma. We're very worried about him.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I understand that this is a very difficult situation for you. Please try to remain calm. I'll explain what we know at the moment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: The doctor told us that his condition was serious. Does that mean he is getting worse?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: The doctor said that his condition was serious, but he also said that the team was monitoring him closely and providing all the necessary treatment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: His brother said that he had complained of a severe headache yesterday. Could that have been a warning sign?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It could have been related to his condition, but we cannot say for certain without reviewing his medical history and test results.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Before he became unconscious, he told me that he felt very dizzy and that his vision was getting blurry.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. That information is important. Did he say whether he had any difficulty speaking or moving one side of his body?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. He said that he felt weakness in his right arm, and he told me that he was having difficulty speaking.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I see. I'll make sure the doctor knows exactly what you have told me.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: His brother said that he suddenly collapsed a few minutes later. Is that correct?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. According to the information we received, he lost consciousness suddenly. The emergency team was called immediately, and he was brought here for further assessment and treatm…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: We are frightened. The doctor said that they had found something on his brain scan. What did he mean?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: The doctor explained that the scan had shown an abnormality in the brain. He said that further assessment was necessary to determine exactly what had happened and what treatment w…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Does that mean he had a stroke?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: The doctors are considering that possibility, but I don't want to give you information that has not yet been confirmed. The doctor will discuss the diagnosis with you once all the…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Can he hear us?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We cannot know for certain how much a patient in a coma can hear or understand. However, you can speak to him calmly and reassure him that you are here.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: His mother told me that we should keep talking to him because he might be able to hear us.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That is understandable. You can talk to him in a calm and familiar voice. You can tell him that his family is here and that he is receiving treatment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What about his condition now? Has anything changed?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: His vital signs are being monitored continuously. The doctor said that his condition had remained stable over the last few hours, but he is still critically ill.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Does "stable" mean that he is improving?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Not necessarily. In this situation, stable means that there has not been a significant deterioration at the moment. The medical team will continue to monitor him closely.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: The doctor told us that the next twenty-four hours would be important. Is that still the case?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. He said that the next twenty-four hours would be particularly important for monitoring his neurological status and response to treatment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What can we do for him?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: The most important thing is to remain calm and follow the medical team's instructions. You can also provide us with any information about his medical history, medications, allergi…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He takes medication for high blood pressure. His doctor told him that he needed to take it regularly, but sometimes he forgot.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. Please tell me the name of the medication if you know it. I'll document the information and inform the medical team.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: We just want to know if he has a chance of recovering.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Does that mean he is getting worse?
Could that have been a warning sign?
Is that correct?
What did he mean?
Does that mean he had a stroke?

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Discharge Planning & Patient Education. Grammar focus: Future Forms & Plans. Includes a reference nurse–patient dialogue, 49 vocabulary items, 56 smart phrases, 18 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning, Mr. Miller. I've come to talk to you about your discharge plan and how you'll manage your recovery at home.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning. That's good to know. I'm feeling much better now.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That's good to hear. The doctor has reviewed your condition, and you're likely to go home tomorrow if everything remains stable.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: That's great news. What will I need to do when I get home?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Before you leave, we're going to go through your discharge instructions carefully. I'll explain your medications, diet, activity level, wound care, and follow-up appointments.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need to continue taking all the medications I was given in the hospital?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You'll need to continue taking the medications listed on your discharge prescription. Some medicines will be stopped, while others will be continued at home.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm sometimes worried that I'll forget when to take them.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Don't worry. I'm going to give you a written medication schedule. We'll also review each medicine together before you leave.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I have to take the pain medication regularly?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You should take it exactly as prescribed. If your pain remains mild, you may not need to take it as often, but you shouldn't change the dose without speaking to your doctor.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What about my wound? It still looks a little red.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'm going to check the wound before you go home. You'll need to keep the area clean and dry, and you'll have to change the dressing according to the instructions we give you.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I be able to change the dressing myself?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes, you're going to learn how to do it safely. I'll demonstrate the procedure first, and then I'll ask you to show me how you would change the dressing.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right. What should I do if the wound becomes more painful?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: If the pain becomes significantly worse, or if you notice increasing redness, swelling, pus, or a fever, you should contact your doctor immediately.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. Am I going to have any restrictions on physical activity?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: For the first few days, you're going to need to take it easy. You'll be able to walk short distances, but you shouldn't lift heavy objects or do strenuous exercise.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: When will I be able to return to my normal activities?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: That will depend on how quickly you recover. Your doctor will assess your progress at the follow-up appointment and will tell you when you can gradually increase your activity.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: When is my follow-up appointment?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You're seeing your doctor next Monday at 10 a.m. The appointment has already been arranged.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good. Will I need any further tests?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Your doctor may order some blood tests at your follow-up appointment. If they are necessary, the doctor will explain them to you.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What should I do about my diet?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: For now, you're going to follow a balanced diet and drink enough fluids unless your doctor has given you different instructions. Try to avoid very salty and highly processed foods while you're recovering.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'll do my best. Will I be completely recovered by next month?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: It's difficult to predict exactly. If your recovery continues as expected, you should be feeling considerably better by then. By the time you attend your follow-up appointment, we'll have a better idea of how well you're recovering.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You're very welcome. Remember, if you have any concerns after going home, contact your healthcare provider rather than changing your treatment on your own.

vocabulary.translation_uz: kelajakdagi ma'lum vaqtda davom etayotgan ish

phrasebook.phrase: I've come to talk to you about your discharge plan.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪv kʌm tə tɔːk tə juː əˈbaʊt jɔːr ˈdɪstʃɑːrdʒ plæn/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men siz bilan shifoxonadan chiqish rejangiz haqida gaplashgani keldim.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я пришёл(ла) поговорить с вами о плане выписки.

phrasebook.phrase: You're likely to go home tomorrow.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вероятно, завтра вы сможете уйти домой.

phrasebook.phrase: Before you leave, we're going to review your discharge instructions carefully.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ketishingizdan oldin chiqarish bo'yicha ko'rsatmalarni diqqat bilan ko'rib chiqamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Перед выпиской мы внимательно рассмотрим инструкции.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll make sure you understand the instructions.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiːl meɪk ʃʊər juː ˌʌndəˈstænd ði ɪnˈstrʌkʃənz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы убедимся, что вы поняли инструкции.

phrasebook.phrase: You'll need to continue taking your medication.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /juːl niːd tə kənˈtɪnjuː ˈteɪkɪŋ jɔːr ˌmedɪˈkeɪʃən/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Dorilaringizni qabul qilishni davom ettirishingiz kerak bo'ladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам нужно будет продолжить принимать лекарства.

phrasebook.phrase: Take it exactly as prescribed.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Принимайте его точно по назначению.

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to give you a written medication schedule.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪm ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ɡɪv juː ə ˈrɪtn ˌmedɪˈkeɪʃən ˈʃedjuːl/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Men sizga dorilarni qabul qilish jadvalini yozma shaklda beraman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я дам вам письменный график приёма лекарств.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll review each medication together.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Har bir dorini birgalikda ko'rib chiqamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы вместе рассмотрим каждое лекарство.

phrasebook.phrase: Don't change the dose without speaking to your doctor.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /dəʊnt tʃeɪndʒ ðə dəʊs wɪˈðaʊt ˈspiːkɪŋ tə jɔːr ˈdɒktə(r)/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не изменяйте дозу без консультации с врачом.

phrasebook.phrase: Some medicines will be stopped.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Некоторые лекарства будут отменены.

phrasebook.phrase: Other medicines will be continued at home.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ˈʌðə ˈmedɪsɪnz wɪl biː kənˈtɪnjuːd ət həʊm/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Boshqa dorilarni uyda ham davom ettirasiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Другие лекарства нужно будет продолжить принимать дома.

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to check the wound before you go home.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪm ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə tʃek ðə wuːnd bɪˈfɔːr juː ɡəʊ həʊm/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я осмотрю рану перед тем, как вы уйдёте домой.

phrasebook.phrase: You'll need to keep the area clean and dry.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /juːl niːd tə kiːp ði ˈeəriə kliːn ænd draɪ/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu joyni toza va quruq saqlashingiz kerak bo'ladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам нужно будет держать эту область чистой и сухой.

phrasebook.phrase: You'll have to change the dressing regularly.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /juːl hæv tə tʃeɪndʒ ðə ˈdresɪŋ ˈreɡjələli/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам нужно будет регулярно менять повязку.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll demonstrate the procedure first.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сначала я продемонстрирую процедуру.

phrasebook.phrase: Show me how you would change the dressing.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ʃəʊ miː haʊ juː wʊd tʃeɪndʒ ðə ˈdresɪŋ/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bog'lamni qanday almashtirishingizni menga ko'rsatib bering.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Покажите мне, как вы будете менять повязку.

phrasebook.phrase: If the pain becomes significantly worse...
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если боль значительно усилится...

phrasebook.phrase: If you notice increasing redness...
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если вы заметите усиливающееся покраснение...

phrasebook.phrase: If you develop a fever...
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если у вас появится температура...

phrasebook.phrase: You should contact your doctor immediately.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам следует немедленно обратиться к врачу.

phrasebook.phrase: These symptoms require urgent medical attention.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bu belgilar shoshilinch tibbiy yordamni talab qiladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Эти симптомы требуют неотложной медицинской помощи.

phrasebook.phrase: You're going to need to take it easy.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /jʊər ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə niːd tə teɪk ɪt ˈiːzi/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам нужно будет поберечь себя.

phrasebook.phrase: You'll be able to walk short distances.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /juːl bi ˈeɪbəl tə wɔːk ʃɔːrt ˈdɪstənsɪz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы сможете ходить на короткие расстояния.

phrasebook.phrase: You shouldn't lift heavy objects.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам не следует поднимать тяжёлые предметы.

phrasebook.phrase: Avoid strenuous exercise for now.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пока избегайте интенсивных физических нагрузок.

phrasebook.phrase: You can gradually increase your activity.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы можете постепенно увеличивать физическую активность.

phrasebook.phrase: You're seeing your doctor next Monday.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Siz kelasi dushanba shifokoringiz qabuliga borasiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы идёте к врачу в следующий понедельник.

phrasebook.phrase: The appointment has already been arranged.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Приём уже назначен.

phrasebook.phrase: You may need further tests.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizga qo'shimcha tekshiruvlar kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам могут понадобиться дополнительные обследования.

phrasebook.phrase: Your doctor may order some blood tests.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /jɔːr ˈdɒktə(r) meɪ ˈɔːdə(r) sʌm blʌd tests/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shifokoringiz ba'zi qon tahlillarini buyurishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Врач может назначить анализы крови.

phrasebook.phrase: Your doctor will assess your progress.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Врач оценит динамику вашего состояния.

phrasebook.phrase: Follow a balanced diet.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Соблюдайте сбалансированную диету.

phrasebook.phrase: Drink enough fluids.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пейте достаточно жидкости.

phrasebook.phrase: Try to avoid highly processed foods.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yuqori darajada qayta ishlangan mahsulotlardan saqlanishga harakat qiling.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Старайтесь избегать продуктов высокой степени переработки.

phrasebook.phrase: Follow your doctor's dietary instructions.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shifokoringizning ovqatlanish bo'yicha ko'rsatmalariga rioya qiling.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Следуйте рекомендациям врача по питанию.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll explain everything before you leave.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я всё объясню вам перед выпиской.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll make sure you understand how to take your medication.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪl meɪk ʃʊər juː ˌʌndəˈstænd haʊ tə teɪk jɔːr ˌmedɪˈkeɪʃən/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Dorilaringizni qanday qabul qilishni tushunganingizga ishonch hosil qilaman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я убедюсь, что вы понимаете, как принимать лекарства.

phrasebook.phrase: I'd like you to show me how you would do it.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪd laɪk juː tə ʃəʊ miː haʊ juː wʊd duː ɪt/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Buni qanday bajarishingizni menga ko'rsatishingizni istayman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я хочу, чтобы вы показали мне, как вы это будете выполнять.

phrasebook.phrase: Do you have any questions before you leave?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /duː juː hæv eni ˈkwestʃənz bɪˈfɔːr juː liːv/
phrasebook.translation_ru: У вас есть вопросы перед выпиской?

phrasebook.phrase: Don't worry. We'll go through everything together.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /dəʊnt ˈwʌri wiːl ɡəʊ θruː ˈevriθɪŋ təˈɡeðə(r)/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Xavotir olmang. Hammasini birgalikda ko'rib chiqamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не волнуйтесь. Мы всё вместе разберём.

phrasebook.phrase: You should contact us if you have any concerns.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /juː ʃʊd ˈkɒntækt ʌs ɪf juː hæv eni kənˈsɜːrnz/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar biror xavotiringiz bo'lsa, biz bilan bog'lanishingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Свяжитесь с нами, если у вас возникнут какие-либо опасения.

phrasebook.phrase: Contact your healthcare provider if your symptoms worsen.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ˈkɒntækt jɔː ˈhelθkeər prəˈvaɪdə(r) ɪf jɔː ˈsɪmptəmz ˈwɜːrsən/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Simptomlaringiz kuchaysa, tibbiyot xodimingiz bilan bog'laning.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Свяжитесь с медицинским работником, если ваши симптомы усилятся.

phrasebook.phrase: Do not change your treatment on your own.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /duː nɒt tʃeɪndʒ jɔːr ˈtriːtmənt ɒn jɔːr əʊn/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не изменяйте лечение самостоятельно.

phrasebook.phrase: Contact your doctor rather than changing your treatment yourself.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ˈkɒntækt jɔːr ˈdɒktə(r) ˈrɑːðə(r) ðæn ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ jɔːr ˈtriːtmənt jɔːrˈself/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Davolashingizni o'zingizcha o'zgartirish o'rniga shifokoringiz bilan bog'laning.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Свяжитесь с врачом, вместо того чтобы самостоятельно изменять лечение.

phrasebook.phrase: You'll need to continue taking your medication as prescribed.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Dorilaringizni buyurilganidek qabul qilishni davom ettirishingiz kerak bo'ladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам нужно будет продолжать принимать лекарства согласно назначению.

phrasebook.phrase: Take the medication exactly as prescribed.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Принимайте лекарство точно по назначению.

phrasebook.phrase: You'll need to keep the wound clean and dry.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yarani toza va quruq saqlashingiz kerak bo'ladi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам нужно будет держать рану чистой и сухой.

phrasebook.phrase: If you notice increasing redness, swelling, pus, or a fever, contact your doctor immediately.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar qizarish, shish, yiring yoki isitma paydo bo'lsa, darhol shifokoringizga murojaat qiling.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если вы заметите усиливающееся покраснение, отёк, гной или повышение температуры, немедленно обратитесь к врачу.

phrasebook.phrase: You'll be able to gradually return to your normal activities.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Siz odatdagi faoliyatingizga asta-sekin qayta olasiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы сможете постепенно вернуться к обычной деятельности.

phrasebook.phrase: You shouldn't lift heavy objects or do strenuous exercise for now.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Hozircha og'ir narsalarni ko'tarmasligingiz va kuchli jismoniy mashqlarni bajarmasligingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пока вам не следует поднимать тяжёлые предметы или выполнять интенсивные физические упражнения.

phrasebook.phrase: Your doctor will assess your progress at the follow-up appointment.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shifokoringiz keyingi nazorat ko'rigida tiklanish jarayoningizni baholaydi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Врач оценит динамику вашего состояния на контрольном приёме.

phrasebook.phrase: If your symptoms get worse, you should contact your doctor immediately.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar simptomlaringiz kuchaysa, darhol shifokoringizga murojaat qilishingiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если ваши симптомы усилятся, вам следует немедленно обратиться к врачу.

phrasebook.phrase: By the end of this session, you'll have reviewed all your medications and their doses.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ushbu mashg'ulot oxiriga kelib, barcha dorilaringiz va ularning dozalarini ko'rib chiqqan bo'lasiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: К концу этой консультации вы уже ознакомитесь со всеми лекарствами и их дозировками.

phrasebook.phrase: If everything remains stable, you'll be ready for discharge tomorrow.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Agar holatingiz barqaror bo'lib qolsa, ertaga shifoxonadan chiqishga tayyor bo'lasiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Если ваше состояние останется стабильным, завтра вы будете готовы к выписке.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll continue monitoring you today.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biz bugun sizni kuzatishda davom etamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сегодня мы продолжим наблюдать за вами.

phrasebook.phrase: Contact your healthcare provider rather than changing your treatment on your own.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Davolashingizni o'zingizcha o'zgartirish o'rniga, tibbiyot xodimingiz bilan bog'laning.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Свяжитесь с медицинским работником, вместо того чтобы самостоятельно изменять лечение.

grammar.title: Future Forms
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: haqida gapirish uchun bir nechta Future shakllari ishlatilgan.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: haqida gapirish uchun bir nechta Future shakllari ishlatilgan.

examples.sentence: will + V1
be going to + V1

grammar.title: Will + Verb
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + will + V1 | Subject + will not (won't) + V1
grammar.signal_words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: will kelajakdagi ish-harakatni bildirish uchun ishlatiladi. Ko'pincha qaror, va'da, taklif, bashorat yoki kelajakdagi natijani ifodalaydi. Signal so'zlar: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Will используется для обозначения будущего действия, решения, обещания, предложения или предположения о будущем. Сигнальные слова: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.

examples.sentence: Will + subject + V1?
What will I need to do when I get home?
examples.translation_uz: Uyga borganimdan keyin nimalar qilishim kerak bo'ladi?

examples.sentence: The doctor will review your condition tomorrow.
examples.translation_ru: Врач завтра оценит ваше состояние.

examples.sentence: We will monitor your condition closely.
examples.translation_ru: Мы будем внимательно наблюдать за вашим состоянием.

examples.sentence: I'll explain your discharge instructions.
