examples.translation_ru: Я объясню вам инструкции по выписке.

grammar.title: Will — Bashorat
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + will + V1
grammar.signal_words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: will kelajak haqida taxmin yoki bashorat qilish uchun ham ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Will» выражает решение, принятое в момент речи, обещание, прогноз и успокоение пациента: «I will give you something for the pain», «The swelling will go down in a few days». Сигнальные слова: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.

examples.sentence: You will probably feel better in a few days.
examples.translation_uz: Bir necha kundan keyin o'zingizni ehtimol yaxshiroq his qilasiz.
examples.translation_ru: Вероятно, через несколько дней вы будете чувствовать себя лучше.

examples.sentence: Your pain will gradually improve.
examples.translation_ru: Ваша боль постепенно уменьшится.

examples.sentence: Your mobility will improve with regular exercise.
examples.translation_ru: Ваша подвижность улучшится при регулярных упражнениях.

grammar.title: Be Going to + Verb
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + am/is/are + going to + V1
grammar.signal_words: now, next, first, then
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: be going to oldindan qabul qilingan reja yoki yaqin kelajakda amalga oshiriladigan rejalashtirilgan ishni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: now, next, first, then.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: be going to используется для заранее запланированных действий или намерений. Сигнальные слова: now, next, first, then.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Be going to" describes a plan or intention and something about to happen: "I am going to examine your abdomen now", "We are going to run some tests". Clinicians use it to announce each step of the examination. Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: now, next, first, then.

examples.sentence: We're going to go through your discharge instructions carefully.
examples.translation_uz: Biz shifoxonadan chiqish bo'yicha ko'rsatmalarni diqqat bilan ko'rib chiqamiz.
examples.translation_ru: Мы внимательно разберём инструкции по выписке.

examples.sentence: I'm going to give you a written medication schedule.
examples.translation_uz: Men sizga dorilarni qabul qilish jadvalini yozma shaklda beraman.
examples.translation_ru: Я дам вам письменный график приёма лекарств.

examples.sentence: I'm going to check the wound before you go home.
examples.translation_ru: Я осмотрю вашу рану перед выпиской домой.

grammar.title: Will vs Be Going to
grammar.structure_pattern: will + V1 | will not (won't) + V1 | am / is / are + going to + V1
grammar.signal_words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: WILL: kelajakdagi qaror/bashorat BE GOING TO: oldindan rejalashtirilgan ish WILL: Men tushuntirib beraman. BE GOING TO: Men tushuntirishni rejalashtirganman. Signal so'zlar: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Will» выражает решение, принятое в момент речи, обещание, прогноз и успокоение пациента: «I will give you something for the pain», «The swelling will go down in a few days». «Be going to» выражает план, намерение или то, что вот-вот произойдёт: «I am going to examine your abdomen now», «We are going to run some tests». Врач так объявляет каждый шаг осмотра. Сигнальные слова: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". "Be going to" describes a plan or intention and something about to happen: "I am going to examine your abdomen now", "We are going to run some tests". Clinicians use it to announce each step of the examination. Signal words: tomorrow, next week, soon, in a few minutes, I think.

examples.sentence: I'll explain it.
I'm going to explain it.
I'll call the doctor.
I'm going to call the doctor.

grammar.title: Present Continuous for Future Arrangements
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + am/is/are + V-ing + future time
grammar.signal_words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Continuous faqat hozir sodir bo'layotgan ishni emas, kelajakdagi aniq kelishilgan rejani ham bildirishi mumkin. Kelajak uchun aniq belgilangan uchrashuv, tashrif yoki reja haqida gapirganda ishlatiladi. Bu yerda are seeing — Present Continuous, lekin kelajakdagi aniq reja. Signal so'zlar: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Continuous используется для заранее договорённых и организованных действий в будущем. Сигнальные слова: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. Signal words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.

examples.sentence: You're seeing your doctor next Monday at 10 a.m.

grammar.title: Present Continuous vs Be Going to
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + V-ing | am / is / are + going to + V1
grammar.signal_words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ikkalasi ham kelajakdagi rejani bildirishi mumkin, lekin farq bor. Signal so'zlar: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Continuous описывает действие в момент речи или временную, меняющуюся ситуацию: «His condition is getting worse», «I am going to examine you now». Также используется для ближайших действий врача. «Be going to» выражает план, намерение или то, что вот-вот произойдёт: «I am going to examine your abdomen now», «We are going to run some tests». Врач так объявляет каждый шаг осмотра. Сигнальные слова: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. "Be going to" describes a plan or intention and something about to happen: "I am going to examine your abdomen now", "We are going to run some tests". Clinicians use it to announce each step of the examination. Signal words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.

grammar.title: Future Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + will be + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: by tomorrow, by the end of, at this time tomorrow
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Kelajakdagi ma'lum bir vaqtda davom etayotgan ish-harakatni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: by tomorrow, by the end of, at this time tomorrow.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Future Continuous обозначает действие, которое будет происходить в определённый момент в будущем. Сигнальные слова: by tomorrow, by the end of, at this time tomorrow.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Future Perfect ("will have + V3") says an action will be completed before a future moment; Future Continuous ("will be + V-ing") describes an action in progress at a future time: "By tomorrow you will have received the results", "The nurse will be monitoring you overnight". "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: by tomorrow, by the end of, at this time tomorrow.

grammar.title: Dialogue Grammatical Analysis
grammar.structure_pattern: are likely to + V1 | will + need + to V | be going to + V1 | will + be able to + V1 | by the time + Present Simple | will have + noun | will have + V3 | will + continue + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund (V-ing) ot vazifasida keladi va avoid, stop, keep, recommend fe'llari hamda predloglardan keyin ishlatiladi ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitiv (to + V1) need, want, decide, advise someone dan keyin keladi va maqsadni bildiradi ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). "Will" hozir qabul qilingan qaror, va'da, bashorat va bemorni tinchlantirishni ifodalaydi: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Герундий (V-ing) выступает как существительное после глаголов avoid, stop, keep, recommend и предлогов («Avoid eating before the test»). Инфинитив (to + V1) стоит после need, want, decide, advise someone и выражает цель («We need to run some tests», «in order to rule out appendicitis»). «Will» выражает решение, принятое в момент речи, обещание, прогноз и успокоение пациента: «I will give you something for the pain», «The swelling will go down in a few days». Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Mr. Miller
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning. That's good to know. I'm feeling much better now.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: That's good to hear. The doctor has reviewed your condition, and you're likely to go home tomorrow if everything remains stable.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning, Mr. Miller. I've come to talk to you about your discharge plan and how you'll manage your recovery at home.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning. That's good to know. I'm feeling much better now.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That's good to hear. The doctor has reviewed your condition, and you're likely to go home tomorrow if everything remains stable.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: That's great news. What will I need to do when I get home?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Before you leave, we're going to go through your discharge instructions carefully. I'll explain your medications, diet, activity level, wound care, and follow-up appointments.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I need to continue taking all the medications I was given in the hospital?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You'll need to continue taking the medications listed on your discharge prescription. Some medicines will be stopped, while others will be continued at home.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm sometimes worried that I'll forget when to take them.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Don't worry. I'm going to give you a written medication schedule. We'll also review each medicine together before you leave.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I have to take the pain medication regularly?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You should take it exactly as prescribed. If your pain remains mild, you may not need to take it as often, but you shouldn't change the dose without speaking to your doctor.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What about my wound? It still looks a little red.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I'm going to check the wound before you go home. You'll need to keep the area clean and dry, and you'll have to change the dressing according to the instructions we give you.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I be able to change the dressing myself?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes, you're going to learn how to do it safely. I'll demonstrate the procedure first, and then I'll ask you to show me how you would change the dressing.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right. What should I do if the wound becomes more painful?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: If the pain becomes significantly worse, or if you notice increasing redness, swelling, pus, or a fever, you should contact your doctor immediately.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand. Am I going to have any restrictions on physical activity?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: For the first few days, you're going to need to take it easy. You'll be able to walk short distances, but you shouldn't lift heavy objects or do strenuous exercise.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: When will I be able to return to my normal activities?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That will depend on how quickly you recover. Your doctor will assess your progress at the follow-up appointment and will tell you when you can gradually increase your activity.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: When is my follow-up appointment?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You're seeing your doctor next Monday at 10 a.m. The appointment has already been arranged.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good. Will I need any further tests?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Your doctor may order some blood tests at your follow-up appointment. If they are necessary, the doctor will explain them to you.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What should I do about my diet?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: For now, you're going to follow a balanced diet and drink enough fluids unless your doctor has given you different instructions. Try to avoid very salty and highly processed foods…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'll do my best. Will I be completely recovered by next month?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It's difficult to predict exactly. If your recovery continues as expected, you should be feeling considerably better by then. By the time you attend your follow-up appointment, we…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

questions_to_ask_doctor: What will I need to do when I get home?
Will I need to continue taking all the medications I was given in the hospital?
Will I have to take the pain medication regularly?
What about my wound?
Will I be able to change the dressing myself?

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Acute Allergic Reactions & Anaphylaxis. Grammar focus: Articles & Determiners. Includes a reference nurse–patient dialogue, 37 vocabulary items, 45 smart phrases, 16 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The patient is stable, Doctor. His vital signs are within the normal range, and the sterile field is ready. Surgeon: Good. Make sure that all the required instruments are available.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: All the instruments are prepared and within reach. Surgeon: Pass me the scalpel, please.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Here you are, Doctor. Surgeon: Thank you. I am making the incision now. Keep the operative field clearly visible.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The operative field is clear, Doctor. Surgeon: Good. Pass me the retractor.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Here is the retractor. Surgeon: Thank you. Retract the tissue gently and maintain a clear view of the surgical site.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Understood, Doctor. Surgeon: I can see the appendix. It is enlarged and inflamed.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The appendix appears significantly inflamed. Surgeon: Yes. There is no obvious perforation. Prepare a sterile specimen container for the appendix.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The specimen container is ready, Doctor. Surgeon: Good. Pass me a small clamp.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Here is the clamp. Surgeon: Thank you. I am carefully separating the appendix from the surrounding tissue.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The surgical field remains clear. Surgeon: Good. Prepare the appropriate sutures for closure.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The sutures are prepared and ready. Surgeon: Excellent. I am now securing the base of the appendix.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The clamp is in position, Doctor. Surgeon: Good. I am going to remove the appendix now.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The appendix has been removed. Surgeon: Place the specimen in the sterile container and make sure it is labelled correctly.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The specimen has been placed in the container and labelled. Surgeon: Now inspect the operative field carefully for any bleeding.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: There is no significant bleeding. The operative field is clear. Surgeon: Good. Prepare the instruments for wound closure.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The instruments are ready. Surgeon: Pass me the suture, please.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Here you are, Doctor. Surgeon: Thank you. I am closing the incision now.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The wound edges are coming together well. Surgeon: Good. Once the closure is complete, perform the final instrument and swab count.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I will, Doctor. Surgeon: The closure is complete. Check the operative site one more time.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The operative site is clean, and there is no significant bleeding. Surgeon: Excellent. Now confirm the final count.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The final count is correct. All instruments and swabs are accounted for. Surgeon: Good. Document the procedure and the condition of the appendix in the operative notes.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The procedure and the specimen details will be documented, Doctor. Surgeon: Excellent. The appendectomy is complete. Prepare the patient for transfer to the recovery area.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Understood, Doctor. The patient remains stable.

phrasebook.phrase: The patient is stable.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Состояние пациента стабильное.

phrasebook.phrase: The vital signs are within the normal range.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə ˈvaɪtəl saɪnz ɑːr wɪˈðɪn ðə ˈnɔːrməl reɪndʒ/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Жизненные показатели находятся в пределах нормы.

phrasebook.phrase: The sterile field is ready.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Стерильное поле готово.

phrasebook.phrase: Keep the operative field clearly visible.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Operatsion maydonni aniq ko'rinadigan holatda saqlang.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Обеспечьте хорошую видимость операционного поля.

phrasebook.phrase: Retract the tissue gently.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Осторожно отведите ткани.

phrasebook.phrase: Maintain a clear view of the surgical site.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /meɪnˈteɪn ə klɪr vjuː əv ðə ˈsɜːrdʒɪkəl saɪt/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Обеспечьте хороший обзор операционной области.

phrasebook.phrase: The appendix appears significantly inflamed.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Аппендикс выглядит значительно воспалённым.

phrasebook.phrase: There is no obvious perforation.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Явных признаков перфорации нет.

phrasebook.phrase: Prepare a sterile specimen container.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Подготовьте стерильный контейнер для образца.

phrasebook.phrase: Separate the appendix from the surrounding tissue.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ˈsepəreɪt ði əˈpendɪks frəm ðə səˈraʊndɪŋ ˈtɪʃuː/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Отделите аппендикс от окружающих тканей.

phrasebook.phrase: Secure the base of the appendix.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Зафиксируйте основание аппендикса.

phrasebook.phrase: Remove the appendix.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Удалите аппендикс.

phrasebook.phrase: Place the specimen in the sterile container.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /pleɪs ðə ˈspesɪmən ɪn ðə ˈsterəl kənˌteɪnər/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Поместите образец в стерильный контейнер.

phrasebook.phrase: Make sure it is labelled correctly.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Убедитесь, что он правильно промаркирован.

phrasebook.phrase: Inspect the operative field carefully.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Внимательно осмотрите операционное поле.

phrasebook.phrase: There is no significant bleeding.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Значительного кровотечения нет.

phrasebook.phrase: Prepare the instruments for wound closure.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Подготовьте инструменты для закрытия раны.

phrasebook.phrase: The wound edges are coming together well.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə wuːnd ˈedʒɪz ɑːr ˈkʌmɪŋ təˈɡeðər wel/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Края раны хорошо сближаются.

phrasebook.phrase: Perform the final instrument and swab count.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /pərˈfɔːrm ðə ˈfaɪnəl ˈɪnstrəmənt ənd swɑːb kaʊnt/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yakuniy asboblar va tamponlar hisobini o'tkazing.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Проведите окончательный подсчёт инструментов и салфеток.

phrasebook.phrase: All instruments and swabs are accounted for.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɔːl ˈɪnstrəmənts ənd swɑːbz ɑːr əˈkaʊntɪd fɔːr/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Barcha asboblar va tamponlar to'liq hisobda.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Все инструменты и салфетки на месте.

phrasebook.phrase: The appendectomy is complete.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Аппендэктомия завершена.

phrasebook.phrase: Prepare the patient for transfer.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Подготовьте пациента к переводу.

phrasebook.phrase: Confirm that the patient is stable.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Подтвердите, что состояние пациента стабильное.

phrasebook.phrase: We are ready to begin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы готовы начать.

phrasebook.phrase: Make sure all the required instruments are available.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /meɪk ʃʊr ɔːl ðə rɪˈkwaɪərd ˈɪnstrəmənts ɑːr əˈveɪləbəl/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Barcha kerakli asboblar mavjudligiga ishonch hosil qiling.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Убедитесь, что все необходимые инструменты имеются.

phrasebook.phrase: The instruments are prepared and within reach.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ði ˈɪnstrəmənts ɑːr prɪˈperd ənd wɪˈðɪn riːtʃ/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Asboblar tayyor va qo'l yetadigan joyda.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Инструменты подготовлены и находятся под рукой.

phrasebook.phrase: Pass me the scalpel, please.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Передайте мне скальпель, пожалуйста.

phrasebook.phrase: I am making the incision now.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сейчас я выполняю разрез.

phrasebook.phrase: The operative field is clear.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Операционное поле хорошо визуализируется.

phrasebook.phrase: Pass me the retractor.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Передайте ретрактор.

phrasebook.phrase: I can see the appendix.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я вижу аппендикс.

phrasebook.phrase: The appendix is enlarged and inflamed.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Аппендикс увеличен и воспалён.

phrasebook.phrase: The surgical field remains clear.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Операционное поле остаётся хорошо визуализируемым.

phrasebook.phrase: I am carefully separating the appendix from the surrounding tissue.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪ æm ˈkerfəli ˈsepəreɪtɪŋ ði əˈpendɪks frəm ðə səˈraʊndɪŋ ˈtɪʃuː/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Appendiksni atrofdagi to'qimalardan ehtiyotkorlik bilan ajratyapman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я осторожно отделяю аппендикс от окружающих тканей.

phrasebook.phrase: Prepare the appropriate sutures.

grammar.title: Indefinite Article — a — An
grammar.structure_pattern: a/an + singular countable noun
grammar.signal_words: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: A / AN artikllari birlikdagi sanaladigan ot bilan ishlatiladi. Ular biror, bitta, qandaydir degan ma'noni beradi. Agar narsa yoki shaxs birinchi marta tilga olinayotgan bo'lsa, odatda a/an ishlatiladi. Undosh tovush bilan boshlanadigan so'zlardan oldin ishlatiladi: Unli tovush bilan boshlanadigan tovushlardan oldin ishlatiladi: Signal so'zlar: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Артикли A / AN используются с исчисляемыми существительными в единственном числе. Они имеют значение "один", "какой-то", "один из". Если предмет или человек упоминается впервые, обычно используется a/an. — Подготовьте стерильный контейнер. — Хирургу нужен зажим. — Для процедуры нужен инструмент. Сигнальные слова: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "A/an" introduces one non-specific countable noun ("a rash", "an infection"); "the" refers to something specific or already mentioned ("the rash on his arm"). No article is used for general plurals and uncountable nouns ("children need fluids"). This/that, these/those and each/every point to particular items. Countable nouns can be counted (symptoms, tablets, episodes) and take many/a few; uncountable nouns (pain, blood, fluid, information) take much/a little and have no plural. "Some" is used in statements and offers, "any" in questions and negatives: "Do you have any pain?" Signal words: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.

grammar.title: The — Definite Article
grammar.structure_pattern: a / an + singular countable (first mention) | the + specific / known noun | no article + general plural / uncountable
grammar.signal_words: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: THE aniq, ma'lum bo'lgan shaxs yoki narsani bildiradi. Agar suhbatdoshlar qaysi bemor, qaysi appendiks, qaysi asbob yoki qaysi operatsion maydon haqida gapirayotganini bilsa, the ishlatiladi. The birlikdagi ham, ko'plikdagi otlar bilan ham ishlatilishi mumkin. Signal so'zlar: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Артикль THE используется, когда речь идёт о конкретном, определённом или уже известном человеке или предмете. Он может использоваться как с существительными в единственном, так и во множественном числе. — Состояние пациента стабильное. — Передайте мне скальпель. Сигнальные слова: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "A/an" introduces one non-specific countable noun ("a rash", "an infection"); "the" refers to something specific or already mentioned ("the rash on his arm"). No article is used for general plurals and uncountable nouns ("children need fluids"). This/that, these/those and each/every point to particular items. Signal words: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.

grammar.title: Key Clinical Patterns
grammar.structure_pattern: Prepare + a/an + noun | Pass me + the + instrument | The + anatomical structure + is + adjective | There is + no + uncountable noun | Each + singular noun | Every + singular noun | All + plural noun | Another + singular noun
grammar.signal_words: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every

Sanaladigan otlar sanaladi (symptoms, tablets, episodes) va many/a few oladi; sanalmaydigan otlar (pain, blood, fluid, information) much/a little oladi va ko'plikda kelmaydi. "Some" darak gap va taklifda, "any" savol va inkorda ishlatiladi: "Do you have any pain?" Signal so'zlar: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «A/an» вводит одно неопределённое исчисляемое существительное («a rash», «an infection»); «the» указывает на конкретное или уже упомянутое («the rash on his arm»). Без артикля — обобщённое множественное число и неисчисляемые («children need fluids»). This/that, these/those, each/every указывают на конкретные предметы. Исчисляемые существительные можно посчитать (symptoms, tablets, episodes) — с ними many/a few; неисчисляемые (pain, blood, fluid, information) — much/a little, без множественного числа. «Some» — в утверждениях и предложениях, «any» — в вопросах и отрицаниях: «Do you have any pain?» Сигнальные слова: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "A/an" introduces one non-specific countable noun ("a rash", "an infection"); "the" refers to something specific or already mentioned ("the rash on his arm"). No article is used for general plurals and uncountable nouns ("children need fluids"). This/that, these/those and each/every point to particular items. Countable nouns can be counted (symptoms, tablets, episodes) and take many/a few; uncountable nouns (pain, blood, fluid, information) take much/a little and have no plural. "Some" is used in statements and offers, "any" in questions and negatives: "Do you have any pain?" Signal words: a, an, the, this, that, these, those, each, every.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning. My name is Nurse Aliya. I'll be looking after you. Could you tell me what brought you to the emergency department today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been having severe chest pain for about an hour.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me where exactly the pain is?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's right in the middle of my chest, behind the breastbone.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: How would you describe the pain? Is it sharp, burning, or more like pressure?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It feels like a heavy pressure, as if something is sitting on my chest.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Does the pain stay in your chest, or does it spread anywhere else?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It spreads to my left arm and sometimes to my jaw.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: When did the pain first start?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: About an hour ago, while I was walking upstairs.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Has the pain been constant since then, or does it come and go?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It has been almost constant.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: On a scale of zero to ten, how would you rate the pain right now?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Around eight out of ten.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Has anything made the pain better or worse?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Resting makes it slightly better, but it comes back when I move.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you experienced this kind of chest pain before?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I had some mild chest discomfort a few months ago, but it wasn't this severe.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Do you have any other symptoms, such as shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, or dizziness?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I'm short of breath and sweating a lot. I also feel nauseated.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I understand. Could you tell me whether you have any medical conditions, such as high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I have high blood pressure and high cholesterol.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Are you currently taking any regular medications?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, I take medication for my blood pressure, but I can't remember the name.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Do you remember whether you took your medication this morning?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, I took it before I left home.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Could you tell me if you have any allergies to medications?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I don't have any known drug allergies.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Do you smoke or have you smoked in the past?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I smoke about five cigarettes a day.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Has anyone in your immediate family had a heart attack or other heart problems?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My father had a heart attack when he was sixty-five.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'd also like to ask whether you have eaten anything recently.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I had breakfast about three hours ago.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to check your vital signs and connect you to the cardiac monitor. Could you please remain as still as possible?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Of course.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Your blood pressure is 158 over 94, and your oxygen saturation is 96% on room air.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is that very high?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Your blood pressure is elevated. The doctor will assess you shortly. I'll continue monitoring you closely.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Do you think I'm having a heart attack?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We need to carry out some tests before we can determine the cause of your symptoms. An ECG and blood tests will be performed.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: How long will that take?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The ECG can be done shortly. Could you let me know immediately if the pain becomes worse or if you develop any new symptoms?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, I will.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Also, could you tell me whether the pain is still at eight out of ten?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's slightly better now. I'd say it's about six out of ten.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Thank you. I'll document that. Please try to stay calm and let me know if the pain changes in character, intensity, or location.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good. I'll stay nearby and keep monitoring you while we arrange the necessary investigations.

phrasebook.phrase: Where exactly is the pain?

phrasebook.phrase: How would you describe the pain?

phrasebook.phrase: Does the pain spread anywhere else?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Распространяется ли боль куда-нибудь ещё?

phrasebook.phrase: Has the pain been constant?

phrasebook.phrase: How would you rate the pain?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you experienced this before?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Испытывали ли вы такое раньше?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you have any other symptoms?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Есть ли у вас другие симптомы?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you have any medical conditions?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Есть ли у вас какие-либо заболевания?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you taking any regular medications?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Принимаете ли вы какие-либо лекарства регулярно?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you have any known drug allergies?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /duː juː hæv ˈeni nəʊn drʌɡ ˈælədʒiz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Есть ли у вас известная аллергия на лекарства?

phrasebook.phrase: Has anyone in your immediate family had a heart attack?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /hæz ˈeniwʌn ɪn jɔːr ɪˈmiːdiət ˈfæməli hæd ə hɑːt æk/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yaqin qarindoshlaringizdan birortasida yurak xuruji bo'lganmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Были ли у кого-нибудь из ваших близких родственников сердечные приступы?

phrasebook.phrase: Please remain as still as possible.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пожалуйста, оставайтесь как можно неподвижнее.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll continue monitoring you closely.
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizni diqqat bilan kuzatishda davom etaman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я продолжу тщательно вас наблюдать.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to carry out some tests.

phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо провести несколько обследований.

phrasebook.phrase: Let me know immediately.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Немедленно сообщите мне.

phrasebook.phrase: The pain has become less intense.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Интенсивность боли уменьшилась.

phrasebook.phrase: I'll document that.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я это задокументирую.

phrasebook.phrase: Stay calm.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сохраняйте спокойствие.

phrasebook.phrase: MODULE 12 — Smart Phrasebook: Chest Pain & Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome
phrasebook.translation_uz: Ko'krak og'rig'i va o'tkir koronar sindromga shubha

phrasebook.phrase: Could you tell me what brought you to the emergency department?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /kʊd juː tel mi wɒt brɔːt juː tə ði ɪˈmɜːdʒənsi dɪˈpɑːtmənt/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Sizni shoshilinch yordam bo'limiga nima olib kelganini ayta olasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Можете рассказать, что привело вас в отделение неотложной помощи?

phrasebook.phrase: Can you tell me where exactly the pain is?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /kæn juː tel mi weər ɪɡˈzæktli ðə peɪn ɪz/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Og'riq aynan qayerda ekanini ayta olasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Можете сказать, где именно находится боль?

phrasebook.phrase: When did the pain first start?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Когда впервые началась боль?

phrasebook.phrase: Has the pain been constant since then?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /hæz ðə peɪn biːn ˈkɒnstənt sɪns ðen/
phrasebook.translation_ru: С тех пор боль постоянная?

phrasebook.phrase: Is it sharp, burning, or more like pressure?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɪz ɪt ʃɑːp ˈbɜːnɪŋ ɔː mɔː laɪk ˈpreʃə/
phrasebook.translation_uz: U sanchuvchi, kuydiruvchi yoki bosuvchi og'riqmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Она острая, жгучая или скорее давящая?

phrasebook.phrase: Has anything made the pain better or worse?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /hæz ˈeniθɪŋ meɪd ðə peɪn ˈbetə ɔː wɜːs/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Biror narsa og'riqni kamaytiradimi yoki kuchaytiradimi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Что-нибудь уменьшает или усиливает боль?

phrasebook.phrase: On a scale of zero to ten, how would you rate the pain?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɒn ə skeɪl əv ˈzɪərəʊ tə ten/
phrasebook.translation_uz: 0 dan 10 gacha og'riqni necha ball deb baholaysiz?
phrasebook.translation_ru: По шкале от нуля до десяти, насколько сильна боль?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you experiencing shortness of breath?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы испытываете одышку?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you been sweating heavily?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы сильно потеете?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you feel nauseated or dizzy?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вас тошнит или у вас кружится голова?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you currently taking any regular medications?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ɑː juː ˈkʌrəntli ˈteɪkɪŋ ˈeni ˈreɡjələ medɪˈkeɪʃənz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Принимаете ли вы сейчас какие-либо лекарства регулярно?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you smoke or have you smoked in the past?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /duː juː sməʊk ɔː hæv juː sməʊkt ɪn ðə pɑːst/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы курите или курили раньше?

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to check your vital signs.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪm ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə tʃek jɔː ˈvaɪtl saɪnz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я проверю ваши жизненные показатели.

phrasebook.phrase: I'm going to connect you to the cardiac monitor.

practice.module: Chest Pain & Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome
practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Nurse Aliya
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.exact_diagnosis: Chest Pain & Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome
medical_condition.chief_complaint: I've been having severe chest pain for about an hour.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. My name is Nurse Aliya. I'll be looking after you. Could you tell me what brought you to the emergency department today?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've been having severe chest pain for about an hour.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me where exactly the pain is?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It's right in the middle of my chest, behind the breastbone.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How would you describe the pain? Is it sharp, burning, or more like pressure?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It feels like a heavy pressure, as if something is sitting on my chest.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Does the pain stay in your chest, or does it spread anywhere else?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It spreads to my left arm and sometimes to my jaw.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When did the pain first start?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: About an hour ago, while I was walking upstairs.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has the pain been constant since then, or does it come and go?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It has been almost constant.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: On a scale of zero to ten, how would you rate the pain right now?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Around eight out of ten.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has anything made the pain better or worse?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Resting makes it slightly better, but it comes back when I move.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you experienced this kind of chest pain before?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I had some mild chest discomfort a few months ago, but it wasn't this severe.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you have any other symptoms, such as shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, or dizziness?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I'm short of breath and sweating a lot. I also feel nauseated.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I understand. Could you tell me whether you have any medical conditions, such as high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I have high blood pressure and high cholesterol.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Are you currently taking any regular medications?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, I take medication for my blood pressure, but I can't remember the name.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you remember whether you took your medication this morning?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, I took it before I left home.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Could you tell me if you have any allergies to medications?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I don't have any known drug allergies.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you smoke or have you smoked in the past?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I smoke about five cigarettes a day.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has anyone in your immediate family had a heart attack or other heart problems?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: My father had a heart attack when he was sixty-five.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Is that very high?
Do you think I'm having a heart attack?
How long will that take?

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Stroke Recognition & Initial Management. Grammar focus: Passive Voice. Includes a reference nurse–patient dialogue, 50 vocabulary items, 61 smart phrases, 13 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Nurse, a new patient has just been brought in. What was noticed when he arrived?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Sudden weakness on the right side of his body was noticed, and his speech was also affected.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: When was he last known to be well?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: He was last seen well at around 8:15 this morning.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. His symptoms appear to have started suddenly. Was his level of consciousness checked?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. He was assessed immediately. He is awake and responds appropriately, but his speech is unclear.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has his blood glucose been checked?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. His blood glucose was checked on arrival, and it was within the normal range.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. Were his vital signs recorded?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. His blood pressure was recorded as 176 over 98, his pulse was 88, and his oxygen saturation was 97% on room air.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has an IV line been inserted?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes, an IV line has been inserted, and blood samples have been taken.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Excellent. Was the patient's medical history obtained?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. His wife was asked about his medical history. She said that he has hypertension and takes medication for it.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Was any previous stroke or transient ischaemic attack reported?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: No previous stroke was reported, and she was not aware of any previous transient ischaemic attack.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Is there any history of anticoagulant use?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: No anticoagulants are being taken, according to his wife.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. We need to determine whether he is a candidate for acute stroke treatment. Has the stroke team been contacted?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. The stroke team has been informed, and they are on their way.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has an urgent brain scan been requested?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. An urgent CT scan has been requested.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. Make sure the patient is kept nil by mouth until his swallowing has been assessed.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Understood. Oral food and fluids will be withheld until a swallowing assessment has been completed.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has his neurological status been reassessed?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. His facial symmetry, arm strength, speech, and level of consciousness have been reassessed.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What was found?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Facial weakness was noted on the right side, and reduced strength was found in his right arm. His speech remains unclear.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Has the time of symptom onset been documented?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. The last-known-well time has been documented as 8:15.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Excellent. That information is critical. Has the patient's wife been informed about the need for urgent assessment?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. She has been informed, and she has been asked to remain available for further questions.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. Please continue monitoring his neurological status and vital signs. Any deterioration must be reported immediately.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Understood, Doctor. His neurological status and vital signs will be monitored closely, and any change will be reported immediately.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has the CT department confirmed that the patient can be taken for scanning?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Yes. The scan has been scheduled, and the patient can be transferred now.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. Make sure all relevant information is sent with the patient.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Of course. The observation chart, blood results, medication history, and last-known-well time will be sent with him.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Excellent. Let's proceed with the urgent assessment and keep the stroke team updated.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Understood, Doctor.

grammar.title: Present Simple Passive
grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + V3
grammar.signal_words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Simple Passive muntazam bajariladigan klinik jarayonlar, protokollar va umumiy tibbiy amaliyotlarni ifodalashda ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Simple Passive используется для описания регулярных процедур, стандартных действий и медицинских протоколов. Сигнальные слова: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: usually, often, every day, sometimes, never.

grammar.title: Past Simple Passive
grammar.structure_pattern: was / were + V3
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Past Simple Passive o'tmishda bajarilgan va tugagan klinik harakatlarni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple Passive используется для описания действий, которые были выполнены в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Passive
grammar.structure_pattern: has / have + been + V3
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect Passive ish-harakat yaqinda bajarilgan va uning natijasi hozirgi vaziyat uchun muhim bo'lganida ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect Passive используется, когда действие уже было выполнено, и его результат важен в настоящий момент. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Future Passive

grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be

grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Future Passive используется для действий, которые будут выполнены в будущем. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Common Clinical Patterns
grammar.structure_pattern: The patient was + V3 | The patient's + noun + was/were + V3 | The + procedure/test + has been + V3 | The patient will be + V3 | Any + problem/change/deterioration + must be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Passive Voice harakatni kim bajarayotganidan ko'ra harakatning o'zi yoki bemor muhim bo'lganda ishlatiladi — tahlillar, muolajalar va davolash rejasi uchun odatiy: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "Must" so'zlovchining qat'iy talabini bildiradi ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — tashqi qoida yoki talab. "Mustn't" — taqiqlangan, "don't have to" esa — shart emas. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». «Must» выражает строгую необходимость со стороны говорящего («You must take the full course of antibiotics»); «have to» — внешнее правило или требование. «Mustn't» — запрещено, «don't have to» — не обязательно. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "Must" expresses strong necessity from the speaker ("You must take the full course of antibiotics"); "have to" — an external rule or requirement. "Mustn't" means it is forbidden, while "don't have to" means it is not necessary. Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Passive Voice harakatni kim bajarayotganidan ko'ra harakatning o'zi yoki bemor muhim bo'lganda ishlatiladi — tahlillar, muolajalar va davolash rejasi uchun odatiy: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "Will" hozir qabul qilingan qaror, va'da, bashorat va bemorni tinchlantirishni ifodalaydi: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». «Will» выражает решение, принятое в момент речи, обещание, прогноз и успокоение пациента: «I will give you something for the pain», «The swelling will go down in a few days». Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the DOCTOR.

patient_profile.name: Thomas Hale
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Nurse, a new patient has just been brought in. What was noticed when he arrived?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Sudden weakness on the right side of his body was noticed, and his speech was also affected.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: When was he last known to be well?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: He was last seen well at around 8:15 this morning.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good. His symptoms appear to have started suddenly. Was his level of consciousness checked?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. He was assessed immediately. He is awake and responds appropriately, but his speech is unclear.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Has his blood glucose been checked?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. His blood glucose was checked on arrival, and it was within the normal range.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good. Were his vital signs recorded?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. His blood pressure was recorded as 176 over 98, his pulse was 88, and his oxygen saturation was 97% on room air.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Has an IV line been inserted?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes, an IV line has been inserted, and blood samples have been taken.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Excellent. Was the patient's medical history obtained?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. His wife was asked about his medical history. She said that he has hypertension and takes medication for it.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Was any previous stroke or transient ischaemic attack reported?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: No previous stroke was reported, and she was not aware of any previous transient ischaemic attack.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is there any history of anticoagulant use?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: No anticoagulants are being taken, according to his wife.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good. We need to determine whether he is a candidate for acute stroke treatment. Has the stroke team been contacted?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. The stroke team has been informed, and they are on their way.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Has an urgent brain scan been requested?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. An urgent CT scan has been requested.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good. Make sure the patient is kept nil by mouth until his swallowing has been assessed.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Understood. Oral food and fluids will be withheld until a swallowing assessment has been completed.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Has his neurological status been reassessed?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. His facial symmetry, arm strength, speech, and level of consciousness have been reassessed.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What was found?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Facial weakness was noted on the right side, and reduced strength was found in his right arm. His speech remains unclear.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you. Has the time of symptom onset been documented?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. The last-known-well time has been documented as 8:15.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Excellent. That information is critical. Has the patient's wife been informed about the need for urgent assessment?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. She has been informed, and she has been asked to remain available for further questions.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good. Please continue monitoring his neurological status and vital signs. Any deterioration must be reported immediately.

Has his blood glucose been checked?
Were his vital signs recorded?

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Acute Kidney Injury & Fluid Balance. Grammar focus: Gerund & Infinitive. Includes a reference nurse–patient dialogue, 45 vocabulary items, 53 smart phrases, 13 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning, Mr. Jeff. How are you feeling today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning. I'm feeling very tired and weak.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I understand. Have you been drinking enough fluids?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I've been drinking less than usual for the past two days.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any changes in your urine output?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been passing much less urine than usual since yesterday.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: When did you first notice the decrease in urine output?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yesterday afternoon. My urine also seems darker than usual.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. My ankles have become slightly swollen.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you experienced any shortness of breath?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: A little. I feel slightly breathless when I lie down.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to check your vital signs and assess your fluid balance.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I'll be checking your blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and weight. We also need to monitor your fluid intake and urine output.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: It is important to keep a record of how much fluid you are drinking and how much urine you are producing.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Your recent blood tests suggest that your kidney function has become reduced. The doctor will review the results to determine the cause.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I see.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We also need to monitor you for signs of fluid retention and dehydration.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Please continue recording your fluid intake and urine output accurately.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I will.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Measuring your urine output regularly will help us to monitor your kidney function.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Please tell us immediately if your urine output decreases further or if you develop worsening breathlessness or swelling.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Of course.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We'll also continue monitoring your blood pressure and weight.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: A rapid increase in weight may indicate that fluid is building up in your body, so your weight will be checked regularly.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Our aim is to monitor your kidney function, maintain an appropriate fluid balance, and prevent your condition from getting worse.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Please let me know if you notice any changes in your urine output, breathing, or swelling.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I will.

grammar.title: Gerund — Verb + -Ing
grammar.structure_pattern: Verb + -ing
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund — fe'lga -ing qo'shimchasi qo'shilib, gapda ot vazifasida ishlatiladigan shakl. Tibbiy ingliz tilida Gerund ko'pincha faoliyat yoki jarayonni umumiy ma'noda ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Gerund — это форма глагола с окончанием -ing, которая выполняет функцию существительного. В медицинском английском Gerund часто используется для обозначения действия или процесса в общем смысле. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

grammar.title: Gerund As the Subject of a Sentence
grammar.structure_pattern: verb + V-ing (avoid, stop, keep, recommend) | verb + to + V1 (need, want, decide, advise sb to)
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund gapning egasi bo'lib kelishi mumkin. Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Gerund может выполнять функцию подлежащего. — Контроль потребления жидкости важен. — Измерение объёма мочи имеет большое значение. — Регистрация потребления жидкости помогает нам оценить водный баланс. Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

practice.setting: hospital ward (the nurse talks to the patient, relatives or the doctor)
practice.role_play: The student is a NURSE. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Mr. Jeff
patient_profile.personality_trait: cooperative, sometimes confused about instructions

medical_condition.chief_complaint: Good morning. I'm feeling very tired and weak.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: Your recent blood tests suggest that your kidney function has become reduced. The doctor will review the results to determine the cause.
A rapid increase in weight may indicate that fluid is building up in your body, so your weight will be checked regularly.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning, Mr. Jeff. How are you feeling today?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Good morning. I'm feeling very tired and weak.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I understand. Have you been drinking enough fluids?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I've been drinking less than usual for the past two days.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any changes in your urine output?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I've been passing much less urine than usual since yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When did you first notice the decrease in urine output?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yesterday afternoon. My urine also seems darker than usual.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. My ankles have become slightly swollen.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you experienced any shortness of breath?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: A little. I feel slightly breathless when I lie down.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. I'm going to check your vital signs and assess your fluid balance.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I'll be checking your blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and weight. We also need to monitor your fluid intake and urine output.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It is important to keep a record of how much fluid you are drinking and how much urine you are producing.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Your recent blood tests suggest that your kidney function has become reduced. The doctor will review the results to determine the cause.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I see.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We also need to monitor you for signs of fluid retention and dehydration.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Please continue recording your fluid intake and urine output accurately.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I will.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Measuring your urine output regularly will help us to monitor your kidney function.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: All right.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Please tell us immediately if your urine output decreases further or if you develop worsening breathlessness or swelling.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Of course.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We'll also continue monitoring your blood pressure and weight.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: A rapid increase in weight may indicate that fluid is building up in your body, so your weight will be checked regularly.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand.

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Electrolyte Imbalances & ECG Changes. Grammar focus: Countable & Uncountable Nouns + Quantifiers. Includes a reference nurse–patient dialogue, 38 vocabulary items, 37 smart phrases, 16 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good morning, Mr. Rashid. How are you feeling at the moment?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I feel ok.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: I understand. Have you had any symptoms?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've had some muscle cramps and a bit of nausea.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: When did these symptoms start?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: They started yesterday, and they seem to be getting worse.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you been drinking enough fluids recently?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Not really. I've only been drinking a little water.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you had much to eat today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I haven't had much food. I've only eaten a few pieces of bread.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any changes in your heartbeat?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. My heart sometimes feels like it is beating irregularly.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to check your vital signs and put you on a cardiac monitor.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Your blood pressure is slightly low, and your heart rate is irregular.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is that serious?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We need to investigate the cause. Your blood tests show that you have an electrolyte imbalance.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I see.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Your potassium level is lower than normal, so we need to monitor your heart rhythm carefully.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We'll also check your blood sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium levels.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: An ECG will be performed to look for any changes in your heart rhythm.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Please remain still while we record the ECG.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Of course.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The ECG shows some changes that may be related to your electrolyte imbalance.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What happens next?

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: The doctor will review the results and decide whether you need electrolyte replacement or further treatment.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: For now, please tell me if you develop any chest discomfort, severe weakness, worsening dizziness, or palpitations.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I will.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We'll continue monitoring your heart rhythm and checking your electrolyte levels.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: We also need to keep an accurate record of your fluid intake and any urine you produce.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: All right. I'll let you know.

dialogue.label: Nurse
dialogue.text: Good. Please report any new symptoms immediately.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.
