patient_profile.personality_trait: distressed, worried, answers briefly because of discomfort

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I had been feeling strange for about ten minutes. I felt dizzy, and I had a strange sensation in my right hand. Then everything went blank.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: It is possible. If a seizure lasts five minutes or longer, or if seizures occur repeatedly without full recovery between them, this may indicate status epilepticus and requires immediate emergency treatment.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What happened immediately before you lost consciousness?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I had been feeling strange for about ten minutes. I felt dizzy, and I had a strange sensation in my right hand. Then everything went blank.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Had you ever experienced anything similar before?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I was diagnosed with epilepsy three years ago, but I hadn't had a seizure for almost a year.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What anti-seizure medication are you taking?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I take levetiracetam, 500 milligrams twice a day.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When did you last take it?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I took my morning dose as usual, but I missed my evening dose yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Why did you miss the dose?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I had run out of tablets and hadn't been able to get a new prescription.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Had you missed any other doses recently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No. I had been taking the medication regularly until yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did anyone witness the seizure?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. My wife was with me.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What did she see?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: She said I suddenly fell to the floor and became unresponsive. My whole body became stiff first, and then my arms and legs started jerking.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you know how long the seizure lasted?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: My wife said the jerking had continued for about three minutes before it stopped.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did you regain consciousness immediately?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No. I had remained unresponsive for another couple of minutes. When I finally opened my eyes, I was very confused.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How long did the confusion last?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I had been confused for about twenty minutes before I started speaking normally again.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did you bite your tongue or lose control of your bladder?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I had bitten the side of my tongue and apparently lost bladder control during the seizure.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did you injure yourself when you fell?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I hit my head on the floor, and my shoulder has been painful since then.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Had you been sleeping normally recently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No. I had been sleeping only four or five hours a night for almost a week.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Had you consumed alcohol or taken any recreational drugs or new medication?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I had drunk some alcohol the previous evening, but I hadn't taken any recreational drugs or new medication.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you had another seizure since this episode?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I haven't.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What can I help you with today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been having increasing difficulty passing urine since yesterday. I feel like I need to urinate, but very little comes out.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: When was the last time you were able to pass urine normally?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I passed a normal amount yesterday morning. Since then, I've been passing only small amounts.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you been able to empty your bladder completely?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No. I've felt a constant pressure in my lower abdomen, and it feels as though my bladder is still full after I urinate.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any pain when you try to urinate?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been having increasing discomfort, especially when I try to start urinating.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any blood in your urine or any change in its colour?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I haven't seen any blood, but my urine has become darker than usual.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you been drinking enough fluids recently?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Not really. I've been drinking much less than usual for the last two days because I've been feeling nauseous.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you had any vomiting or diarrhoea?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've vomited several times since yesterday, but I haven't had diarrhoea.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed that you've been passing less urine overall?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been producing much less urine than usual since yesterday.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you ever had problems with urinary retention before?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I've never had anything like this before.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you recently started taking any new medications?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I started taking a new medication for my back pain about a week ago.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you know the name of the medication?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's a strong painkiller. I don't remember the exact name.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you had any fever, chills, or pain in your sides?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I haven't had a fever or chills, but I've had some discomfort in both sides of my lower back.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Your bladder feels quite distended, and your urine output has been significantly reduced. We also need to check your kidney function because reduced urine output can occur with acute kidney injury, or AKI.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean my kidneys are failing?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Not necessarily. We need to identify the cause first. Your urinary retention, reduced fluid intake, vomiting, and recent medication changes may all be relevant.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What tests will I need?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We'll check your blood tests, including creatinine and electrolytes, and we'll measure the amount of urine remaining in your bladder. We may also arrange an ultrasound to look at your urinary tract and kidneys.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. We'll assess you now and determine whether the reduced urine output is mainly due to urinary obstruction, dehydration, medication, or another cause.

grammar.title: Grammar focus: Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.title_en: Grammar focus: Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.title_uz: Modul grammatikasi: Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.title_ru: Грамматика модуля: Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3 | Have/Has + subject + V3? | have / has + been + V-ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu dialogda Present Perfect va Present Perfect Continuous asosan simptomlarning hozirgi holat bilan bog'liqligi, ularning davomiyligi, siydik ajralishidagi yaqindagi o'zgarishlar, oldingi tajriba va yaqinda boshlangan dori qabulini aniqlash uchun ishlatilgan. O'zbekcha: Present Perfect ko'proq natija, tajriba yoki hozirgi vaziyat uchun muhim bo'lgan hodisani; Present Perfect Continuous esa davom etayotgan yoki takrorlanayotgan jarayonni ta'kidlaydi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое с настоящим. В этом диалоге он используется для текущего результата, медицинского опыта, недавних изменений и состояний, которые важны сейчас. Present Perfect Continuous подчёркивает процесс или длительность действия, начавшегося в прошлом и продолжающегося до настоящего момента. Повторяющееся действие: I've been passing only small amounts. Главное: если важно "что произошло / какой результат / был ли такой опыт", чаще выбираем Present Perfect. Если важно "как долго / как долго продолжается процесс / повторяется ли действие", чаще выбираем Present Perfect Continuous. Русский: Present Perfect связывает прошлое с настоящим и часто подчёркивает результат, опыт или недавнее изменение. Present Perfect Continuous подчёркивает процесс, длительность или повторяющееся действие, начавшееся в прошлом и продолжающееся сейчас. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Present Perfect Continuous describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing (or has just stopped and its effect is visible). It is the key tense for symptom duration: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + been + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect Continuous o'tmishda boshlangan va hozirgacha davom etayotgan yoki yaqinda davom etib kelgan jarayonni, ayniqsa davomiylik yoki takrorlanishni ta'kidlash uchun ishlatiladi. for / since bilan davomiylik; hozirgacha davom etayotgan simptom; jarayonning davom etgani muhim bo'lganda. Signal so'zlar: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается (или только что закончилось и результат заметен). Ключевое время для длительности симптомов: «How long have you been feeling unwell?» — «I have been coughing for five days». Сигнальные слова: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect Continuous describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing (or has just stopped and its effect is visible). It is the key tense for symptom duration: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal words: since, for, how long, lately, recently, all day.

grammar.title: Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3 | Have/Has + subject + V3? | have / has + been + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ikkalasi ham o'tmish va hozirni bog'laydi. Asosiy farq: Present Perfect ko'proq fakt, natija yoki tajribani; Present Perfect Continuous esa jarayon, davomiylik yoki takrorlanishni ta'kidlaydi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Present Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается (или только что закончилось и результат заметен). Ключевое время для длительности симптомов: «How long have you been feeling unwell?» — «I have been coughing for five days». Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Present Perfect Continuous describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing (or has just stopped and its effect is visible). It is the key tense for symptom duration: "How long have you been feeling unwell?" — "I have been coughing for five days". Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: For vs Since
grammar.structure_pattern: for + duration | since + starting point | for + period
grammar.signal_words: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Muhim: for vaqt davomiyligini bildiradi; since esa harakat boshlangan nuqtani bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Важно: for указывает продолжительность, а since — момент, с которого действие началось. Сигнальные слова: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Since" gives the starting point ("since yesterday"), "for" the length of time ("for three days") and "ago" counts back from now ("two hours ago"). Exact times ("at about 7:15 this morning") are essential in time-critical conditions such as stroke. Signal words: since, for, ago, at about, over the last, until.

grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое началось в прошлом и всё ещё продолжается (или только что закончилось и результат заметен). grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect Continuous describes an action that started in the past and is still continuing (or has just stopped and its effect is visible). grammar.title: Other Tenses in This Dialogue
grammar.structure_pattern: Passive / be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Grammar focus ikki zamonga qaratilgan bo'lsa-da, tabiiy clinical dialogue boshqa tense va constructionslarni ham o'z ichiga oladi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

practice.setting: emergency department / resuscitation bay
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Anna Collins
patient_profile.personality_trait: distressed, worried, answers briefly because of discomfort

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I've been having increasing difficulty passing urine since yesterday. I feel like I need to urinate, but very little comes out.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What can I help you with today?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've been having increasing difficulty passing urine since yesterday. I feel like I need to urinate, but very little comes out.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When was the last time you were able to pass urine normally?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I passed a normal amount yesterday morning. Since then, I've been passing only small amounts.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you been able to empty your bladder completely?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No. I've felt a constant pressure in my lower abdomen, and it feels as though my bladder is still full after I urinate.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any pain when you try to urinate?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I've been having increasing discomfort, especially when I try to start urinating.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any blood in your urine or any change in its colour?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I haven't seen any blood, but my urine has become darker than usual.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you been drinking enough fluids recently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Not really. I've been drinking much less than usual for the last two days because I've been feeling nauseous.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you had any vomiting or diarrhoea?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've vomited several times since yesterday, but I haven't had diarrhoea.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed that you've been passing less urine overall?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I've been producing much less urine than usual since yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you ever had problems with urinary retention before?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I've never had anything like this before.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you recently started taking any new medications?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I started taking a new medication for my back pain about a week ago.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you know the name of the medication?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It's a strong painkiller. I don't remember the exact name.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you had any fever, chills, or pain in your sides?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I haven't had a fever or chills, but I've had some discomfort in both sides of my lower back.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Your bladder feels quite distended, and your urine output has been significantly reduced. We also need to check your kidney function because reduced urine output can occur with ac…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Does that mean my kidneys are failing?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Not necessarily. We need to identify the cause first. Your urinary retention, reduced fluid intake, vomiting, and recent medication changes may all be relevant.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What tests will I need?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We'll check your blood tests, including creatinine and electrolytes, and we'll measure the amount of urine remaining in your bladder. We may also arrange an ultrasound to look at…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Does that mean my kidneys are failing?
What tests will I need?

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Thermal Injuries & Burns. Grammar focus: Passive Voice — Different Tenses. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 48 vocabulary items, 37 smart phrases, 9 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Hello. What happened?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I was cooking at home when a pan of boiling water tipped over and spilled onto my chest and left arm.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How long ago did this happen?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: About forty minutes ago.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What did you do immediately afterwards?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I moved away from the stove and took off my wet clothes. I didn't put anything on the burns because I wasn't sure what I should use.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's fine. Were any of your clothes stuck to the skin?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, they weren't.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you been burned anywhere else?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: There's a small area on my upper abdomen, but most of the burn is on my chest and left arm.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Are you having any difficulty breathing or swallowing?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No. I'm breathing normally, and I can swallow without any problems.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. And how bad is the pain?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's quite severe. It's probably about eight out of ten, especially in my left arm.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. Your vital signs will be checked first, and I'll examine the burns carefully. We'll also give you something for the pain.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you. Do they look serious?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Some areas are red and blistered, and a few areas look deeper. We need to assess the depth of the burns and how much of your body surface has been affected.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What happens next?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Once the burns have been assessed, they'll be cleaned and covered with appropriate dressings. We'll also make sure your pain is under control.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I have to stay in hospital?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We can't say yet. It depends on the size, location, and depth of the burns. If they're more extensive or deeper than they currently appear, you may be referred to a specialist burns unit.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: How long will they take to heal?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Superficial burns usually heal relatively quickly. Deeper burns can take much longer and may require specialist treatment and regular follow-up.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I be able to go home today?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We'll make that decision after you've been examined and your pain has been controlled. If it's safe for you to go home, you'll be given clear instructions about wound care and follow-up.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What should I look out for at home?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If you develop increasing pain, spreading redness, swelling, fever, or discharge from the wound, you should come back for reassessment.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay. I understand.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. Let's get your vital signs checked and then we'll assess the burns properly.

grammar.title_uz: Modul grammatikasi: Passive Voice — Different Tenses
grammar.title_ru: Грамматика модуля: Passive Voice — Different Tenses
grammar.structure_pattern: be (am/is/are/was/were/will be/has been) + V3 | modal + be + V3
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Ruscha: Passive Voice tibbiy jarayonni bemor nuqtayi nazaridan tushuntirishga yordam beradi. O'zbekcha: Passive Voice bemorga qanday tekshiruv, davolash yoki keyingi tibbiy choralar qo'llanilishini aniq va professional tarzda ifodalash imkonini beradi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Главная идея: в Passive Voice главное не тот, кто выполняет действие, а действие или результат действия. В медицинском английском Passive Voice очень часто используется, потому что внимание сосредоточено на пациенте, процедуре, обследовании и лечении. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice — Different Tenses Passive Voice is especially useful when describing what happens to the patient: vital signs are checked, burns are examined, wounds are cleaned, dressings are applied, and patients may be referred for specialist treatment. Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Passive Voice
grammar.structure_pattern: be + V3 | have/has been + V3 | was/were + V3 | may be + V3 | will be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Passive Voice harakatni kim bajarayotganidan ko'ra harakatning o'zi yoki bemor muhim bo'lganda ishlatiladi — tahlillar, muolajalar va davolash rejasi uchun odatiy: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "May" va "might" ehtimollik va ehtiyotkor klinik xulosani bildiradi: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" muloyim ruxsat ham beradi. "Might have + V3" — o'tmishdagi ehtimol. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». «May» и «might» выражают возможность и осторожное клиническое суждение: «It may be an infection», «You might need to stay in hospital». «May» также даёт вежливое разрешение. «Might have + V3» — возможное событие в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Future Passive — Will Be + V3
grammar.structure_pattern: English: will be + past participle (V3)
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Uzbekcha: kelajakda bajariladigan ish-harakatni ifodalaydi. Kim bajarishi muhim bo'lmaganda yoki aytilmaganda Passive ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Future Passive используется, когда важно не кто выполнит действие, а само действие, которое будет выполнено в будущем. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "Will" expresses decisions made now, promises, predictions and reassurance: "I will give you something for the pain", "The swelling will go down in a few days". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Passive — Have/Has Been + V3
grammar.structure_pattern: English: have/has been + V3
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Uzbekcha: o'tmishda bajarilgan ishning hozirgi vaziyat bilan bog'liqligini ko'rsatadi. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect Passive показывает, что действие уже выполнено, а его результат важен сейчас. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Tibbiy ingliz tilida Passive Voice tekshiruv, muolaja, davolash va keyingi nazoratni tasvirlashda juda ko'p ishlatiladi. Chunki asosiy e'tibor ishni kim bajarayotganiga emas, bemor va bajarilayotgan jarayonga qaratiladi. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Почему Passive Voice так часто используется в медицине? В медицинском английском Passive Voice особенно распространён в описании обследований, процедур, лечения и дальнейшего наблюдения. Это позволяет сосредоточиться на пациенте и медицинском процессе, а не на конкретном исполнителе. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

grammar.title: Important Clinical Patterns
grammar.structure_pattern: Once + Present Perfect Passive, Future Passive | If + Present Simple, Passive/Modal | After + Present Perfect Passive
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect o'tmishdagi voqeani hozirgi holat bilan bog'laydi: tajriba, yaqinda bo'lgan voqea yoki hozir muhim bo'lgan natija. Anamnez yig'ishda hozirgacha bo'lgan simptomlar so'raladi: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Passive Voice harakatni kim bajarayotganidan ko'ra harakatning o'zi yoki bemor muhim bo'lganda ishlatiladi — tahlillar, muolajalar va davolash rejasi uchun odatiy: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect связывает прошлое событие с настоящим: опыт, недавнее событие или результат, важный сейчас. При сборе анамнеза так спрашивают о симптомах вплоть до настоящего момента: «Have you had any fever?», «I have vomited three times». Passive Voice используется, когда важнее само действие или пациент, а не исполнитель — типично для анализов, процедур и плана лечения: «Blood samples will be taken», «You will be referred to a specialist», «The wound has been cleaned». Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.title: Quick Grammar Guide
grammar.structure_pattern: will be + V3 | has/have been + V3 | was/were + V3 | may be + V3
grammar.signal_words: by, will be, has been, needs to be
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Asosiy qoida: avval signalni toping, keyin zamonni aniqlang. Signal so'zlar: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Главное: не нужно сразу вспоминать все грамматические правила. Сначала найдите сигнал: will be, has/have been, was/were, may be. Затем определите время и смысл. Сигнальные слова: by, will be, has been, needs to be.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Passive Voice is used when the action or the patient matters more than who performs it — typical for tests, procedures and treatment plans: "Blood samples will be taken", "You will be referred to a specialist", "The wound has been cleaned". "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. Signal words: by, will be, has been, needs to be.

practice.setting: emergency department / resuscitation bay
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Grace Hughes
patient_profile.personality_trait: distressed, worried, answers briefly because of discomfort

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I was cooking at home when a pan of boiling water tipped over and spilled onto my chest and left arm.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Hello. What happened?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I was cooking at home when a pan of boiling water tipped over and spilled onto my chest and left arm.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How long ago did this happen?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: About forty minutes ago.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What did you do immediately afterwards?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I moved away from the stove and took off my wet clothes. I didn't put anything on the burns because I wasn't sure what I should use.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: That's fine. Were any of your clothes stuck to the skin?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, they weren't.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you been burned anywhere else?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: There's a small area on my upper abdomen, but most of the burn is on my chest and left arm.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Are you having any difficulty breathing or swallowing?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No. I'm breathing normally, and I can swallow without any problems.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good. And how bad is the pain?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It's quite severe. It's probably about eight out of ten, especially in my left arm.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. Your vital signs will be checked first, and I'll examine the burns carefully. We'll also give you something for the pain.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Thank you. Do they look serious?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Some areas are red and blistered, and a few areas look deeper. We need to assess the depth of the burns and how much of your body surface has been affected.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What happens next?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Once the burns have been assessed, they'll be cleaned and covered with appropriate dressings. We'll also make sure your pain is under control.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I have to stay in hospital?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We can't say yet. It depends on the size, location, and depth of the burns. If they're more extensive or deeper than they currently appear, you may be referred to a specialist bur…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: How long will they take to heal?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Superficial burns usually heal relatively quickly. Deeper burns can take much longer and may require specialist treatment and regular follow-up.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I be able to go home today?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We'll make that decision after you've been examined and your pain has been controlled. If it's safe for you to go home, you'll be given clear instructions about wound care and fol…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What should I look out for at home?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: If you develop increasing pain, spreading redness, swelling, fever, or discharge from the wound, you should come back for reassessment.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay. I understand.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Do they look serious?
What happens next?
Will I have to stay in hospital?
How long will they take to heal?
Will I be able to go home today?

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Anaphylactic Shock. Grammar focus: Reported Speech + Reporting Verbs. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 46 vocabulary items, 39 smart phrases, 16 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Hello. Can you tell me what happened?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I suddenly became very unwell after eating some food at a restaurant. My lips started swelling, and I found it difficult to breathe.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How long ago did the symptoms start?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: About twenty minutes ago. I had been eating for about half an hour when I suddenly felt that something was wrong.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What did you notice first?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My mouth started tingling, and then my lips and tongue began to swell. I also developed an itchy rash across my chest and arms.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you feel light-headed or faint?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I felt very light-headed, and I thought I was going to pass out.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did anyone give you any medication before you arrived here?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction and gave me an antihistamine. She told me that I should sit down and try to stay calm.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did the antihistamine help?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Not really. My breathing became worse afterwards.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you ever had a reaction like this before?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I had a mild reaction to nuts when I was a child. My doctor told me that I probably had a nut allergy, so I've avoided them since then.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you know exactly what you ate today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I had a dessert containing nuts, although I wasn't aware that it contained them. The waiter said that the dessert was safe, but now I'm not so sure.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you ever been prescribed an adrenaline auto-injector?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I was given one several years ago, but I haven't carried it with me recently.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you remember what your doctor told you about using it?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: He told me that I should use it immediately if I developed difficulty breathing or swelling of my tongue or throat.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's important. Your symptoms suggest that you're having a severe allergic reaction, possibly anaphylaxis. We're going to treat you immediately.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is it serious?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes. Anaphylaxis can become life-threatening very quickly. Your blood pressure is low, and your breathing is affected. We'll give you adrenaline immediately and monitor your breathing, blood pressure, and oxygen levels closely.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Even if your symptoms improve quickly, you'll need to be observed because the reaction can return after the initial treatment. Before you leave, we'll make sure that you understand how to avoid the trigger and how to use an adrenaline auto-injector.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. For now, try to remain calm and let us know immediately if your breathing gets worse or if you feel faint again.

phrasebook.pronunciation: /maɪ ˈdɒktə təʊld mi ðət aɪ ˈprɒbəbli hæd ə nʌt ˈælədʒi/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Shifokorim menda yong'oqqa allergiya bo'lishi mumkinligini aytgan.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мой врач сказал мне, что у меня, вероятно, аллергия на орехи.

phrasebook.phrase: The waiter said that the dessert was safe.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə ˈweɪtə sed ðət ðə dɪˈzɜːt wəz seɪf/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Официант сказал, что десерт безопасен.

phrasebook.phrase: He told me that I should use it immediately.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /hi təʊld mi ðət aɪ ʃəd juːz ɪˈmiːdiətli/
phrasebook.translation_uz: U menga uni darhol ishlatishim kerakligini aytdi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Он сказал мне, что я должен использовать его немедленно.

phrasebook.phrase: Have you ever been prescribed an adrenaline auto-injector?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /hæv juː ˈevə biːn prɪˈskraɪbd ən əˈdrenəlɪn ˌɔːtəʊ ɪnˈdʒektə/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам когда-нибудь назначали автоинъектор адреналина?

phrasebook.phrase: I was given one several years ago.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪ wəz ˈɡɪvən wʌn ˈsevrəl jɪəz əˈɡəʊ/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Menga bir necha yil oldin berilgandi.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мне его выдали несколько лет назад.

phrasebook.phrase: I haven't carried it with me recently.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪ ˈhævənt ˈkærid ɪt wɪð mi ˈriːsəntli/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Oxirgi paytlarda uni o'zim bilan olib yurmayapman.
phrasebook.translation_ru: В последнее время я не носил его с собой.

phrasebook.phrase: I wasn't aware that it contained nuts.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aɪ ˈwɒzənt əˈweə ðət ɪt kənˈteɪnd nʌts/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Uning tarkibida yong'oq borligini bilmagan edim.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я не знал, что в нём содержатся орехи.

phrasebook.phrase: I've avoided nuts since then.
phrasebook.translation_ru: С тех пор я избегал орехов.

phrasebook.phrase: Your symptoms suggest a severe allergic reaction.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /jɔː ˈsɪmptəmz səˈdʒest ə sɪˈvɪə əˈlɜːdʒɪk riˈækʃən/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Ваши симптомы указывают на тяжёлую аллергическую реакцию.

phrasebook.phrase: We're going to treat you immediately.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы немедленно начнём вас лечить.

phrasebook.phrase: Anaphylaxis can become life-threatening very quickly.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ˌænəfɪˈlæksɪs kən bɪˈkʌm ˈlaɪf ˌθretənɪŋ ˈveri ˈkwɪkli/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Anafilaksiya juda tez hayot uchun xavfli bo'lishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Анафилаксия может очень быстро стать опасной для жизни.

phrasebook.phrase: Your blood pressure is low.
phrasebook.translation_ru: У вас низкое артериальное давление.

phrasebook.phrase: Your breathing is affected.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Ваше дыхание нарушено.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll give you adrenaline immediately.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы немедленно введём вам адреналин.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll monitor your breathing closely.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем внимательно следить за вашим дыханием.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll monitor your blood pressure and oxygen levels.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiːl ˈmɒnɪtə jɔː blʌd ˈpreʃə ənd ˈɒksɪdʒən ˈlevəlz/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Qon bosimingiz va kislorod darajangizni kuzatamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем контролировать ваше давление и уровень кислорода.

phrasebook.phrase: You'll need to be observed.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам потребуется наблюдение.

phrasebook.phrase: The reaction can return after the initial treatment.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /ðə riˈækʃən kən rɪˈtɜːn ˈɑːftə ði ɪˈnɪʃəl ˈtriːtmənt/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Dastlabki davolashdan keyin reaksiya qaytishi mumkin.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Реакция может вернуться после первоначального лечения.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll make sure that you understand how to avoid the trigger.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiːl meɪk ʃɔː ðət juː ˌʌndəˈstænd haʊ tə əˈvɔɪd ðə ˈtrɪɡə/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Qo'zg'atuvchi omildan qanday saqlanishni tushunganingizga ishonch hosil qilamiz.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы убедимся, что вы понимаете, как избегать провоцирующего фактора.

phrasebook.phrase: Try to remain calm.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Постарайтесь сохранять спокойствие.

phrasebook.phrase: Let us know immediately if your breathing gets worse.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /let əs nəʊ ɪˈmiːdiətli ɪf jɔː ˈbriːðɪŋ ɡets wɜːs/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Nafasingiz yomonlashsa, darhol bizga xabar bering.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Немедленно сообщите нам, если ваше дыхание ухудшится.

phrasebook.phrase: Let us know if you feel faint again.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /let əs nəʊ ɪf juː fiːl feɪnt əˈɡen/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Yana hushdan ketayozgandek bo'lsangiz, bizga xabar bering.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите нам, если снова почувствуете предобморочное состояние.

grammar.title: Reported Speech
grammar.structure_pattern: said (that) + clause with tense shifted back | told + object + (that) … | asked + if / wh-word …
grammar.signal_words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Reported Speech — boshqa odamning aytgan gapini aynan takrorlamasdan, uning mazmunini yetkazish. Dialogda bemor do'stining aytgan gapini shunday yetkazadi: Signal so'zlar: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Reported Speech (косвенная речь) — это передача слов другого человека не дословно, а по смыслу. Сигнальные слова: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Reported Speech relays what someone said without quoting: "My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction". Tenses usually shift back (is → was, has → had, will → would); questions use "if" or a wh-word with statement word order. Signal words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.

grammar.title: Basic Structure of Reported Speech
grammar.structure_pattern: Reporting verb + that + reported statement
grammar.signal_words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: O'zlashtirma gap birovning gapini iqtibossiz yetkazadi: "My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction". Zamon odatda orqaga siljiydi (is → was, has → had, will → would); savollar "if" yoki so'roq so'zi bilan, darak gap tartibida beriladi. Signal so'zlar: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: I was having... — косвенная часть предложения. Сигнальные слова: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Reported Speech relays what someone said without quoting: "My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction". Tenses usually shift back (is → was, has → had, will → would); questions use "if" or a wh-word with statement word order. Signal words: said, told, asked, explained, advised, backshift.

grammar.title: Backshift
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Reported Speech'da reporting verb o'tgan zamonda bo'lsa, ko'pincha ikkinchi qismdagi zamon ham bir pog'ona orqaga siljiydi.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Reported Speech'da reporting verb o'tgan zamonda bo'lsa, ko'pincha ikkinchi qismdagi zamon ham bir pog'ona orqaga siljiydi.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Simple → Past Simple Present Continuous → Past Continuous

grammar.title: Reporting Medical Advice
grammar.structure_pattern: told me + that + should
grammar.signal_words: advice, recommendation
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu klinik tavsiyalarni reported speech'da berish uchun juda foydali. Signal so'zlar: advice, recommendation.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Should» и «ought to» выражают совет и рекомендацию — самый частый способ сказать пациенту, что делать: «You should drink plenty of fluids», «You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice». Сигнальные слова: advice, recommendation.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Should" and "ought to" give advice and recommendations — the most common way to tell a patient what to do: "You should drink plenty of fluids", "You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice". Signal words: advice, recommendation.

grammar.title: Should in Reported Speech
grammar.structure_pattern: should / ought to + V1 | shouldn't + V1 | said (that) + clause with tense shifted back | told + object + (that) … | asked + if / wh-word …
grammar.signal_words: advice, recommendation
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: should maslahat yoki tavsiyani bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: advice, recommendation.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: should используется для выражения совета или рекомендации. Сигнальные слова: advice, recommendation.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Should" and "ought to" give advice and recommendations — the most common way to tell a patient what to do: "You should drink plenty of fluids", "You shouldn't stop your insulin without medical advice". Reported Speech relays what someone said without quoting: "My friend said that I was having an allergic reaction". Tenses usually shift back (is → was, has → had, will → would); questions use "if" or a wh-word with statement word order. Signal words: advice, recommendation.

grammar.title: Past Simple
grammar.structure_pattern: Subject + V2 (V-ed) | Did + subject + V1? | was / were
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Past Simple tugallangan o'tmishdagi voqealarni bildiradi. qanday simptomlar paydo bo'lganini; Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Simple используется для завершённых действий в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

grammar.title: Past Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: while, when, at that moment, all morning
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu o'tmishdagi ma'lum bir vaqtda davom etayotgan jarayonni bildiradi. Signal so'zlar: while, when, at that moment, all morning.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Используется для действия, которое находилось в процессе в определённый момент в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: while, when, at that moment, all morning.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Continuous describes an action in progress at a moment in the past, often interrupted by a Past Simple event: "I was carrying boxes when I suddenly felt chest pain". It gives the background of the onset. Signal words: while, when, at that moment, all morning.

grammar.title: Past Perfect Continuous
grammar.structure_pattern: Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: for, since, before, until
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Past Perfect Continuous o'tmishdagi boshqa voqeadan oldin bir muddat davom etgan harakatni bildiradi: "I had been feeling dizzy for ten minutes before I collapsed". Asosiy voqeadan oldingi davomiylikni ta'kidlaydi. Signal so'zlar: for, since, before, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Past Perfect Continuous описывает действие, которое длилось некоторое время до другого события в прошлом: «I had been feeling dizzy for ten minutes before I collapsed». Подчёркивает длительность до ключевого события. Сигнальные слова: for, since, before, until.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Perfect Continuous describes an action that had been going on for some time before another past event: "I had been feeling dizzy for ten minutes before I collapsed". It stresses duration before the key event. Signal words: for, since, before, until.

practice.setting: emergency department / resuscitation bay
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Oliver Grant
patient_profile.personality_trait: distressed, worried, answers briefly because of discomfort

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I suddenly became very unwell after eating some food at a restaurant. My lips started swelling, and I found it difficult to breathe.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: That's important. Your symptoms suggest that you're having a severe allergic reaction, possibly anaphylaxis. We're going to treat you immediately.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Hello. Can you tell me what happened?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I suddenly became very unwell after eating some food at a restaurant. My lips started swelling, and I found it difficult to breathe.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How long ago did the symptoms start?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: About twenty minutes ago. I had been eating for about half an hour when I suddenly felt that something was wrong.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What did you notice first?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: My mouth started tingling, and then my lips and tongue began to swell. I also developed an itchy rash across my chest and arms.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Hello. What brought you to the emergency department today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been having severe abdominal pain since last night, and it has become much worse this morning.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Can you tell me where the pain started?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It started around my belly button, but it has gradually moved to the lower right side of my abdomen.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How would you describe the pain?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: It's sharp and constant. Moving around seems to make it worse.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed anything that makes the pain better?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Staying still seems to help a little, but walking makes it much worse.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you had any nausea or vomiting?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've felt nauseous since this morning, and I've vomited twice.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you been able to eat or drink anything?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Not really. I don't feel like eating, and drinking seems to make the nausea worse.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you had any diarrhoea or constipation?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No diarrhoea, but I haven't opened my bowels since yesterday.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any fever or chills?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I felt feverish earlier, but I haven't checked my temperature.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you had this kind of pain before?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, I've never experienced anything like this before.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you taken anything for the pain?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I tried taking some paracetamol, but it didn't help much.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to examine your abdomen now. Try to relax as much as possible.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Does it hurt when I press here?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, especially when you press on the lower right side.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I can see that you're uncomfortable. The tenderness in this area needs to be investigated further.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Do you think it could be appendicitis?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It's one possibility, but we need to carry out some tests before making a diagnosis.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What tests will I need?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You'll probably need blood tests and an abdominal scan. We may also need to monitor your temperature and other vital signs.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need surgery?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It's too early to say. If the tests show that your appendix is inflamed, surgery may be recommended to remove it.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: For now, avoid eating or drinking until we've completed the initial assessment. We'll also give you appropriate pain relief and monitor your condition closely.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay. Thank you.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Let us know immediately if the pain becomes suddenly worse or if you develop severe vomiting, dizziness, or difficulty breathing.

grammar.title: Gerund — V-ing
grammar.structure_pattern: verb + V-ing (avoid, stop, keep, recommend) | verb + to + V1 (need, want, decide, advise sb to)
grammar.signal_words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Gerund (V-ing) ot vazifasida keladi va avoid, stop, keep, recommend fe'llari hamda predloglardan keyin ishlatiladi ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitiv (to + V1) need, want, decide, advise someone dan keyin keladi va maqsadni bildiradi ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal so'zlar: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Герундий (V-ing) выступает как существительное после глаголов avoid, stop, keep, recommend и предлогов («Avoid eating before the test»). Инфинитив (to + V1) стоит после need, want, decide, advise someone и выражает цель («We need to run some tests», «in order to rule out appendicitis»). Сигнальные слова: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Gerunds (V-ing) act as nouns and follow verbs like avoid, stop, keep, recommend and prepositions ("Avoid eating before the test"). Infinitives (to + V1) follow need, want, decide, advise someone and express purpose ("We need to run some tests", "in order to rule out appendicitis"). Signal words: avoid -ing, need to, in order to, before -ing.

practice.setting: emergency department / resuscitation bay
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Olivia Brooks
patient_profile.personality_trait: distressed, worried, answers briefly because of discomfort

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I've been having severe abdominal pain since last night, and it has become much worse this morning.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Hello. What brought you to the emergency department today?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've been having severe abdominal pain since last night, and it has become much worse this morning.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Can you tell me where the pain started?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It started around my belly button, but it has gradually moved to the lower right side of my abdomen.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How would you describe the pain?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: It's sharp and constant. Moving around seems to make it worse.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed anything that makes the pain better?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Staying still seems to help a little, but walking makes it much worse.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you had any nausea or vomiting?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I've felt nauseous since this morning, and I've vomited twice.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you been able to eat or drink anything?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Not really. I don't feel like eating, and drinking seems to make the nausea worse.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you had any diarrhoea or constipation?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No diarrhoea, but I haven't opened my bowels since yesterday.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed any fever or chills?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I felt feverish earlier, but I haven't checked my temperature.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you had this kind of pain before?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, I've never experienced anything like this before.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you taken anything for the pain?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I tried taking some paracetamol, but it didn't help much.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. I'm going to examine your abdomen now. Try to relax as much as possible.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Does it hurt when I press here?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, especially when you press on the lower right side.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I can see that you're uncomfortable. The tenderness in this area needs to be investigated further.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Do you think it could be appendicitis?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It's one possibility, but we need to carry out some tests before making a diagnosis.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What tests will I need?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You'll probably need blood tests and an abdominal scan. We may also need to monitor your temperature and other vital signs.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I need surgery?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It's too early to say. If the tests show that your appendix is inflamed, surgery may be recommended to remove it.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: All right. I'm going to examine your abdomen now. Try to relax as much as possible.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Does it hurt when I press here?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, especially when you press on the lower right side.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I can see that you're uncomfortable. The tenderness in this area needs to be investigated further.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Do you think it could be appendicitis?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It's one possibility, but we need to carry out some tests before making a diagnosis.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What tests will I need?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: You'll probably need blood tests and an abdominal scan. We may also need to monitor your temperature and other vital signs.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I need surgery?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: It's too early to say. If the tests show that your appendix is inflamed, surgery may be recommended to remove it.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I understand.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Hello. Can you tell me what has been happening?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been feeling very unwell since yesterday. I developed a high fever, and I've been feeling extremely weak.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed anything else?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've been shivering a lot, and I became confused earlier today. I also feel short of breath.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did the confusion start?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: About two hours ago. My wife noticed that I was answering questions slowly and seemed confused.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you had any recent infections or illnesses?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I've had a painful wound on my leg for several days. The area around it has become red and swollen.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Was the wound caused by an injury?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I cut my leg while working in the garden about five days ago.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has the wound been getting worse?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. The redness has been spreading, and I've noticed some fluid coming from the wound.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I can see a swollen area surrounding the wound. The skin covered with redness also feels warm.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Is it serious?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Your condition is concerning. You have a high temperature, a fast heart rate, and low blood pressure. Together with the infected wound and your confusion, these findings could indicate sepsis.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What does that mean?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Sepsis is a serious condition caused by the body's response to an infection. If it becomes severe, it can lead to septic shock.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What will happen now?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We need to act quickly. Blood samples taken immediately will be sent to the laboratory, and we'll check your blood pressure, oxygen level, and other vital signs closely.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need antibiotics?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes. You will be given antibiotics as soon as possible. You may also need intravenous fluids to support your blood pressure.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: What about the wound on my leg?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: The wound will be examined carefully. Any infected tissue requiring treatment may need to be cleaned or removed.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I have to stay in hospital?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes. Given your symptoms and low blood pressure, you will need close monitoring in hospital. If your blood pressure remains low despite treatment, you may need care in an intensive care unit.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm quite worried.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: I understand. The important thing is that you've come in early. The treatment started promptly can improve the chances of recovery.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay. What should I do now?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Please remain in bed and let us know immediately if you develop worsening breathlessness, chest pain, severe dizziness, or become more confused. We'll continue monitoring you closely.

grammar.title: Present Participle — V-ing
grammar.structure_pattern: V-ing + noun | V-ing clause
grammar.signal_words: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Hozirgi zamon sifatdoshi (-ing) faol jarayonni ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"), o'tgan zamon sifatdoshi (V3) holat yoki natijani ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately") bildiradi. Ular nisbiy ergash gaplarni qisqartiradi. Signal so'zlar: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present participle (-ing) faol harakatni bildiradi. Present participle (-ing) обозначает действие, которое выполняет сам предмет/человек. Сигнальные слова: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present participles (-ing) describe an active process ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"); past participles (V3) describe a state or result ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately"). They shorten relative clauses. Signal words: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.

grammar.title: Past Participle — V3
grammar.structure_pattern: V3 + noun | V3 phrase
grammar.signal_words: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Past participle (V3) ko'pincha passiv ma'noni bildiradi. Past participle (V3) часто имеет пассивное значение. Signal so'zlar: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Причастие настоящего времени (-ing) описывает активный процесс («a spreading infection», «the patient lying in bed»); причастие прошедшего времени (V3) — состояние или результат («an infected wound», «samples taken immediately»). Они сокращают придаточные предложения. Сигнальные слова: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present participles (-ing) describe an active process ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"); past participles (V3) describe a state or result ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately"). They shorten relative clauses. Signal words: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.

grammar.title: Reduced Relative Clauses — Present Participle
grammar.structure_pattern: V-ing + noun (active) | V3 + noun (passive) | noun + V-ing / V3 phrase | noun + who / which / that / whose / where + clause
grammar.signal_words: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: A relative clause with who/that + be + V-ing can often be shortened to V-ing. who/that + be + V-ing shaklidagi relative clause ko'pincha V-ing bilan qisqartiriladi. Придаточное с who/that + be + V-ing часто можно сократить до формы V-ing. Passive relative clauses can often be reduced by removing who/that + be and keeping V3. Passiv relative clause qisqartirilganda who/that + be olib tashlanib, V3 saqlanadi. Пассивное относительное придаточное можно сократить, убрав who/that + be и оставив V3. Signal so'zlar: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Причастие настоящего времени (-ing) описывает активный процесс («a spreading infection», «the patient lying in bed»); причастие прошедшего времени (V3) — состояние или результат («an infected wound», «samples taken immediately»). Они сокращают придаточные предложения. Определительные придаточные добавляют информацию о существительном: «the patient who collapsed at work», «a test which measures kidney function». Ограничительные (defining) пишутся без запятых и уточняют существительное; распространительные (non-defining) выделяются запятыми. Сигнальные слова: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present participles (-ing) describe an active process ("a spreading infection", "the patient lying in bed"); past participles (V3) describe a state or result ("an infected wound", "samples taken immediately"). They shorten relative clauses. Relative clauses add information about a noun: "the patient who collapsed at work", "a test which measures kidney function". Defining clauses have no commas and identify the noun; non-defining clauses add extra information between commas. Signal words: -ing, -ed, taken, lying, spreading.

practice.setting: emergency department / resuscitation bay
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Emma Hale
patient_profile.personality_trait: distressed, worried, answers briefly because of discomfort

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I've been feeling very unwell since yesterday. I developed a high fever, and I've been feeling extremely weak.
doctor_explanations_from_reference_dialo: Your condition is concerning. You have a high temperature, a fast heart rate, and low blood pressure. Together with the infected wound and your confusion, these findings could indicate sepsis.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Hello. Can you tell me what has been happening?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I've been feeling very unwell since yesterday. I developed a high fever, and I've been feeling extremely weak.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you noticed anything else?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I've been shivering a lot, and I became confused earlier today. I also feel short of breath.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When did the confusion start?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: About two hours ago. My wife noticed that I was answering questions slowly and seemed confused.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you had any recent infections or illnesses?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I've had a painful wound on my leg for several days. The area around it has become red and swollen.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Was the wound caused by an injury?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I cut my leg while working in the garden about five days ago.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has the wound been getting worse?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. The redness has been spreading, and I've noticed some fluid coming from the wound.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I can see a swollen area surrounding the wound. The skin covered with redness also feels warm.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Is it serious?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Your condition is concerning. You have a high temperature, a fast heart rate, and low blood pressure. Together with the infected wound and your confusion, these findings could ind…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What does that mean?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Sepsis is a serious condition caused by the body's response to an infection. If it becomes severe, it can lead to septic shock.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What will happen now?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: We need to act quickly. Blood samples taken immediately will be sent to the laboratory, and we'll check your blood pressure, oxygen level, and other vital signs closely.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I need antibiotics?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. You will be given antibiotics as soon as possible. You may also need intravenous fluids to support your blood pressure.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: What about the wound on my leg?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: The wound will be examined carefully. Any infected tissue requiring treatment may need to be cleaned or removed.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Will I have to stay in hospital?

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Yes. Given your symptoms and low blood pressure, you will need close monitoring in hospital. If your blood pressure remains low despite treatment, you may need care in an intensiv…
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm quite worried.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: I understand. The important thing is that you've come in early. The treatment started promptly can improve the chances of recovery.
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Okay. What should I do now?

questions_to_ask_doctor: Is it serious?
What does that mean?
What will happen now?
Will I need antibiotics?
What about the wound on my leg?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Hello. Tell me exactly what happened.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Doctor, we were in a car accident about 20 minutes ago. His chest hit the steering wheel very hard. More importantly, he has a deep cut on his left thigh, and we cannot stop the bleeding.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you apply firm direct pressure to the wound? Have you used a tourniquet?

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: We wrapped the wound with medical gauze from the first-aid kit, but it isn't stopping the bleeding. He has lost a lot of blood.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did he lose consciousness at any point?

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: No, but his face has gone very pale, and he is becoming extremely weak.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Doctor... I feel dizzy... and very cold...

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Can you hear me? Where do you have severe pain?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My chest... I can hardly breathe... and my abdomen hurts badly.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Stay with me. We are going to help you. Nurses, take him to the Emergency Room immediately. Apply firm pressure to the thigh and a tourniquet if the bleeding cannot be controlled.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Assess his airway and breathing immediately. Put him on the monitor and check his heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Establish two large-bore IV lines and start emergency fluid and blood-product resuscitation according to the trauma protocol.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Give him oxygen and keep him warm. He is showing signs of severe blood loss and hemorrhagic shock.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Prepare for a FAST scan to look for internal bleeding, especially because of the chest and abdominal trauma. Call the trauma surgeon immediately.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Doctor, is it really that dangerous?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes. He is in critical condition because of severe blood loss and multiple injuries. Our immediate priorities are to control the bleeding, support his circulation, and assess for internal injuries.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If we find significant internal bleeding or other serious injuries, he may need emergency surgery. Please wait outside. We will update you as soon as possible.
