grammar.title: Imperative
grammar.structure_pattern: V1 + object
grammar.signal_words: please, do not, never, always
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Imperative buyruq, ko'rsatma, iltimos yoki tezkor topshiriq berish uchun ishlatiladi. Tibbiyotda, ayniqsa emergency vaziyatlarda, shifokor va hamshiralar o'rtasidagi tezkor ko'rsatmalarda juda ko'p ishlatiladi. Buyruq gapda odatda you ishlatilmaydi. Signal so'zlar: please, do not, never, always.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Imperative используется для приказов, инструкций, просьб и указаний. В медицинском английском, особенно в экстренных ситуациях, эта форма часто используется для быстрых и чётких команд. ⚠️ Eslab qoling / Запомните Сигнальные слова: please, do not, never, always.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Imperatives give direct instructions and emergency commands: "Take a deep breath", "Do not eat or drink anything", "Call an ambulance immediately". "Please" or "could you" softens them for patients. Signal words: please, do not, never, always.

grammar.title: Present Perfect
grammar.structure_pattern: have / has + V3
grammar.signal_words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Perfect o'tmishda sodir bo'lgan, lekin natijasi hozir muhim bo'lgan harakatni ifodalaydi. Tibbiyotda bu zamon bemorning hozirgi holatiga ta'sir qilayotgan oldingi voqealarni tasvirlashda juda foydali. Nima uchun Present Perfect? Qon yo'qotish oldin boshlangan, lekin uning natijasi hozir ham mavjud: bemor holsiz, oqarib ketgan va shok belgilari bor. Compare / Taqqoslang / Сравните U ko'p qon yo'qotgan. Signal so'zlar: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Perfect используется, когда действие произошло в прошлом, но его результат важен в настоящем. В медицинском английском это время часто используется для описания предыдущего события, которое влияет на состояние пациента сейчас. Потеря крови произошла раньше, но её результат виден сейчас: пациент слабый, бледный, у него признаки шока. Этот вопрос помогает врачу узнать, что уже было сделано до настоящего момента. Он потерял много крови. Сигнальные слова: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Perfect links a past event to the present: an experience, a recent event or a result that matters now. In history taking it asks about symptoms and events up to now: "Have you had any fever?", "I have vomited three times". Signal words: already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for, recently, so far.

grammar.structure_pattern: am / is / are + V-ing
grammar.signal_words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Present Continuous ayni paytda sodir bo'layotgan yoki hozir rivojlanib/o'zgarib borayotgan jarayonni ifodalaydi. Tibbiyotda bemorning holati ayni vaqtda o'zgarayotganini ko'rsatish uchun juda foydali. Bu yerda bemorning holati hozir yomonlashib boryapti. Signal so'zlar: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Present Continuous используется для действия или процесса, который происходит сейчас, в данный момент. В медицинском английском он особенно полезен для описания изменяющегося состояния пациента. Здесь состояние пациента ухудшается прямо сейчас. Eslab qoling / Запомните Сигнальные слова: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Present Continuous describes what is happening now or a temporary, changing situation: "His condition is getting worse", "I am going to examine you now". It is also used for the immediate plan of the clinician. Signal words: now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.

examples.sentence: He is becoming extremely weak.

examples.sentence: He is showing signs of severe blood loss.

grammar.title: Modal Verb May
grammar.structure_pattern: may + V1
grammar.signal_words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: May biror hodisa yoki holatning ehtimolini bildiradi. Tibbiyotda shifokor natija hali aniq bo'lmaganda may dan foydalanadi. Shifokor operatsiya albatta kerak demayapti. Faqat ehtimolni bildiryapti. may dan keyin fe'lning oddiy shakli keladi: Signal so'zlar: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: May используется для выражения возможности или вероятности. В медицинском английском врач использует may, когда результат ещё точно не определён. Врач не говорит, что операция точно необходима. Он говорит о возможности. ⚠️ Muhim / Важно Сигнальные слова: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. Signal words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.

examples.sentence: He may need emergency surgery.
examples.translation_uz: Unga shoshilinch operatsiya kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
examples.translation_ru: Ему может потребоваться экстренная операция.

grammar.title: First Conditional
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Present Simple, may + V1
grammar.signal_words: if, unless, as soon as, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: First Conditional kelajakda yuz berishi mumkin bo'lgan shart va uning ehtimoliy natijasini ifodalaydi. Ya'ni if-clause ichida Present Simple ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: First Conditional используется для описания реального или возможного условия в будущем и его возможного результата. ⚠️ Muhim / Важно После if для будущего значения обычно используется Present Simple, а не will. Сигнальные слова: if, unless, as soon as, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: First Conditional describes a real, possible future situation and its result. Clinicians use it for warnings, plans and safety-netting: "If the pain gets worse, you should come back immediately". Do not use "will" after "if". Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: if, unless, as soon as, when.

grammar.title: Past Simple Questions
grammar.structure_pattern: Past Simple'da savol tuzishda did + subject + V1 ishlatiladi.
grammar.signal_words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Did ishlatilsa, asosiy fe'l V1 bo'ladi. Signal so'zlar: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: В вопросах в Past Simple используется вспомогательный глагол did, после которого смысловой глагол ставится в начальной форме (V1). ⚠️ Muhim / Важно Сигнальные слова: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: yesterday, last night, two days ago, in 2020, when.

grammar.title: Can
grammar.structure_pattern: can / could + V1 | Can you …? | Could you …, please?
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Can qobiliyat, imkoniyat yoki bemorning hozirgi holatini tekshirish uchun ishlatilishi mumkin. Bu emergency vaziyatda bemorning hushyorligi va javob bera olish qobiliyatini tezda tekshirish uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Can используется для выражения способности, возможности, а в медицинском контексте — для быстрой проверки состояния пациента. В экстренной ситуации этот вопрос помогает быстро проверить уровень сознания и способность пациента реагировать. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

grammar.title: Clinical Grammar Patterns
grammar.structure_pattern: He is + adjective | He is + V-ing | He has + V3 | He may + V1 | If + Present Simple, may + V1
grammar.signal_words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "May" va "might" ehtimollik va ehtiyotkor klinik xulosani bildiradi: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" muloyim ruxsat ham beradi. "Might have + V3" — o'tmishdagi ehtimol. Present Simple odatiy, takrorlanuvchi harakatlar, umumiy faktlar va doimiy holatlarni bildiradi. Klinikada odatdagi simptomlar ("The pain usually starts at night"), muntazam dori qabuli va umumiy tibbiy faktlar uchun ishlatiladi. Signal so'zlar: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «May» и «might» выражают возможность и осторожное клиническое суждение: «It may be an infection», «You might need to stay in hospital». «May» также даёт вежливое разрешение. «Might have + V3» — возможное событие в прошлом. Present Simple описывает привычные, регулярные действия, общие факты и постоянные состояния. В клинике используется для типичных симптомов («The pain usually starts at night»), регулярного приёма лекарств и общих медицинских фактов. Сигнальные слова: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. Present Simple describes habits, routines, general facts and permanent states. In the clinic it is used for typical symptoms ("The pain usually starts at night"), regular medication and general medical facts. Signal words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.

grammar.title: Quick Grammar Guide
grammar.structure_pattern: V1! | have/has + V3 | am/is/are + V-ing | may + V1 | If + Present, may + V1 | Did + V1? | Can + V1? | has/have + V3
grammar.signal_words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Hamma grammatik qoidani birdan yodlash shart emas. Avval gapdagi grammatik signalni toping, keyin uning ma'nosini aniqlang. Signal so'zlar: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Не нужно сразу запоминать все грамматические правила. Сначала найдите грамматический сигнал в предложении, а затем определите его значение. Сигнальные слова: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.

modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Syncope & Unexplained Collapse. Grammar focus: Relative Clauses — Defining & Non-defining. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 41 vocabulary items, 49 smart phrases, 13 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. I understand you had an episode of collapse at work. Can you tell me what happened from the beginning?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I was standing in the office when I suddenly felt weak. My vision became blurred, and I felt as if I was going to faint. A few seconds later, I collapsed.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you remember everything that happened, or did you completely lose consciousness?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I don't remember the actual moment when I collapsed. The next thing I remember is waking up on the floor.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How long were you unconscious, as far as you know?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm not sure. My colleague said I was unconscious for about a minute.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you have any warning symptoms before you collapsed?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. I felt light-headed, my vision became blurred, and I started sweating. I also felt very weak.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you have any chest pain, palpitations, or difficulty breathing before you collapsed?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I felt my heart beating very fast, but I didn't have any chest pain or breathing problems.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What happened after you regained consciousness?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I was confused for a few seconds, but I recovered quite quickly. I felt tired afterwards.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did anyone notice any shaking or unusual movements while you were unconscious?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My colleague said that my arms moved a little, but there was no prolonged shaking.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Did you bite your tongue or lose control of your bladder?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No, neither of those happened.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you ever had a similar episode before?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I nearly fainted once last year when I had a blood test, but I have never completely lost consciousness before.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you have any medical conditions?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I have mild hypertension, which was diagnosed about three years ago.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: What medication are you taking for it?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I take amlodipine every morning.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you taken your medication as usual recently?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, although I haven't been drinking enough water lately because I've been very busy.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you eaten normally today?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: No. I skipped breakfast and only had coffee.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How much coffee did you have?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Three large cups before noon.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you drink alcohol or use recreational drugs?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I drink occasionally, but I don't use drugs.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has anyone in your family had heart problems or unexplained sudden death?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My father, who had a heart attack at 52, has high blood pressure, but there is no history of sudden death.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. There are several possible causes for your collapse. Dehydration, not eating, and prolonged standing could have contributed to a fainting episode. However, because you experienced palpitations before losing consciousness, we also need to rule out a heart rhythm problem.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean there could be something serious?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: It is possible, although we cannot say that yet. We need to check your blood pressure, blood glucose, ECG, and blood tests. Depending on the results, we may need further cardiac assessment.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: For now, please remain seated and avoid standing up suddenly. If you develop chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or another episode of collapse, tell us immediately.

grammar.title: Relative Clauses
grammar.structure_pattern: noun + who / which / that / whose / where + clause
grammar.signal_words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Relative clause — ot yoki olmosh haqida qo'shimcha ma'lumot beradigan gap qismi. who collapsed — qaysi bemor ekanini aniqlab beradi. Qaysi bemor? → Yiqilgan bemor. Relative clauses ayniqsa tibbiy ingliz tilida juda foydali, chunki ular anamnez va klinik ma'lumotni aniq, ixcham va professional tarzda ifodalashga yordam beradi. Signal so'zlar: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Relative clause — это придаточное определительное предложение, которое даёт дополнительную или уточняющую информацию о существительном или местоимении. the patient — пациент; who collapsed — уточняет, какой именно пациент имеется в виду. Какой пациент? → Пациент, который потерял сознание. В медицинском английском такие конструкции особенно полезны при сборе анамнеза, описании симптомов и объяснении клинической ситуации. Сигнальные слова: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Relative clauses add information about a noun: "the patient who collapsed at work", "a test which measures kidney function". Defining clauses have no commas and identify the noun; non-defining clauses add extra information between commas. Signal words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.

examples.translation_ru: Объяснение на русском

grammar.title: Defining Relative Clauses
grammar.structure_pattern: noun + who / which / that / whose / where + clause
grammar.signal_words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Defining Relative Clause shaxs yoki narsani aniqlash uchun zarur bo'lgan ma'lumotni beradi. Agar relative clause olib tashlansa, qaysi odam yoki narsa haqida gap ketayotganini bilish qiyinlashadi. Bu yerda who collapsed juda muhim. Signal so'zlar: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Defining Relative Clause содержит необходимую информацию, которая помогает определить, о каком именно человеке, пациенте или предмете идёт речь. Если убрать эту часть предложения, становится непонятно, какой именно пациент или предмет имеется в виду. Сигнальные слова: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Relative clauses add information about a noun: "the patient who collapsed at work", "a test which measures kidney function". Defining clauses have no commas and identify the noun; non-defining clauses add extra information between commas. Signal words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.

grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Определительные придаточные добавляют информацию о существительном: «the patient who collapsed at work», «a test which measures kidney function». Ограничительные (defining) пишутся без запятых и уточняют существительное; распространительные (non-defining) выделяются запятыми. Сигнальные слова: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Relative clauses add information about a noun: "the patient who collapsed at work", "a test which measures kidney function". Defining clauses have no commas and identify the noun; non-defining clauses add extra information between commas. Signal words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.

grammar.title: Non-Defining Relative Clauses
grammar.structure_pattern: noun + who / which / that / whose / where + clause
grammar.signal_words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Non-defining Relative Clause shaxs yoki narsa haqida qo'shimcha ma'lumot beradi. Bu ma'lumot asosiy gap uchun majburiy emas. Agar relative clause olib tashlansa ham, asosiy gapning ma'nosi saqlanib qoladi. Bu yerda my father kimligi allaqachon ma'lum. who had a heart attack at 52 — faqat qo'shimcha ma'lumot. Signal so'zlar: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Non-defining Relative Clause даёт дополнительную информацию о человеке или предмете, который уже известен из контекста. Эта информация не является необходимой для понимания основной мысли. Если убрать придаточную часть, основное предложение всё равно будет грамматически и смыслово полным. Сигнальные слова: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Relative clauses add information about a noun: "the patient who collapsed at work", "a test which measures kidney function". Defining clauses have no commas and identify the noun; non-defining clauses add extra information between commas. Signal words: who (people), which (things), that, whose, where.

practice.setting: emergency department / resuscitation bay
practice.role_play: The student is the DOCTOR. You play the PATIENT.

patient_profile.name: Jack Turner
patient_profile.personality_trait: distressed, worried, answers briefly because of discomfort

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I was standing in the office when I suddenly felt weak. My vision became blurred, and I felt as if I was going to faint. A few seconds later, I collapsed.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Good morning. I understand you had an episode of collapse at work. Can you tell me what happened from the beginning?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I was standing in the office when I suddenly felt weak. My vision became blurred, and I felt as if I was going to faint. A few seconds later, I collapsed.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you remember everything that happened, or did you completely lose consciousness?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I don't remember the actual moment when I collapsed. The next thing I remember is waking up on the floor.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How long were you unconscious, as far as you know?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm not sure. My colleague said I was unconscious for about a minute.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did you have any warning symptoms before you collapsed?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes. I felt light-headed, my vision became blurred, and I started sweating. I also felt very weak.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did you have any chest pain, palpitations, or difficulty breathing before you collapsed?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I felt my heart beating very fast, but I didn't have any chest pain or breathing problems.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What happened after you regained consciousness?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I was confused for a few seconds, but I recovered quite quickly. I felt tired afterwards.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did anyone notice any shaking or unusual movements while you were unconscious?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: My colleague said that my arms moved a little, but there was no prolonged shaking.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Did you bite your tongue or lose control of your bladder?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No, neither of those happened.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you ever had a similar episode before?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I nearly fainted once last year when I had a blood test, but I have never completely lost consciousness before.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you have any medical conditions?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I have mild hypertension, which was diagnosed about three years ago.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: What medication are you taking for it?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I take amlodipine every morning.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you taken your medication as usual recently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, although I haven't been drinking enough water lately because I've been very busy.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you eaten normally today?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: No. I skipped breakfast and only had coffee.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How much coffee did you have?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Three large cups before noon.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you drink alcohol or use recreational drugs?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I drink occasionally, but I don't use drugs.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has anyone in your family had heart problems or unexplained sudden death?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: My father, who had a heart attack at 52, has high blood pressure, but there is no history of sudden death.

questions_to_ask_doctor: Does that mean there could be something serious?

modules.description_ru: Модуль клинического общения: Острое отравление и передозировка. Грамматика: Mixed Conditionals. Эталонный диалог, 37 терминов, 61 smart-фраз, 15 грамматических тем и симуляция с виртуальным пациентом.
modules.description_en: Clinical communication module: Acute Intoxication & Overdose. Grammar focus: Mixed Conditionals. Includes a reference doctor–patient dialogue, 37 vocabulary items, 61 smart phrases, 15 grammar points and a virtual patient simulation.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Hello. I understand you were brought in because you became unwell after taking some medication. Can you tell me what happened?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm not completely sure. I took some tablets at home because I had a bad headache. A few hours later, I became very sleepy and started feeling sick.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you know exactly what you took?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I think they were painkillers, but I'm not sure which ones. They were in a bottle without a proper label.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: How many tablets did you take?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I honestly don't know. I took two at first, and then I took some more because the headache wasn't getting better.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Approximately how many tablets could you have taken altogether?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Maybe six or seven. It could have been more. I really can't remember.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did you take the first tablets, and when did you take the last ones?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I took the first two at about 6 p.m. Then I took more about an hour later.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you taken anything else today, including alcohol, sleeping tablets, or recreational drugs?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I had two glasses of wine earlier in the evening. I didn't take any sleeping tablets or drugs.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you vomited?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes, twice. I also feel very dizzy, and I'm having difficulty staying awake.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you have any chest pain or difficulty breathing?

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: My breathing feels a little slow, but I don't have chest pain.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has anyone found the medication bottle you took the tablets from?

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Yes, Doctor. I brought it with me. We found it beside his bed.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. We need to identify the medication and estimate how much was taken. Do you know whether he has taken any other medicines recently?

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: He takes medication for high blood pressure, but I don't know whether he took it today.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: That's important information. If we knew exactly what he had taken, we could assess the risk more accurately. Because the amount and type of medication are uncertain, we need to treat this as a potentially serious overdose.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: Am I going to be okay?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We cannot predict the outcome yet, but we are going to monitor you closely. We'll check your airway, breathing, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen level, and level of consciousness.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Could the alcohol make the situation worse?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes. Alcohol can increase the effects of some medications, particularly those that cause drowsiness or slow breathing. If he had taken a smaller amount, he might not be this drowsy now, but because the exact dose is unknown, we have to be cautious.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I didn't realise the tablets could be dangerous.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: If you had known what medication you were taking and how much you had already taken, you might have avoided taking the additional tablets. At the moment, however, our priority is to prevent further complications.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: We'll take blood samples, perform an ECG, and contact the toxicology team for further advice. Please do not give him anything to eat or drink until we have assessed his swallowing and level of consciousness.

dialogue.label: Relative
dialogue.text: Should I stay with him?

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: You can stay nearby, but please give the nurses any information you remember about the medication, including when he took it and approximately how many tablets may be missing.

dialogue.label: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. I'm sorry. I should have checked the bottle first.

dialogue.label: Doctor
dialogue.text: Don't worry about that right now. The important thing is that you told us what happened. We'll focus on keeping you safe and identifying the substance as quickly as possible.

phrasebook.phrase: Can you tell me what happened?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Можете рассказать, что произошло?

phrasebook.phrase: What did you take?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Что вы приняли?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you know exactly what you took?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /dʊ juː nəʊ ɪɡˈzæktli wɒt juː tʊk/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы точно знаете, что приняли?

phrasebook.phrase: How many tablets did you take?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сколько таблеток вы приняли?

phrasebook.phrase: Approximately how many tablets could you have taken?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /əˈprɒksɪmətli haʊ ˈmeni ˈtæbləts kʊd juː hæv ˈteɪkən/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Taxminan nechta tabletka qabul qilgan bo'lishingiz mumkin?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Примерно сколько таблеток вы могли принять?

phrasebook.phrase: When did you take the first tablets?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wen dɪd juː teɪk ðə fɜːst ˈtæbləts/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Когда вы приняли первые таблетки?

phrasebook.phrase: When did you take the last ones?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wen dɪd juː teɪk ðə lɑːst wʌnz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Когда вы приняли последние таблетки?

phrasebook.phrase: How long ago did you take them?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /haʊ lɒŋ əˈɡəʊ dɪd juː teɪk ðəm/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Как давно вы их приняли?

phrasebook.phrase: Did you take any more tablets afterwards?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /dɪd juː teɪk ˈeni mɔː ˈtæbləts ˈɑːftəwədz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы принимали ещё таблетки после этого?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you taken anything else today?
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bugun boshqa biror narsa qabul qildingizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы сегодня принимали что-нибудь ещё?

phrasebook.phrase: Did you drink any alcohol?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы употребляли алкоголь?

phrasebook.phrase: Did you take any sleeping tablets?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы принимали снотворные?

phrasebook.phrase: Did you use any recreational drugs?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы употребляли наркотики?

phrasebook.phrase: Have you vomited?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вас рвало?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you feeling dizzy?
phrasebook.translation_ru: У вас кружится голова?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you having difficulty staying awake?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам трудно оставаться в сознании?

phrasebook.phrase: Are you having difficulty breathing?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам трудно дышать?

phrasebook.phrase: Does your breathing feel slower than usual?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /dʌz jɔː ˈbriːðɪŋ fiːl ˈsləʊə ðən ˈjuːʒuəl/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вам кажется, что дыхание стало медленнее обычного?

phrasebook.phrase: Has anyone found the medication bottle?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Кто-нибудь нашёл флакон с лекарством?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you know whether he took any other medicines?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /dʊ juː nəʊ ˈweðə hiː tʊk ˈeni ˈʌðə ˈmedɪsɪnz/
phrasebook.translation_uz: U boshqa dorilarni qabul qilgan-qilmaganini bilasizmi?
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы знаете, принимал ли он другие лекарства?

phrasebook.phrase: Do you know how many tablets are missing?
phrasebook.pronunciation: /dʊ juː nəʊ haʊ ˈmeni ˈtæbləts ɑː ˈmɪsɪŋ/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вы знаете, сколько таблеток не хватает?

phrasebook.phrase: Please tell us anything you remember.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сообщите нам всё, что вы помните.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to assess the risk carefully.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː niːd tə əˈses ðə rɪsk ˈkeəfəli/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо тщательно оценить риск.

phrasebook.phrase: The exact dose is unknown.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Точная доза неизвестна.

phrasebook.phrase: The type of medication is uncertain.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Вид препарата неизвестен.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to treat this as a potentially serious overdose.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː niːd tə triːt ðɪs æz ə pəˈtenʃəli ˈsɪəriəs ˈəʊvədəʊs/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Buni jiddiy bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan overdose sifatida ko'rishimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы должны расценивать это как потенциально серьёзную передозировку.

phrasebook.phrase: We have to be cautious.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы должны соблюдать осторожность.

phrasebook.phrase: We are going to monitor you closely.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː ə ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ˈmɒnɪtə juː ˈkləʊsli/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы будем внимательно наблюдать за вами.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll check your airway and breathing.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы проверим дыхательные пути и дыхание.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll check your level of consciousness.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы проверим уровень сознания.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll take blood samples.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы возьмём образцы крови.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll perform an ECG.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы сделаем ЭКГ.

phrasebook.phrase: We'll contact the toxicology team.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Мы свяжемся с токсикологической службой.

phrasebook.phrase: Please do not give him anything to eat or drink.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /pliːz duː nɒt ɡɪv ɪm ˈeniθɪŋ tə iːt ɔː drɪŋk/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Не давайте ему ничего есть или пить.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to assess his swallowing first.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː niːd tə əˈses hɪz ˈswɒləʊɪŋ fɜːst/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Avval uning yutish qobiliyatini baholashimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Сначала нам нужно оценить его способность глотать.

phrasebook.phrase: Tell us immediately if his breathing changes.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /tel ʌs ɪˈmiːdiətli ɪf hɪz ˈbriːðɪŋ ˈtʃeɪndʒɪz/
phrasebook.translation_ru: Немедленно сообщите нам, если его дыхание изменится.

phrasebook.phrase: I'm not completely sure.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я не совсем уверен.

phrasebook.phrase: I honestly don't know.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Честно говоря, я не знаю.

phrasebook.phrase: It could have been more.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Возможно, было больше.

phrasebook.phrase: I really can't remember.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Я действительно не могу вспомнить.

phrasebook.phrase: We cannot predict the outcome yet.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Пока мы не можем предсказать исход.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to identify the medication.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо определить препарат.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to estimate how much was taken.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /wiː niːd tə ˈestɪmeɪt haʊ mʌtʃ wəz ˈteɪkən/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Qancha qabul qilinganini taxmin qilishimiz kerak.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо приблизительно определить, какое количество было принято.

phrasebook.phrase: This information is important.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Эта информация важна.

phrasebook.phrase: We need to prevent further complications.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Нам необходимо предотвратить дальнейшие осложнения.

phrasebook.phrase: Our priority is to keep you safe.
phrasebook.pronunciation: /aʊə praɪˈɒrəti ɪz tə kiːp juː seɪf/
phrasebook.translation_uz: Bizning asosiy maqsadimiz sizning xavfsizligingizni ta'minlash.
phrasebook.translation_ru: Наша главная задача — обеспечить вашу безопасность.

grammar.title: Mixed Conditionals
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Past Perfect, would/might/could + V1 | If + had + V3 | If + Past Perfect → would/might/could + V1
grammar.signal_words: if … had …, now
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Mixed Conditional — shart gapning sharti va natijasi turli vaqtga tegishli bo'lgan gapdir. Bu mavzu tibbiy ingliz tilida juda muhim, chunki shifokor bemorning o'tmishda qilgan harakati uning hozirgi holatiga qanday ta'sir qilganini tushuntirishi mumkin. now → natija hozirga tegishli ekanini ko'rsatadi. Past Perfect o'tmishda boshqa bir voqeadan oldin sodir bo'lgan harakatni bildiradi. Ammo aslida u kamroq miqdorda qabul qilmagan. Shuning uchun bu unreal / hypothetical past. Might not be hozirgi ehtimoliy natijani bildiradi. Might ishlatilgani uchun shifokor natijani 100% aniq deb aytmayapti. Bu klinik kommunikatsiyada juda muhim. Signal so'zlar: if … had …, now.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Mixed Conditional — это условное предложение, в котором условие и результат относятся к разным временным периодам. Если бы он принял меньшее количество препарата, возможно, сейчас он не был бы настолько сонливым. had taken — действие относится к прошлому; might not be — результат относится к настоящему; now показывает, что результат наблюдается сейчас. ПРОШЛОЕ ДЕЙСТВИЕ → РЕЗУЛЬТАТ СЕЙЧАС Она используется, потому что речь идёт о нереальном условии в прошлом. Он фактически принял большее количество, поэтому врач говорит о возможном другом варианте прошлого. Might not be показывает предполагаемый, не абсолютно уверенный результат в настоящем. Врач не утверждает, что состояние пациента точно было бы другим. Это делает медицинское высказывание более осторожным и профессиональным. Сигнальные слова: if … had …, now.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Mixed Conditional combines a past condition with a present result: "If he had taken a smaller amount, he might not be this drowsy now". It links a past decision to the current clinical picture. Past Perfect shows that one past action happened before another past action: "I had eaten a large meal before the pain started". It orders events in the clinical timeline. Signal words: if … had …, now.

grammar.title: "if We Knew..." — Hypothetical Present
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Past Simple → could/would/might + V1
grammar.signal_words: if, if I were you
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu yerda shifokor hozirgi vaziyat haqida gapiryapti. Biz hozir dorining aniq turini bilmaymiz. Signal so'zlar: if, if I were you.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: На данный момент мы не знаем точно, какой препарат был принят. Если бы мы знали... Сигнальные слова: if, if I were you.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Second Conditional describes an unreal or unlikely present/future situation: "If we knew exactly what he had taken, we could assess the risk better". "If I were you, I would…" gives tactful advice. Past Simple describes completed events at a definite time in the past: "The pain started yesterday", "When did you take the last dose?". Use it whenever the time is finished or stated. Signal words: if, if I were you.

grammar.title: "could" — Possibility — Ability
grammar.structure_pattern: can / could + V1 | Can you …? | Could you …, please?
grammar.signal_words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "Can" qobiliyat, ruxsat va hozirgi ehtimollikni bildiradi ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" yumshoqroq, muloyimroq ("Could you describe the pain?") va o'tmishdagi qobiliyatni ifodalaydi. Signal so'zlar: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: «Can» выражает способность, разрешение и возможность в настоящем («DKA can become life-threatening»); «could» — более мягкий, вежливый вариант («Could you describe the pain?») и способность в прошлом. Сигнальные слова: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "Can" expresses ability, permission and present possibility ("DKA can become life-threatening"); "could" is more tentative or polite ("Could you describe the pain?") and refers to past ability. Signal words: ability, permission, polite request, possibility.

examples.sentence: If we knew exactly what he had taken, we could assess the risk more accurately.
examples.translation_ru: могли бы оценить.

grammar.title: Mixed Conditional vs Third Conditional
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Past Perfect, would / might + V1 (now) | If + Past Perfect, would / might / could + have + V3
grammar.signal_words: if … had …, now
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Bu ikki grammatikani adashtirmaslik juda muhim. Signal so'zlar: if … had …, now.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Mixed Conditional соединяет условие в прошлом с результатом в настоящем: «If he had taken a smaller amount, he might not be this drowsy now». Связывает прошлое решение с текущей клинической картиной. Third Conditional говорит о нереальной ситуации в прошлом и её прошлом результате — часто чтобы объяснить, чего можно было избежать: «If he had taken a smaller dose, he might not have become so drowsy». Сигнальные слова: if … had …, now.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: Mixed Conditional combines a past condition with a present result: "If he had taken a smaller amount, he might not be this drowsy now". It links a past decision to the current clinical picture. Third Conditional talks about an unreal past situation and its past result — often to explain what could have been avoided: "If he had taken a smaller dose, he might not have become so drowsy". Signal words: if … had …, now.

grammar.title: Third Conditional
grammar.structure_pattern: If + Past Perfect, would / might / could + have + V3
grammar.signal_words: if, had … would have
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: Third Conditional o'tmishdagi noreal vaziyat va uning o'tmishdagi natijasini bildiradi — ko'pincha nimadan qochish mumkin edi, deb tushuntirishda: "If he had taken a smaller dose, he might not have become so drowsy". Signal so'zlar: if, had … would have.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: Third Conditional говорит о нереальной ситуации в прошлом и её прошлом результате — часто чтобы объяснить, чего можно было избежать: «If he had taken a smaller dose, he might not have become so drowsy». Сигнальные слова: if, had … would have.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: had taken → might not have become Signal words: if, had … would have.

grammar.title: "if You Had Known..." — Past Consequence

grammar.title: "might Have + V3"
grammar.structure_pattern: may / might + V1 | may / might + have + V3 (past possibility)
grammar.signal_words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that
grammar.rule_explanation_uz: "May" va "might" ehtimollik va ehtiyotkor klinik xulosani bildiradi: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" muloyim ruxsat ham beradi. "Might have + V3" — o'tmishdagi ehtimol. Signal so'zlar: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_ru: might have taken → предположение о прошлом. Сигнальные слова: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.
grammar.rule_explanation_en: "May" and "might" express possibility and cautious clinical judgement: "It may be an infection", "You might need to stay in hospital". "May" also gives polite permission. "Might have + V3" refers to a possible past event. Signal words: possibly, perhaps, it is possible that.

medical_condition.chief_complaint: I'm not completely sure. I took some tablets at home because I had a bad headache. A few hours later, I became very sleepy and started feeling sick.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Hello. I understand you were brought in because you became unwell after taking some medication. Can you tell me what happened?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I'm not completely sure. I took some tablets at home because I had a bad headache. A few hours later, I became very sleepy and started feeling sick.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you know exactly what you took?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I think they were painkillers, but I'm not sure which ones. They were in a bottle without a proper label.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: How many tablets did you take?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I honestly don't know. I took two at first, and then I took some more because the headache wasn't getting better.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Approximately how many tablets could you have taken altogether?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Maybe six or seven. It could have been more. I really can't remember.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: When did you take the first tablets, and when did you take the last ones?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I took the first two at about 6 p.m. Then I took more about an hour later.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: I had two glasses of wine earlier in the evening. I didn't take any sleeping tablets or drugs.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Have you vomited?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, twice. I also feel very dizzy, and I'm having difficulty staying awake.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Do you have any chest pain or difficulty breathing?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: My breathing feels a little slow, but I don't have chest pain.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Has anyone found the medication bottle you took the tablets from?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: Yes, Doctor. I brought it with me. We found it beside his bed.

expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.doctor_question_topic: Thank you. We need to identify the medication and estimate how much was taken. Do you know whether he has taken any other medicines recently?
expected_doctor_questions_and_answers.patient_answer: He takes medication for high blood pressure, but I don't know whether he took it today.
